cycle1.result: 18 of 59 (30.5%) not managed per NICE; 22% given rigid casts (mean 3.8 weeks); 18.6% followed up in clinic; 63.6% of those followed up had repeat X-ray.

result.other_findings: Inappropriate cost of almost £2000 over 4 months. Recommendations presented at paediatric orthopaedic meeting; ED education, protocol update and re-audit planned.

result.topic: Perioperative antithrombotic management in skin surgery
result.setting: Minor operations theatre, Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust
result.standard: BSDS and BSH perioperative antithrombotic guidelines

cycle1.result: Postoperative bleeding 8.6%; aspirin monotherapy not stopped 80%; pre-op INR for warfarin 75%.

result.intervention: Poster 'cheat sheet' of antithrombotic advice displayed in the department.

cycle2.result: Postoperative bleeding 7.4%; aspirin monotherapy not stopped 71.4%; pre-op INR for warfarin 100%.

result.other_findings: 165 patients in total. DOACs were most often linked to bleeding (33.3% and 42.9%); high-risk operations bled more (26.7% vs 4.6%).

result.setting: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean SURG-TLX 39.65 with tourniquet (n=47) vs 41.59 without (n=53), p = 0.299; field visibility higher with tourniquet (mean difference 0.527, p = 0.001).

result.other_findings: No significant differences in individual SURG-TLX domains or between procedure types.

result.topic: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
result.setting: Busy district general hospital (Royal Free London NHS Trust)
result.standard: BOAST: intra-articular distal radius fractures operated within 72 hours; extra-articular fractures needing surgery within 7 days

cycle1.result: 65% of 49 intra-articular fractures fixed within 72 hours; 82% of 60 extra-articular fractures fixed within one week; mean injury to operation 3.88 and 2.98 days.

result.other_findings: Mean decision to operation 2.32 days (intra-articular) and 2.18 days (extra-articular); education on recognising intra-articular fractures proposed.

result.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Success defined as calcium returning to normal (<2.6 mmol/L) per NICE guidelines

cycle1.result: 222 (90.24%) successful; 24 (9.75%) persistent or recurrent hypercalcaemia; complications in 5 (2.03%).

result.other_findings: Success rate was 96.84% in 2019–2020. Complications were cord paresis (2), neck haematoma (2) and hungry bone syndrome (1).

result.topic: Day-case discharge after inguinal hernia repair
result.setting: Medway NHS Foundation Trust, elective day-case inguinal hernia repair
result.standard: BADS and GIRFT day-case guidance

cycle1.result: 44% failed same-day discharge; most common cause was failure to discharge by nursing staff (42%) despite medical fitness.

result.intervention: Standardised day-case discharge checklist; doctors, nurses and ward managers briefed on its use.
result.other_findings: In cycle 2, 32.7% of failed discharges stayed despite being medically fit; older age and Friday afternoon lists contributed.

result.setting: Basildon University Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists: ultrasound sensitivity >85% for acute appendicitis

cycle1.result: Ultrasound identified 52 of 77 histologically confirmed cases, sensitivity 67.5%, below the 85% benchmark.

result.other_findings: Ultrasound correctly diagnosed 17 of 25 without appendicitis. Sonographer training and second-opinion protocols recommended.

result.setting: East Surrey Hospital, Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines and GIRFT recommendations for acute ureteric stones

cycle1.result: Serum calcium checked 47%; dietary advice 17%; stents without clear indication or sepsis 83%; conservative management 65%; urgent treatment within 48 hours 35%.

result.intervention: Hot primary URS theatre opened and efforts to improve follow-up.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium 66%; dietary advice 72%; stents without clear indication 57%; conservative management 46%; urgent treatment within 48 hours 53%.

result.other_findings: Lost hot stone clinic follow-ups fell significantly. Staffing and lack of CEPOD support limited primary URS.

result.setting: Basildon & Thurrock University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Arterial thrombosis 38%, venous thrombosis 15%, NOMI 13%; CT-proven AMI 63%; 46 (41%) had surgery; mortality 16% within 24 hours and a further 39% within 90 days.

result.other_findings: 15 patients (13%) with CT not showing AMI were diagnosed intra-operatively.

result.setting: Single NHS trust, NELA patients aged 65 or over (Leeds Teaching Hospitals affiliation)
result.standard: NICE 2017: MUST on admission and nutritional support for high-risk (MUST 2 or above) patients

cycle1.result: 98% had a MUST score; of 114 high-risk patients, 35% had no dietetic review and 24% received no oral or parenteral supplementation.

result.other_findings: Nutritional screening is not currently included in NELA.

result.topic: Extubation after status epilepticus before critical care transfer
result.setting: 10 UK paediatric critical care transport teams
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Of 1,622 referrals, 1,136 (70%) intubated; 396 (34.8%) extubated locally, 19 (4.8%) reintubated; overall successful extubation 33% (377/1136).

result.other_findings: Local extubation rates varied from 2% to 74% between teams; regions with high rates had established extubation guidelines.

result.setting: Thoracic surgery, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust chest drain monitoring protocol (patency, swing, bubbling, volume/type, clamping, site, suction, bottle change)

cycle1.result: Bubbling 90%, fluid volume/type 84%, suction 87%; 0% for all other parameters.

result.intervention: Poster highlighting the protocol distributed across the department.

cycle2.result: Bubbling, fluid volume/type, suction and drain site 100%; tube patency 14%, swinging 36%, clamping 21%, bottle change 21%.

result.other_findings: Tube patency, swinging, clamping and bottle change remained poorly documented.

result.setting: Wexham Park Hospital, Frimley NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital
result.standard: NELA: formal frailty assessment for patients over 65 (NoLap patients)

cycle1.result: No patient had a clinical frailty score; social history recorded in 34 (72%); no cognitive documentation in 33 (70%); baseline mobility not recorded in 21 (45%).

result.other_findings: Exercise tolerance not recorded in 39 (83%), package of care in 15 (32%) and place of residence in 12 (26%).

result.topic: Time to analgesia in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency Department, St Vincent's University Hospital; patients aged 75 or over with head injury
result.standard: RCEM: analgesia within 15 minutes of presentation

cycle1.result: Average time from registration to analgesia just under 3 hours.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in time to analgesia reported (no figures); final results awaited.

result.other_findings: A significant proportion of older patients did not receive analgesia.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis prescribing
result.setting: General Surgery directorate inpatients, Darlington Memorial Hospital
result.standard: NICE VTE guidelines

cycle1.result: Risk assessment completed 90.7% (16.3% delayed); prophylaxis prescribed 88.4%.

cycle2.result: Risk assessment completed 96.4% (35.7% delayed); prophylaxis prescribed 96.4%.

result.other_findings: Proportion of delayed assessments rose; teaching at induction and a qualitative audit of delays suggested.

result.setting: Kettering General Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Updated RCS England COVID-19 guidance: conservative treatment of acute appendicitis unless unresponsive or complicated

cycle1.result: Conservative treatment in 16/63 (25.4%), successful in 10/16 (63%); operative management first in 47/63 (74.6%).

result.other_findings: Readmissions 3/16 (18.75%) after conservative vs 1/47 (2.12%) after operative management; no complications after failed conservative treatment. Re-audit planned.

result.topic: Decompressive craniectomy time to surgery in MCA stroke
result.setting: Neurosurgery Department, Hospital Sultanah Aminah Johor Bahru (HSAJB)
result.standard: NICE: decompressive craniectomy within 48 hours for ischaemic MCA stroke

cycle1.result: Only 16 of 38 had clear documentation of time to surgery; 75% (n=12) had DC within 48 hours, of whom 25% (n=3) achieved mRS 0–3.

result.other_findings: No patient operated after 48 hours achieved mRS 0–3. Time to surgery was poorly documented (22 of 38 lacked clear documentation).

result.setting: Royal Orthopaedic Hospital, Birmingham
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 16 of 26 had spinal without GA and 10 spinal plus GA; median postoperative oral morphine equivalent 30mg/day (range 0–60mg).

result.other_findings: Peripheral nerve blocks showed a trend towards less opioid use and shorter stay; mean anaesthetic time 19 minutes and recovery 51 minutes.

result.setting: Surgical patients, Raigmore Hospital, Inverness
result.standard: WHO analgesic ladder, with reasons documented when not followed

cycle1.result: 83.3% prescribed analgesia following the ladder; of the rest, only 50% had reasons documented.

result.intervention: Presentation at audit meeting, educational sessions, information leaflets and email reminders.
result.other_findings: 103 patients across both cycles. Authors judged the deviations from the ladder clinically justified.

result.setting: Ward staff, Great Ormond Street Hospital
result.standard: Tongue Reduction Integrated Care Pathway for Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome

cycle1.result: 44% (11/25) unaware of the pathway; 56% (14/25) did not know the associated condition; correct fluid rationale 24%.

result.intervention: Two teaching sessions and posters in key wards and staff areas.

cycle2.result: 77.8% (14/18) aware of the pathway; 88.9% (16/18) knew the syndrome; 100% aware of the analgesia protocol; correct fluid rationale 56%.

result.other_findings: Audit was by anonymous staff survey. Knowledge of the fluid regime rationale remained poor.

result.topic: Acute pancreatitis diagnosis and severity scoring
result.setting: University Hospital Lewisham, general surgery department
result.standard: National guidelines and the Atlanta criteria for diagnosis and severity stratification of acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Severity scoring completed in 33% and used incorrectly in the majority; almost half of CT scans were deemed unnecessary.

result.intervention: Acute pancreatitis protocol created with Upper GI surgeons (re-audit not yet reported).
result.other_findings: Significant shortfalls in interventions for alcohol and gallstone cases.

result.setting: Resident doctors in a single district general hospital
result.standard: Aim to improve resident doctors' confidence by 25%

cycle1.result: Baseline Likert confidence survey completed by 25 resident doctors (scores not given).

result.intervention: Teaching session in the foundation programme teaching series.

cycle2.result: Confidence in non-pharmacological approaches up 21%, prescribing up 32%, managing a delirious patient up 26%; overall up 26%.

result.other_findings: A poster has been developed and confidence will be re-audited.

result.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after major abdominal surgery
result.setting: District general hospital, Southport and Ormskirk NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE: extended VTE prophylaxis (LMWH for 28 days) after major abdominal surgery

cycle1.result: 189 (61%) discharged with extended VTE prophylaxis; 121 (39%) did not receive it.

result.other_findings: Of the 121 without extended prophylaxis, 2 developed VTE (one DVT and PE, one DVT).

result.topic: Perioperative PPI use in cardiac surgery
result.setting: Cardiac surgery, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough
result.standard: PPI the day before and day of surgery, continued until eating and drinking (until discharge if on DAPT); discharge letter to state indication and duration

cycle1.result: Preoperative PPI 96%; discontinued once eating 25%; continuation documented 38%; discharge letter indication and duration 87%.

cycle2.result: Preoperative PPI 86%; discontinued once eating 19%; continuation documented 38%; discharge letter indication and duration 62%.

result.other_findings: Middle cycle (December 2021, n=51): preoperative PPI 100%, discontinued 6%, documented 12%, discharge letter 68%. 100% on DAPT continued PPI; non-adherence persisted and tick-box checklists were suggested.

result.setting: Russells Hall Hospital, The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE: acute appendicitis should be diagnosed clinically

cycle1.result: Imaging in 50.9%; CT 91.5% accurate, bloods 65.5%; ultrasound detected 57.1% of histologically proven appendicitis and reported 52% as normal.

result.other_findings: Authors advise against ultrasound for diagnosing appendicitis.

result.setting: HPB surgery, Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, tertiary centre
result.standard: Key components of ward round documentation (date, time, diagnosis, procedure, consultant, author, information given, observations, investigations, plan)

cycle1.result: Time, history, NEWS and plan recorded in more than 50%; diagnosis, consultant, author, information to patient, wound and medication review, fluid balance, investigations and discharge plans in less than 50%.

cycle2.result: Date and time 94%; consultant and author initials 84%; examination, information to patient, wound and medication review more than 80%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, Northampton General Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: GIRFT day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy rate (national median 60%)

cycle1.result: Day-case rate 64% (55/86).

result.intervention: Day surgery unit recovery hours extended to 9 PM; local anaesthetic protocol changed to include liver bed infiltration.
result.other_findings: Main causes of unplanned admission were DSU closing at 6 PM, intraoperative concerns and pain; unplanned admissions cost about £12,000.

result.topic: CT pathway for emergency laparotomy patients
result.setting: Three hospitals (Tameside, Stepping Hill, Pilgrim), NELA laparotomy patients
result.standard: Hospital abdominal pain CT pathway criteria and RCEM CT criteria at triage

cycle1.result: 67/70 (96%) met hospital abdominal pain CT pathway criteria at triage; 10/70 (14%) met RCEM criteria; mean time to CT from ED arrival 11 hr 36 min.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: James Paget University Hospital, Great Yarmouth; emergency laparotomy patients over 65
result.standard: British Geriatrics Society recommendations and local guidance: RCFS, CGA, AMTS, memory screen, residence and care level

cycle1.result: RCFS 28%; CGA 15%; place of residence 67%; level of care 41%; memory screen 13%; AMTS 7%.

result.intervention: Presentation to surgical juniors on frailty, frailty assessments and guidelines.

cycle2.result: RCFS, CGA, place of residence and care level completion increased; memory screening and AMTS decreased; average criteria completed per patient up 39%.

result.other_findings: Frailty teaching added for Foundation trainees and clerking booklet reviewed; further re-audit planned.

result.setting: Main centre of the South West Wales Vascular Network (Morriston Hospital, Swansea)
result.standard: CEPOD booking category target timescales

cycle1.result: 133 emergency vascular procedures; amputations 47%.

result.intervention: Reorganisation of CEPOD during the first COVID-19 wave (not a planned audit intervention).

cycle2.result: 98 procedures; amputations 53%; median waits for category 1 and 2a significantly shorter, category 3 longer; no significant difference in proportion operated within target.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Postoperative opioid prescribing after hip replacement
result.setting: University College London Hospital, elective primary THR patients aged 60+
result.standard: NICE NG180 postoperative analgesia recommendations

cycle1.result: Baseline rates of regular oral opioid prescribing on D0 and time to first oral opioid (figures not given).

result.intervention: Printed NICE NG180 posters and face-to-face education on postoperative analgesia.

cycle2.result: 30% increase in purely regular oral opioid prescriptions on D0; 10% increase in first oral opioid within 2 hours for those on regular opioids.

result.other_findings: 2–8 hour and >8 hour timings stayed similar; an electronic prescription order set is proposed.

result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: TIA guidelines (brain imaging, neurovascular imaging and cardiac evaluation)

cycle1.result: All had CT brain on admission (2/28 waited more than 12 hours); 25/28 (89%) carotid Doppler, mean wait 33 hours (6–72); 14/24 (58%) inpatient cardiac monitoring.

result.other_findings: Average AMU stay 3 days, up to 5 days in three patients; protected AMU imaging slots recommended.

result.setting: Care of the Elderly wards, Nottingham University Hospitals Trust
result.standard: 7 audit standards matching key sections of the DNACPR form

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: DNACPR champions with monthly audit and personal feedback, mandatory e-learning, NerveCentre alert system, and new patient information (webpage, videos, leaflets) via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Sustained improvement in most of the 7 standards, largest for review date, mental capacity assessment and use of patient leaflets (figures not given).

result.other_findings: Documentation of discussions with patients and relatives stayed below standard and largely unchanged.

result.setting: Medical school Trauma & Orthopaedics society, University of Birmingham
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean improvement in understanding of audit 1.18 ± 1.07, confidence to approach a supervisor 1.29 ± 1.21 and ability to conduct an audit 1.77 ± 1.15 (all p < 0.001).

result.other_findings: Interest in a T&O career rose from 35.3% to 70.6%; all 5 responding supervisors were happy with the work.

result.topic: Secondary cardiovascular prevention after major amputation
result.setting: Department of Vascular Surgery, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: Antiplatelet (or anticoagulant) and statin prescribed at discharge

cycle1.result: 80% prescribed an antiplatelet or anticoagulant and 82% a statin at discharge.

result.other_findings: 282 major amputations; 68% had peripheral arterial disease and 52% diabetes.

result.setting: Emergency general surgical admissions over 65, Manchester Royal Infirmary, tertiary centre
result.standard: NELA: clinical frailty score documented at first encounter for patients over 65

cycle1.result: CFS recorded 0/47; OPAL review 13% (6/47).

result.intervention: Standardised rapid-use EPR documentation templates and staff education.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth, rural general hospital
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 LGIB guidelines (Oakland score for safe discharge)

cycle1.result: 13 minor and 60 major by Oakland score; 4 discharged same day; median stay 3 days; 72% managed conservatively; 18 transfused, 3 had surgery.

result.other_findings: Commonest causes were diverticular disease (45%) and haemorrhoids (17%). Oakland score judged insufficiently accurate for safe discharge.

result.setting: Vascular service, University Hospitals North Midlands, Stoke-on-Trent
result.standard: Trust guideline: discharge letters available to GPs within 24 hours

cycle1.result: 52 delayed discharge letters; average delay 14.6 days.

result.intervention: Interventions presented to the clinical team (not specified).
result.other_findings: Central Treatment Suite day cases had no delays in 2024; 44% of delays were interventional radiology angioplasty cases. Responsibility for IR letters has since been assigned.

result.setting: Tertiary cancer unit (University College Hospital, London)
result.standard: HERO consensus and Royal College of Pathologists minimum dataset for gastro-oesophageal cancer resection specimens

cycle1.result: Lymphovascular invasion 92.3%; ≥15 nodes 88.5%; CRM in mm 77.8%; LRM in mm 80.8%; peri-oesophageal fat blocking 88.9%; R1 reporting, lesser curve fat blocking and node response 100%.

cycle2.result: Lymphovascular invasion 100%; ≥15 nodes 91.3%; CRM in mm 100%; LRM in mm 82.6%; peri-oesophageal fat blocking 77.8%; other items 100%.

result.other_findings: Both low-yield specimens in cycle 2 were re-examined, versus one of three in cycle 1. Peri-oesophageal fat blocking did not improve.

result.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, University College Hospital, London
result.standard: GMC and RCS consent guidance for carpal tunnel decompression and trigger finger release

cycle1.result: Risks explained 88%; alternatives discussed and documented 61%; 'new' risks on consent form not in clinic letter 66%.

result.intervention: Re-education of surgeons on the consent process.

cycle2.result: Risks explained 100%; alternatives 100%; 'new' risks on consent form not in clinic letter 79%.

result.other_findings: Identical risks in consent form and clinic notes in only 3.5% (cycle 1) and 2% (cycle 2); standardised risk lists recommended.

result.setting: Three surgical wards, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust, Hastings
result.standard: NICE guidelines on maintenance IV fluids (25-30 ml/kg/day water; approximately 1 mmol/kg/day potassium, sodium and chloride; approximately 50-100 g/day glucose)

cycle1.result: No patients were given IV fluids according to NICE guidelines.

result.intervention: Proforma and teaching to foundation doctors on the ward.

cycle2.result: Second cycle in progress; early signs show a positive improvement (no figures reported).

result.other_findings: Data collected daily from patient records, drug charts and nurses in charge for nil by mouth patients.

result.setting: Tertiary centre, Leeds Institute of Emergency Surgery
result.standard: WSES guidelines endorsing structured diagnostic pathways; RIFT study reported UK negative appendicectomy rate of 20% (no target stated)

cycle1.result: 20% negative appendicectomy rate; negative cases mean age 28 years, 67% female.

result.intervention: Establishment of a dedicated consultant-led Emergency General Surgery service in 2020.

cycle2.result: Negative appendicectomy rate reduced to 13%; negative cases mean age 29 years, 62% female.

result.other_findings: Negative cases in both years were more likely to be younger females than positive and total groups.

result.topic: Bone protection plan in discharge letters after hip fracture
result.setting: Orthogeriatric service, Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda (Model 3 hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Only 60% (n=27) of discharge letters completed; of those, 51.8% (n=14) included orthogeriatric involvement and an ongoing bone protection plan; 71% (n=32) had no handover of bone protection plan to GP.

result.intervention: Orthogeriatrics discharge proforma and NCHD education (ongoing, not yet re-audited).
result.other_findings: 55% (n=25) were planned for IV zoledronic acid 10 weeks after discharge and 24% (n=11) denosumab; 6% (n=3) died as inpatients.

result.topic: Patient information leaflet provision before surgery
result.setting: NHS hospital, Manchester Royal Infirmary, North-West England
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons advice to provide patient information leaflets; BAUS TURBT leaflet

cycle1.result: 30% (6 of 20) provided with the TURBT PIL.

result.intervention: Email to all consultants and registrars encouraging use of PILs (departmental reminder).
result.other_findings: Authors recommend standardising PIL provision and regular re-audit to reach full compliance.

result.setting: HPB surgery, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice (2025) operative note documentation standards

cycle1.result: Incision 93%, findings 100%, closure 100%, postoperative instructions 100%, surgeon signature 100%; EBL 20%, specimen details 71%, extra procedures 13%.

result.intervention: Planned: standardised electronic operative note template, educational sessions and visual reminders in theatres (not yet implemented).
result.other_findings: ICG use documented in 2 of 9 laparoscopic liver resections (22%); IOUS and frozen section documented in 25% and 30% of relevant cases; Pringle's manoeuvre recorded in all applicable cases.

result.setting: Surgical department at a tertiary centre
result.standard: Local group and save sample protocols

cycle1.result: 203 G&S samples collected, 52 (26%) not indicated: 25/82 (30%) emergency, 27/121 (22%) elective; avoidable cost £1508 per month.

result.intervention: Posters and email communication targeted to pre-operative clinics.

cycle2.result: 73 of 260 samples not indicated: 44/114 (28%) emergency, 29/146 (20%) elective; avoidable cost £2177 per month.

result.other_findings: Small decrease in unnecessary elective samples but emergency procedures remained a problem; annual avoidable cost £18,096 in cycle 1 and £25,404 in cycle 2.

result.topic: Time to cholecystectomy after gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: UGI tertiary referral cancer centre, Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Trust
result.standard: Key performance indicators: time to Lap-C, rate of Lap-C within 2 weeks after pancreatitis, inpatient Lap-C rate, outpatient appointments saved

cycle1.result: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 27%; average time to Lap-C 68 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 2%.

result.intervention: Dedicated consultant-led biliary service, live biliary admission tracking system, increased inpatient Lap-C, ambulatory pathways and integrated care approach.

cycle2.result: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 69% (41% as inpatients); average time to Lap-C 13 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 19% for fit and consenting patients.

result.other_findings: 103 outpatient appointments saved (£12360) by counselling and pre-assessing as inpatients; project followed 3 earlier audit cycles.

result.setting: Kings College Hospital, London
result.standard: NICE guidance clinical audit tool for endovascular repair of popliteal aneurysms

cycle1.result: All 11 patients had vascular MDT discussion before the procedure; all had appropriate antiplatelet therapy; 6 stents failed, 3 within one year, 1 amputation.

result.other_findings: Stents failing within 1 year had reduced run-off (mean 2 vessels); smallest stent (6mm) failed within 7 months.

result.setting: Royal Sussex County Hospital, tertiary centre
result.standard: National and WSES recommendations for laparoscopic appendicectomy

cycle1.result: Time to diagnosis 16.8 hours; diagnosis to surgery 28.1 hours; CT 80%; scoring system use 0%; negative appendicectomy 8.9%; drains 44%; postoperative antibiotics 92.1%; complications 17.8%.

cycle2.result: Time to diagnosis 8.27 hours; diagnosis to surgery 20.54 hours; CT 77.8%; scoring system use 3.3%; negative appendicectomy 7.7%; drains 31%; postoperative antibiotics 75.6%; complications 3.3%.

result.other_findings: Scoring system use remained low; cycle 2 complications were exclusively postoperative ileus.

result.topic: Patient understanding of diagnosis and plan at discharge
result.setting: Emergency general surgery ward, district general hospital (Royal Free Hospital and UCL Hospital, London)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 40-65% of patients gave correct answers (50% correct diagnosis/investigations, 40% correct follow-up plan).

result.intervention: Patient prompt sheet suggesting questions to ask, given 1-2 days before discharge.

cycle2.result: 75-100% answered correctly (88% correct diagnosis, 100% correct follow-up plan).

result.other_findings: Total cohort across both audits was 28 patients.

result.setting: Tertiary neurosurgical centre, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National guidelines including NICE: formal audiology during workup of vestibular schwannoma

cycle1.result: 186 (96.4%) had at least one pure tone assessment; 135 (70%) also had speech discrimination; surgical 38/38, surveillance 116/121 (96%), radiotherapy 32/34 (94%).

result.other_findings: Reasons for no audiology: profound hearing loss (2/7), audiometry at local centres (4/7), patient compliance (1/7); speech discrimination rate could be improved.

result.setting: University Hospitals North Midlands NHS Trust, Stoke-on-Trent
result.standard: BOAST Open Fracture Guidelines (2017): soft tissue coverage within 72 hours and 7 days; combined orthoplastic consultant debridement

cycle1.result: 28% missed the 72-hour soft tissue coverage target, 11% missed the 7-day target; 10% had both orthopaedic and plastics consultants at initial debridement.

result.intervention: Business case leading to a second scheduled weekly orthoplastics list.

cycle2.result: Missed 7-day soft tissue coverage target halved to 5%; both consultants at initial debridement 26%.

result.other_findings: Open tibial fractures only; cycle 1 retrospective, cycle 2 prospective.

result.setting: Hand trauma clinic and acute take, St George's Hospital, London
result.standard: BSSH standards of care in hand trauma (15 data points)

cycle1.result: Free-text clerking quality varied between clinician groups (surgical trainees outperformed advanced nurse practitioners in 5/15 data points); some data points universally poorly documented.

result.intervention: Electronic hand trauma clerking proforma introduced in the acute take.

cycle2.result: Proforma uptake 95% in acute take and 100% in hand trauma clinic; statistically significant improvement in 11/15 data points.

result.other_findings: Proforma has become a Trust-wide ClinDoc.

result.setting: Medway NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital, Gillingham
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines on lower GI bleeding

cycle1.result: DRE compliance 79%; TXA use 44%; CT-A 29%.

result.intervention: Educational posters and email summarising BSG guidelines and audit recommendations.

cycle2.result: DRE compliance 91%; TXA use 38%; CT-A 19%; Oakland score documentation unchanged.

result.other_findings: Oakland score documentation did not improve.

result.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: BOAST Fracture Clinic Services: timely imaging to avoid delays to surgery

cycle1.result: Mean time from imaging request to performance 4.51 days (range 0-30); imaging delays 29.5% of time from VFC review to surgery (9 surgical patients).

result.intervention: Interdepartmental T&O-radiology imaging pathway with priority slots for VFC patients.

cycle2.result: Mean time from request to performance 3.56 days (range 0-24); imaging delays 21.0% of time from VFC review to surgery (10 surgical patients).

result.other_findings: Imaging delay reduced by 21.1%; sample size is imaging requests.

result.setting: Furness General Hospital, district general hospital, Barrow-in-Furness
result.standard: NELA Best Practice Tariff: 80% of NELA high-risk patients have consultant surgeon and consultant anaesthetist present during surgery and are admitted directly to critical care

cycle1.result: 57% of high-risk cases met BPT criteria; consultant surgeon present 100%; consultant anaesthetist 63% (37% SAS-grade anaesthetist); 87% admitted to critical care.

result.other_findings: Of 43% not meeting BPT, 29 had no consultant anaesthetist, 6 not admitted to critical care and 8 both; survival 81% with SAS-grade anaesthetist versus 82% with consultant anaesthetist.

result.setting: One large NHS trust in England (Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Observations of four patient journeys, interviews with 21 staff and clinical data each identified specific local practices to address in a patient warming care bundle (no figures reported).

result.other_findings: Methodological study showing that a comprehensive audit identified local contextual issues not found through other recommended methods before care bundle design.

result.setting: Single tertiary centre (NHS Grampian, Aberdeen)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Limb salvage 53% (n=69); subsequent amputation 15% (n=19); debridement at 6 months 18% (n=23); 6-month mortality 25% (n=32).

result.other_findings: Of patients having below-knee amputation, 50% (n=9) had it within 60 days of angioplasty.

result.topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis
result.setting: Salisbury District Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: NICE: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis of acute cholecystitis

cycle1.result: 285 (87%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days; of 43 who did not, 31 had clinically justified delay; 285/297 (96%) met the NICE standard.

cycle2.result: Re-audit showed significant improvement (no figures reported).

result.other_findings: Poor documentation was the most common cause of failure; other reasons were awaiting ERCP/MRCP, unfit for surgery and patient choice.

result.setting: University Hospital Bristol
result.standard: UK guidance: follow-up outpatient LGI endoscopy 6-8 weeks after discharge for uncomplicated diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 42% (179/426) had LGI endoscopy; 23% (99/426) within the 8-week target; median time to outpatient endoscopy 70 days (6-287).

result.other_findings: Polyps in 21% (37/179), tubular adenoma 5% (9/179), one high grade dysplasia, no malignancy; authors question necessity of routine endoscopy.

result.setting: Queen Elizabeth Queen Mother Hospital, Margate
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidance: discuss risk of hospital-acquired COVID-19 during consent

cycle1.result: 17/29 (59%) documented discussion of COVID-19 risk.

result.intervention: Education of the surgical team at a local meeting.
result.other_findings: One patient (3%) in cycle 2 contracted hospital-acquired COVID-19; none in cycle 1.

result.setting: Wellington Hospital, teaching and tertiary referral hospital
result.standard: Adequate oxygen prescription (device, flow rate or inspired oxygen concentration, and target saturation), administration and monitoring

cycle1.result: Oxygen prescribed in 15/85 (17.6%); adequate prescription 5/85 (5.9%).

result.intervention: New drug chart with a specific oxygen prescription section and targeted educational lectures mainly to medical staff.

cycle2.result: Oxygen prescribed in 39/98 (39.8%), RR 2.3 (95% CI 1.3 to 3.9); adequate prescription 36/98 (36.7%), RR 6.2 (95% CI 2.5 to 15.0).

result.other_findings: No change in assessment of room-air saturations with oxygen started at 92% or below, or in titration of oxygen to saturations.

result.setting: Emergency surgical team, Salford Royal Hospital (Northwest NHS hospital)
result.standard: Local hospital policy on CT imaging in acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 28% of CT scans for acute pancreatitis were unnecessary.

result.intervention: Targeted education and retraining of staff on the local imaging policy.

cycle2.result: CT in 23 patients (71.8%); only 1 scan (4.3%) unnecessary, 95.6% compliance with imaging policy.

result.other_findings: 15 (46.1%) CTs done in patients without diagnostic amylase levels, 3 after 72 hours for complications.

result.setting: Dorset County Hospital, district general hospital without electronic stent-tracking
result.standard: Stent removal within 6 weeks or by target date

cycle1.result: Removal plan documented in 95.7% (93.5% of discharge summaries); timely removal 59.1%; delayed 35.5% (33/93), 4.3% in situ over six months; possible retained 3.2%; unknown 2.1%.

result.other_findings: No reason recorded in 88% of delayed cases; Cook UFI-600-R stents accounted for 73% of delays and 93% of encrustations; complication rate 22.6%.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Swansea Bay University Health Board
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Co-ordinated programme of trainee QIPs from a fishbone analysis (NELA data capture, risk scoring, sepsis, pre-operative antibiotics, infection prevention, early imaging).

cycle2.result: Non-significant downward trend in length of stay and mortality (no figures reported).

result.other_findings: 9 QIPs started, first cycle complete in all and 3 completed; 5 presented locally and 2 nationally.

result.setting: Four CMHT clozapine clinics, north Wales (BCUHB)
result.standard: BCUHB guidelines for physical health monitoring in clozapine clinics; NICE annual monitoring of weight, blood pressure, waist, glucose and lipids

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Audit followed a Coroner's investigation; criteria included annual review, plasma level, MSE and risk assessment, lifestyle advice, care coordinator and side-effect monitoring.

result.topic: Copy of consent form offered to patient
result.setting: Major Trauma Centre and District General Hospital, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons: provide patients with a copy of their consent form

cycle1.result: All forms adequately completed; none (0%) offered a copy; 1 (2.5%) received one.

cycle2.result: 76 (74%) offered a copy and 68 (67%) received one (p<0.05).

result.other_findings: 141 consent forms reviewed over three months; post-operative feedback collected qualitatively.

result.setting: Sunderland and South Tyneside NHS Trust
result.standard: Quality indicator: complete photo-documentation of eight standard OGD landmarks

cycle1.result: Complete eight-site documentation in 6.35%; upper oesophagus 15.9%, GOJ 73.0%, fundus 76.2%, body 34.9%, incisura 27.0%, antrum 49.2%, duodenal bulb 41.3%, D2 79.4%.

result.intervention: Planned: structured reporting templates, operator education and feedback (not yet implemented).
result.other_findings: Mean sites documented: gastroenterologists 4.15, surgeons 3.94, gastroenterology trainees 4.73.

result.setting: Geriatric assessment and treatment clinic, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: 2021 UK National Osteoporosis Guideline Group strong recommendations

cycle1.result: Only 25% investigated, treated and prescribed bone health medication as per NOGG 2021.

result.other_findings: Comorbidity, mobility and frailty history well completed and follow-up well documented, but referrals to allied health practitioners lacking.

result.setting: Major Trauma Centre, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: Departmental guidance: COVID-19 specified as a risk on consent forms

cycle1.result: 49% of consent forms specified COVID-19 as a risk.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental governance meeting and infographic sent to all clinicians.
result.other_findings: Indicative perioperative COVID-19 risk fell from 2.15% (2 positive tests) to less than 1% (none).

result.setting: Surgical department, Southend University Hospital
result.standard: Association of Stoma Care Nurses (ASCN) guidelines on high output stoma management

cycle1.result: Junior doctors answered 51% of knowledge questions correctly.

result.intervention: Poster and checklist summarising ASCN guidelines, then teaching sessions for surgical junior doctors and an improved checklist.

cycle2.result: 91% of answers correct; 85% of junior doctors reported applying knowledge from the teaching session.

result.other_findings: Three cycles: intermediate result 72% correct in September 2022 after poster and checklist; measured by survey of junior doctors' knowledge.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.setting: Barnsley District General Hospital
result.standard: Local departmental antimicrobial guidelines for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Adherence to guidelines 36%; correct antibiotics in penicillin-allergic patients 75%; co-amoxiclav overuse 60%.

cycle2.result: Adherence to guidelines 3%; correct antibiotics in penicillin-allergic patients 100%; co-amoxiclav overuse 87%.

result.other_findings: Antibiotic use estimated at 39% to 63% because of poor documentation in operation notes; proposed microbiology teaching and laminated guidelines in theatre.

result.topic: Ureteric stent dwell time and encrustation
result.setting: Emergency theatre database, The Royal London Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Average time from emergency stenting to definitive procedure 140 days; 16% readmitted with stent symptoms, 3% urosepsis, 0.9% blocked stents; encrustation 11.5%.

result.other_findings: 16.7% of encrusted stents needed complex ureteroscopy and laser fragmentation.

result.topic: Pregnancy testing in acute abdominal pain
result.setting: CHED and CAU, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital
result.standard: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital guidance: 100% of girls over 12 years with acute abdominal pain have a pregnancy test on admission

cycle1.result: Only 13.3% had a documented pregnancy test; 86.7% had no evidence of testing.

result.other_findings: Among documented tests, 20% negative, 1% positive and 30% performed without a recorded result; results often recorded only in nursing notes.

result.topic: Substance misuse assessment in liaison psychiatry
result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, general hospital (Livewell Southwest; Derriford Hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Nearly half of patients assessed were not asked about alcohol or drug use.

cycle2.result: 78% asked about alcohol use and 77% about drug use; 73% of those with an identified misuse problem (n = 15) offered advice or intervention.

result.other_findings: Documentation of advice or intervention offered rose by 21% since the August 2020 audit; 27% with identified misuse had no intervention documented.

result.setting: Single-centre Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service
result.standard: NICE NG134 and CG31: prescribing with psychological therapy, risk-benefit discussion, written information, first-line medication, off-licence only after review, signed consent for off-licence use

cycle1.result: Good compliance with prescribing alongside psychological therapy, risk-benefit discussion, first-line medication and off-licence review; moderate compliance for written information; no compliance for signed consent form.

result.intervention: Planned: presentation to the local team; re-audit standards to use case-note documentation of consent (not yet re-audited).
result.other_findings: 30 of 86 eligible patients randomly selected; re-audit planned in 6 months.

result.setting: Regional Mersey Burn Unit, Whiston Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: History 94%, comorbidities 94%, drug history 95%, TBSA 83%, treatment plan 91%, admission documentation 24%, consultant confirmation of TBSA 5%.

result.intervention: New version 4.0 of the Mersey Burns Admission Proforma with a flowchart layout.

cycle2.result: 58 of 61 comparable fields (95%) improved; history, comorbidities and drug history 100%; TBSA 93%; treatment plan 95%; admission documentation 51%; consultant confirmation of TBSA 10%.

result.other_findings: 3 fields (5%) deteriorated and Lund & Browder chart use was unchanged; consultant TBSA confirmation still needs improvement.

result.setting: Single centre, two thyroid surgeons (NHS Lothian, Edinburgh)
result.standard: Data in UK Registry of Endocrine and Thyroid Surgery compared with electronic patient records

cycle1.result: 94.0% (3835/4080) of data points accurate; pre-operative 91.9% (937/1020), peri-operative 97.7% (997/1020), post-operative 93.8% (957/1020), follow-up 92.5% (944/1020).

result.other_findings: Date of operation most accurate (99.0%, 202/204) and date of discharge least accurate (89.0%, 182/204).

result.setting: East Lancashire Hospitals Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 25 cemented and 23 uncemented primary prostheses; conservative management most common (39.6%); C Stem most common implant (12 patients).

result.other_findings: Vancouver B fractures: 20 in uncemented versus 12 in cemented prostheses.

result.topic: Critical care admission after high-risk emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Busy district general hospital surgical department (Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: NELA Standards (2019 and 2023): high-risk patients directly admitted to critical care

cycle1.result: 136 (84%) high-risk patients directly admitted to critical care; median LOS 22 days; 30-day O/E mortality ratio 0.98 (26 deaths).

result.other_findings: Of 25 ward-admitted high-risk patients, one escalated to ICU and one died; median ward LOS 10 days.

result.setting: Three general surgery wards, South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidance on safe handover

cycle1.result: Patient inclusion on handover list 42%; entries updated before handover 27%; documentation completeness 23%.

result.intervention: Results disseminated departmentally, then a structured handover tutorial embedded in resident doctor induction.
result.other_findings: Three cycles across 304 patients; omissions in patient status and outstanding investigations persisted and completeness plateaued at 50%.

result.topic: Dual antiplatelet therapy after minor stroke
result.setting: University Hospital Galway
result.standard: American Heart Association class 1A recommendation for DAPT in minor ischaemic stroke (NIHSS 3 or less); rationale documented if not prescribed

cycle1.result: 8 commenced on DAPT; 48.3% (n = 14) either prescribed DAPT or had a documented rationale for SAPT.

result.other_findings: Documented reasons for SAPT included presentation after 72 hours and atrial fibrillation.

result.setting: Three DME wards, Southend Hospital
result.standard: Antibiotic prescribing guidelines: indication, duration, end-date documentation and PPI co-prescription

cycle1.result: Guideline adherence 65%; end-date documentation 75%; unjustified PPI co-prescription 50%.

result.intervention: Poster on prescriber responsibilities, then an educational talk.

cycle2.result: Guideline adherence 72%; end-date documentation 85%; unjustified PPI co-prescription 33%.

result.other_findings: After the poster alone (intermediate cycle): adherence 68%, end-date documentation 84%, unjustified PPI co-prescription 43%.

result.setting: One general practice surgery (population 14,315)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons recommendations for phimosis management and paediatric surgical referral

cycle1.result: 25 (71.4%) referred; 32% of referrals (n = 8) without a topical steroid trial; 53.5% of steroids (n = 15) weaker than RCS recommends; 14 (73.7%) reviewed had physiological phimosis.

result.other_findings: Referral waiting times 3–232 days (mean 111.4).

result.setting: Emergency Department, George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust, district general hospital
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines on lower GI bleeding (Oakland score, shock index)

cycle1.result: Of 45 major bleeds, 4 unstable (1 CT angiogram); 32 admitted (71.1%), 13 discharged (28.9%), 5 without endoscopy; 3 (23.1%) readmitted within 28 days.

result.intervention: Efforts to integrate the BSG guidelines (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Of 27 major bleeds, 2 unstable (1 CT angiogram); 15 admitted (55.6%), 12 discharged (44.4%), all with endoscopy; 1 (8.3%) readmitted within 28 days.

result.other_findings: Minimal improvement in Oakland score compliance; all minor bleeds (Oakland 8 or less) discharged without readmission.

result.setting: On-call surgical team, Royal Free Hospital, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Presenting complaint 66%, past history 72%, medical history 44%, NEWS 66%, clinical findings 88%, key lab results 27%, key imaging 33%, management plan 94%.

result.intervention: Standardised post-take ward round template circulated by email, posters in the surgery office and a teaching presentation for junior doctors.

cycle2.result: Presenting history 100%, medical history 85%, vital signs 79%, key lab results 55%, key imaging 78%, management plan 100%.

result.other_findings: Authors advise reiterating the template at junior doctor changeover.

result.setting: Diana Princess of Wales Hospital, district general hospital, Grimsby
result.standard: NICE NG104 (cause, antibiotic stewardship, nutrition, severity and complications, lifestyle advice)

cycle1.result: Cause identified 55% (86% within 48 hours); antibiotics 51%, indication recorded in 23%; nil by mouth 91%, reason recorded in 20%; severity documented 6%; lifestyle advice 33%.

result.intervention: Ongoing: Pancreatitis Management Bundle, local clinical guidelines, staff awareness and patient education (no re-audit reported).
result.other_findings: Oral nutrition offered in 9% versus 56.4% in the national PANC study; four patients discussed with a tertiary centre.

result.setting: Surgical wards, James Paget University Hospital, Great Yarmouth
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians 'Ward Rounds in Medicine'

cycle1.result: First checklist used in a mean of 13% (SD 22%); documentation with checklist mean 67% (SD 22%) versus 26% (SD 10%) without, t(64)=8.85, p<.00001.

result.intervention: Revised second version of the ward round checklist based on feedback.

cycle2.result: Second checklist used in a mean of 56% (SD 28%), t(75)=7.59, p<.00001.

result.other_findings: Documentation especially improved for fluid balance, analgesia and physiotherapy needs.

result.topic: ANP-led direct streaming of acute surgical patients
result.setting: University teaching hospital, Manchester University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 81% referred within first 2 hours of presentation; 85 (24%) admitted and 276 (76%) discharged the same day; no adverse events.

result.other_findings: Prospective audit of a pilot pathway streaming patients from A&E to the surgical ANP team using set criteria.

result.setting: University Hospitals Plymouth
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean self-rated confidence 3.75-5.75 out of 10 before teaching.

result.intervention: One-off small group teaching session with homemade models (cost £10).

cycle2.result: Mean confidence 8.00-9.25 out of 10 after teaching; 87.5% rated the session excellent and 12.5% good.

result.other_findings: None of the eight learners had received formal fascia iliaca block teaching before.

result.setting: Tertiary breast surgery unit, Imperial College Healthcare Trust
result.standard: NICE NG45 pre-operative tests; trust guidance POA at least two weeks before surgery
result.intervention: Planned: MDT discussion, EPR virtual checklist and staff education (not yet implemented).
result.other_findings: Low clotting and G&S compliance attributed to ambiguity in guidelines; re-audit planned in 3 months.

result.topic: First rib fractures and associated injuries
result.setting: UK Trauma Audit and Research Network database
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: First rib fracture predicted ISS >15 (adjusted OR 2.64, 95% CI 2.33 to 3.00) and polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.80 to 2.25); risk-adjusted mortality unchanged (adjusted OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.19).

result.other_findings: Comparison group of 8369 patients with fractures of other ribs.

result.topic: Weight bearing after fragility fracture surgery
result.setting: Major Trauma Centre, Royal Stoke University Hospital
result.standard: BOAST: surgery in frail patients should allow full weight-bearing and be performed within 36 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 146 (93%) allowed full weight-bearing: 133 (98.5%) hip fractures and 12 (54.5%) non-hip fractures.

result.other_findings: Mean restricted weight bearing 42 days (range 28 to 56); authors suggest routine frailty assessment.

result.topic: Lynch syndrome testing in colorectal cancer
result.setting: Kettering General Hospital
result.standard: NICE DG27: Lynch syndrome testing for all newly diagnosed colorectal cancer; IHC results within 7–10 days

cycle1.result: All patients had IHC testing; only 15% had IHC results within 7–10 days; only 50% with MMR-deficient results referred for genetic testing.

result.other_findings: Recommendations include a clinical lead for the testing pathway, inter-specialty collaboration and education.

result.setting: 2 Week Wait one-stop breast clinic, Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCS Outpatient Clinics: A Guide to Good Practice and GIRFT Clinically-Led Specialty Outpatient Guidance (2023)

cycle1.result: Mean 2 hours 20 minutes from imaging to results; only 20% required core biopsy, further imaging or assessment.

result.intervention: New breast clinic proforma and pathway redesign allowing earlier discharge of patients with normal findings.

cycle2.result: Total clinic duration reduced by 36 minutes.

result.other_findings: Time saved was redirected to patients needing more complex assessment.

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2014: 19 operation note points

cycle1.result: 0% of the 19 points achieved 100% compliance.

result.intervention: Introduction of an electronic patient record, with results presented at the local governance meeting.

cycle2.result: Compliance improved by almost 19% (p=0.0003) between periods 1 and 5; 11 of 19 points (57.9%) achieved 100% compliance post-EPR.

result.other_findings: 250 notes over five periods (1 week, 4 weeks and a re-audit after EPR); antibiotic use, VTE prophylaxis and estimated blood loss stayed poor.

result.setting: University hospital, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, London
result.standard: ABS guidelines (excision for B3 lesions, pain, increasing size) and local consensus (excision over 30mm on ultrasound)

cycle1.result: 83.7% met ABS or local criteria.

result.intervention: Presentation and teaching at local departmental meeting.

result.other_findings: Discharge to long-term care 21.7% vs 14.3% (p = 0.19).

result.setting: Elective colorectal resections, North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local Enhanced Recovery after Surgery (ERAS) protocol

cycle1.result: not reported (baseline compliance figures not given).

result.intervention: Staff education and a postoperative ERAS booklet completed during the inpatient stay.

cycle2.result: Oral nutritional supplements, deep breathing, oral fluids and stoma care plans all above 90% compliance; average length of stay fell from 9 to 6 days between cycles 2 and 3.

result.other_findings: Three cycles over two years (30 patients); discharge planning documented in under 50% and mobilisation quantified in under 50%.

result.setting: Emergency and trauma theatres, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Local policy: preoperative hair removal in the anaesthetic room

cycle1.result: 6/15 (40%) shaved in the anaesthetic room; general surgery 2/9 (22%), trauma and orthopaedics 2/4 (50%).

result.intervention: Results presented to surgical leadership and SSI steering groups, information disseminated to teams, and posters on hair removal location.

cycle2.result: 9/12 (75%) shaved in the anaesthetic room; general surgery 7/9 (78%), trauma and orthopaedics 1/1 (100%).

result.other_findings: SSI rates were not measured.

result.topic: Public understanding of surgeon outcome data
result.setting: In-person survey at a state fair (Department of Urology, University of Minnesota)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 142 (40.6%) correctly estimated the complication rate; 7.6% recognised it was above the 99th percentile.

result.other_findings: Misinterpreters were more likely to make an inappropriate hypothetical decision (OR 2.75).

result.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon; district general hospital
result.standard: GIRFT 2019 hip and knee arthroplasty best practice documentation data items

cycle1.result: 26 THR and 23 knee arthroplasties; average compliance knee 71%, THR 68%.

result.intervention: Clinician education and discussion of the guidelines among local surgeons.

cycle2.result: 34 THR and 28 knee arthroplasties; average compliance knee 74%, THR 64%.

result.other_findings: 100% compliance in 5/23 THR and 9/27 knee criteria; range of movement and vascular status at end of surgery improved least.

result.topic: Early mobilisation of stable distal radius fractures
result.setting: Orthopaedic team receiving virtual fracture clinic referrals (Chelsea & Westminster Hospital, London; Worthing Hospital)
result.standard: BOAST guideline for distal radius fractures: patients with a stable fracture should be considered for early mobilisation with a removable support once pain allows

cycle1.result: 49.7% of 163 referred distal radius fractures were stable; of these only 37% were mobilised early, the rest fully immobilised for 6 weeks without an active mobilisation protocol

result.intervention: Proposed only: a protocol to screen all distal radius fractures in virtual fracture clinic as stable or unstable, with stable fractures seen for early physiotherapy face to face or virtually
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Outcomes of trainee-performed emergency inguinal hernia repair
result.setting: Single clinical unit, Department of General Surgery, tertiary care hospital (All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: SSI 4 (9.3%); mesh explantation 1 (2.32%); re-exploration 1 (2.32%); 1 mortality; mean LOH 4.33 days; long-term pain 20.93%; no recurrence; mean operating time 116.92 min; mean blood loss 93.7 ml

result.other_findings: Compared with published literature, trainee cases had more blood loss, more long-term pain (20.93% vs 1.2%) and slightly more wound complications (9.3% vs 6.74%), with comparable operating time, LOH, recurrence and mortality.

result.setting: Tertiary hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) national figures used as comparison

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 33.59 vs 15.1 days nationally (median 15 days); geriatrician review 87% vs 24% nationally; 30-day mortality 5.5% vs 9.7% nationally

result.intervention: Proposed only: special discussion of long-staying patients in weekly ward round meetings
result.other_findings: Patients with stomas had higher mean LOS (42 vs 26 days); more patients had high pre-operative mortality risk (51.5% vs 43.5%), ischaemia (20.8% vs 8.9%) and haemorrhage (5.6% vs 2.6%) than nationally.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Department of Health and Social Care and other national/local guidelines: post-diagnostic support offered to all patients diagnosed with dementia

cycle1.result: All patients were offered post-diagnostic support; diagnosis discussed in about 93%, medication in 82%, driving in only 64% and LPA in only 63%

result.other_findings: Slightly more women chose the post-diagnostic support group over a dementia adviser; 21% more patients opted for the group when they had a carer.

result.topic: Preoperative group and save before mastectomy
result.setting: Department of Breast Surgery, University Hospital Limerick
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: All patients had a routine preoperative G&H; 2/100 received post-operative blood transfusion (transfusion probability 2%); only 15% had a post-operative haemoglobin checked

result.other_findings: Mean haemoglobin drop was 2.3 g/dL; selective G&H requesting was projected to give significant cost savings but would need a validated risk stratification system.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis prescribing
result.setting: Adult ENT ward, emergency and pre-operative admissions (NHS GGC, Glasgow)
result.standard: ENT UK VTE prophylaxis guideline

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment clearly done for 39%; 22/63 (35%) meeting LMWH criteria received it; 5/96 (5%) meeting TEDS criteria received it; 45% had both prescribed according to the guideline

result.intervention: Planned only: departmental policy and staff education
result.other_findings: Pro-forma clerking (n = 148) improved risk assessment compared with freehand clerking (n = 25) (43% vs 12%) but not correct prescription (45% vs 40%); no VTE or unexpected bleeding occurred.

result.setting: Single bariatric centre (Phoenix Health, Chester)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 17 patients underwent SADIS, average BMI 55; weight loss greater than bypass patients at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years, with better sustained weight loss at 6-10 years; no increase in nutritional deficiencies

result.other_findings: The ratio of psychological to physiological co-morbidities was higher than average.

result.topic: Routine postoperative blood tests after arthroplasty
result.setting: One hospital, elective hip and knee arthroplasty (Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Four (3.8%) patients had no post-operative blood tests; mean haemoglobin drop 22.5 g/L; no transfusions or iron given; seven patients given IV fluids (one AKI, six hyponatraemia)

result.other_findings: Mean creatinine and eGFR were essentially unchanged after surgery; authors suggest targeting postoperative bloods to higher-risk patients.

result.setting: Buckinghamshire Breast Unit (Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: ABS 2023 Phyllodes guidelines for excision margins

cycle1.result: Unit not yet fully compliant; 59% (n=20) had one operation, 29% (n=10) two and 12% (n=4) three to obtain clear margins; 41% (n=14) required >1 operation; one mastectomy for malignant phyllodes might have been avoided under new guidelines

result.intervention: Planned: disseminate new guidance within departmental and regional networks, then re-audit
result.other_findings: 29 women (85%) had breast conservation and 5 (15%) mastectomy; no excess mastectomies for wide clear margins were identified.

result.setting: Regional plastic surgery department (Department of Burns and Plastic Surgery, Whiston Hospital, Liverpool)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: X-ray findings documented 55%; antibiotic plan 35%; post-op plan 100%; post-op antibiotics 90%; follow-up plan 95%

result.intervention: Updated hand trauma proforma including a free text box

cycle2.result: Overall completion increased; responsible consultant 100%; X-ray findings 85%; antibiotic plan 80%; but post-op plan fell to 85%, post-op antibiotics 75% and follow-up plan 60%

result.other_findings: Operation note documentation of anaesthetic type and tourniquet use/time improved; clinicians asked for a larger free-text box and hand diagram.

result.setting: Tertiary hospital surgical unit (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Local gentamicin dosing and serum level monitoring guidelines

cycle1.result: 70% of initial doses matched weight-based dosing; 55% had serum levels measured within the appropriate timeframe

cycle2.result: 92% of initial doses accurately prescribed; 78% had timely serum level measurements

result.other_findings: Re-audit was done at both one and two months after the interventions.

result.topic: Pre-operative mortality risk documentation in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Great Western Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: NELA key performance indicator: pre-operative mortality risk calculated and documented on consent form and in medical record; target ≥ 85%

cycle1.result: 80% (n = 39) had a calculated risk; of 27 (55%) who went to theatre, none had correct documentation as per NELA standards

result.intervention: Proposed only: NELA pathway document, poster and pre-operative mortality risk sticker
result.other_findings: Of 7 trainee and consultant questionnaire respondents, 4 rarely or never documented pre-operative mortality risk as per NELA guidance.

result.setting: Emergency departments, St Helier and Epsom hospitals (Epsom & St Helier Hospitals, London)
result.standard: NICE quality standards for assessment and management of renal colic (CTKUB timing, NSAID analgesia, time to urological intervention, bone profile/calcium, stone diet advice)

cycle1.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 97.9%; NSAIDs 54.5%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 70%; calcium requested 77.9%; dietary/fluid advice 8.7%

result.intervention: Patient leaflet on stone diet and a renal order-set, plus raising clinician awareness

cycle2.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 100%; NSAIDs 71.9%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 100%; calcium requested 94.7%; dietary/fluid advice 39.4%

result.other_findings: Dietary and lifestyle advice improved but remained low at 39.4%.

result.setting: North Devon District Hospital (Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, Barnstaple)
result.standard: NICE bladder cancer guidance 1.2.6 and 1.2.7 (documentation of tumour size and number, and mitomycin instillation)

cycle1.result: 78.20% of operation notes did not include mitomycin instillation or justification for not giving it; tumour number documented in 98.71% and tumour size in 88.46%

cycle2.result: Quality of operation note documentation improved doubly (no further figures given)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency department, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of attending ED

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% (8/31) reached ward <4 hours

result.intervention: 90 minute multidisciplinary simulation training programme on the hip fracture pathway for ED and related staff (32 people), in person and via Zoom, February 2021

cycle2.result: Average time to ward 5 hrs 58 mins (32% reduction); 72% (18/25) reached ward <4 hours

result.other_findings: Training included Emergency Medicine, Orthopaedics, nursing, Radiology, Radiography and porters.

result.setting: Single multicentre tertiary health network (Monash Health), Melbourne
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 23 438 ENA tests in 19 603 patients; 2636 (13.4%) had repeat testing, of whom 2523 (95.7%) had stable results and 53 (2.2%) changed from negative to positive; five new AARDs among 34 eligible patients

result.other_findings: 20 918 (89.2%) tests were negative; the commonest specificity was anti-Ro52 (1185, 51.4% of positives). No guidelines exist for repeat ENA ordering.

result.topic: Identification of faecal incontinence in inpatients
result.setting: Hospital inpatient wards, spot-check audit (Scunthorpe General Hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Nursing bowel documentation 90%, medical 48%; 10.8% had FI; 31% would have been identified by medical documentation; all (100%) referred appropriately

cycle2.result: Nursing bowel documentation 94%, medical 47%; 5.3% had FI; only 28% would have been identified by medical documentation; some action taken in 71.42% but no referral arranged in any

result.other_findings: 28.57% of patients with FI were on general surgical wards; medical documentation and onward referral need improvement.

result.setting: 8 UK district general hospitals, multicentre
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 21%; no association between PAS scores and histology (Spearman 0.004, p=0.951) or between ultrasound and histology (p= 0.336)

result.setting: Breast surgery under one consultant (Ysbyty Gwynedd, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Bangor)
result.standard: Association of Breast Surgery (ABS UK) recommendations on chemoprophylaxis in high-risk groups; national VTE risk <0.4%

cycle1.result: No VTE in any patient (compliant with national risk <0.4%); only two patients received chemoprophylaxis despite 11 with anaesthetic >3 hours and 22 with predisposing conditions

result.intervention: Planned only: a breast-specific standardised local VTE protocol
result.other_findings: 119 (73.5%) operations were for malignancy; one patient was imaged for suspected pulmonary embolism and was negative.

result.setting: Acute surgical unit, University Hospital Limerick
result.standard: University Hospital Limerick guidelines on urine testing

cycle1.result: 68% had urinalysis and 48% urine culture; only 23 of 47 (49%) cultures were indicated

result.intervention: Information sheet placed in the ASU and an education session for nursing staff

cycle2.result: 39% had urinalysis; 28% had urine culture, of which 79% were indicated

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Admission for epistaxis with nasal packing
result.setting: ENT department (Ulster Hospital, Dundonald)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 100% (n = 15) of patients with rapid rhino admitted; average 3.9 bed-days; 5 (33%) needed arterial ligation

result.intervention: Patients sent home with nasal pack in situ and outpatient follow-up

cycle2.result: 7% (n = 1) admitted; average 2 bed-days; one (7%) needed ligation; no difference in 30-day morbidity and mortality

result.other_findings: Total bed-days 57 v 4, costing £12654 v £888 at £222 per bed-day; 60% attended out of hours.

result.topic: Botulinum toxin injection for plantar fasciitis
result.setting: Musculoskeletal clinic
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: All patients improved on VAS at 4 weeks, 38 (90.48%) pain free; 38 (90.48%) had no heel pain on palpation; 40 (95.24%) had improved HTI scores

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in inguinal hernia repair

result.standard: National guidance: no antibiotic prophylaxis for low-risk patients; single dose for high-risk patients

cycle1.result: 53.33% of patients received antibiotics in line with national guidelines; 50.00% had prophylactic antibiotics overall

result.setting: Paediatric tonsillectomy discharge summaries (Musgrove Park Hospital, Taunton)
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines for paediatric tonsillectomy discharge information

cycle1.result: Go to ED if significant bleed 21% (6); see GP if persistent fever 7% (2); regular analgesia 78% (22); regular diet 46% (13)

result.intervention: One-click pre-defined discharge summary inserts ("snippets"), designed after a departmental survey

cycle2.result: Go to ED if significant bleed 93% (14); see GP if persistent fever 73% (11); regular analgesia 100% (15); regular diet 73% (11)

result.other_findings: Further cycles planned on parent understanding and satisfaction.

result.setting: Community mental health team, Parkview Mental Health Resource Centre, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Two simultaneous online MDTs run by the same staff, with staff dipping in and out and no formal structure (no baseline figures given)

cycle2.result: 100% of staff felt the new MDT structure was useful; 84% satisfied with the new way of running MDT; 84% satisfied with designated MDT teams

result.other_findings: Outcome was measured by staff feedback survey only.

result.setting: Laparoscopic appendicectomy consent forms (The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust)
result.standard: GMC and RCS England consent standards; 17 key risks from national guidelines and consultant consensus

cycle1.result: Only four risks documented in >75%: bleeding 98.5%, infection 95.6%, injury to nearby structures 83.8%, conversion to open 88.2%; bowel injury 61.8%, bladder injury 36.8%, ureter injury 22.1%, death 13.2%, reintervention 23.5%, hernia 63.2%

result.intervention: Procedure-specific consent template introduced; re-audit planned
result.other_findings: Among 46 female patients, gynaecological risks were documented in just 30.4%.

result.setting: General surgery and urology receiving wards (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Clinical governance: every patient should have a named consultant, with bedside whiteboard matching the electronic system (TrakCare)

result.intervention: Verbal and written communication with nursing staff and junior doctors

cycle2.result: Third cycle: only 1 (2.6%) missing consultant's name

result.other_findings: Second cycle, 2 weeks after the intervention, found only 1 (2.6%) bed-board with incorrect or no names.

result.setting: Major trauma centre (University Hospital Coventry)
result.standard: Departmental guideline on upper limb bite injuries, updated in line with the British Society for Surgery of the Hand

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Departmental guideline updated in accordance with BSSH guidance, with an action plan

result.setting: Surgical ambulatory unit, general surgery (Southern Health & Social Care Trust, Craigavon)
result.standard: NICE QS174 and RCS England safe handover guidance: referral to include diagnosis, background and plan

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Team education and reminder prompts across the department

cycle2.result: Improvement in all domains: diagnosis (p<0.0001), background (p<0.0001) and plan (p=0.0007); referrals with no information significantly reduced (p=0.0063)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary referral neurosurgery centre (Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: not reported

result.other_findings: Average length of stay 17 days; average theatre time 2h11m; designated acute theatres used about 75% of the time. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: District hospital internal paper referral slips (University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay Trust)
result.standard: not reported

result.other_findings: True usage was approximated because some sheets were retained by consultants.

result.setting: Laparoscopic appendicectomy patients (Aneurin Bevan Health Board; Cardiff & Vale Health Board)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 100% included infection and bleeding; 88% conversion to open; 82% bowel resection and damage to local structures; 76% blood clots; 76% legible; 65% contained acronyms; 82% documented alternative therapies discussed

result.other_findings: 18 different complications were used with high variability; on questionnaire only 64% of patients recalled basic complications and 43% remembered being offered alternative treatments.

result.setting: University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust, regional audit
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for management of ACL injury

cycle1.dates: 1st of July 2018 and the 1st of July 2019 (pre-covid); 1st of July 2021 and 1st of July 2022 (post-covid)
cycle1.result: 82% had timely clinic assessment; 37% had MRI within 14 days; 38% referred for prehabilitation; 84% had post-operative physiotherapy

result.topic: Violence and aggression on inpatient mental health wards
result.setting: Pine Ward, Park Royal mental health unit
result.standard: Project aim: improve patient and staff safety by 20% by end of December 2025

cycle1.result: Verbal aggression 4 per day shift; aggression towards objects 2; PRN psychotropic use 4 per day shift

result.intervention: Weekly community meeting, observation of patient positive strengths, messages in nursing station on using soft words, and Section 17 leave flow chart for patients

cycle2.result: Patient safety improved by 25% and staff safety by 30%; verbal aggression fell from 4 to 2 per day shift; aggression towards objects 2 to 1; PRN use 4 to 2

result.other_findings: Verbal aggression against staff remains a key concern; Datix incident records to be reviewed in a future audit.

result.setting: Emergency surgical unit (Belfast Health & Social Care Trust)
result.standard: GAIN Guidelines 2011; Trust discharge proforma of 33 parameters, summary acceptable if >90% of information recorded accurately

cycle1.result: Discharge failure rate 60%

result.intervention: Dedicated teaching and training on E-Discharge compilation at induction
result.other_findings: Recording of follow-up care and ongoing primary care involvement remained inadequate.

result.setting: ENT Rapid Access Clinic, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines for management of sudden onset sensorineural hearing loss

cycle1.result: Average referral to intervention 1.47 days, to first ENT review 3.82 days, to first audiogram 4.43 days; presentation to oral steroids 0.33 days; symptom onset to oral steroids 7.5 days

result.intervention: Management pathway reinforced as per ENT UK guidelines and urgent audiogram organisation improved
result.other_findings: Late patient presentation noted; importance of tuning fork testing when an audiogram is not immediately available emphasised.

result.topic: Below knee amputation pathway in orthoplastic trauma
result.setting: Major trauma centre, orthoplastic patients (Royal London Hospital)
result.standard: NICE guidelines for complex fractures and the Vascular Society guidance for major amputations

cycle1.result: 100% compliance with pre-operative MDT discussion, recording decision to amputate, and formal referral to amputee rehabilitation; average time to surgery after decision 1.75 days

result.intervention: Planned: a written pathway for lower limb amputations in the trust
result.other_findings: Lower compliance with written counselling for families, naming a discharge co-ordinator pre-operatively and pain team review within 24 hours post-operatively.

result.topic: qFIT use in two week wait colorectal referrals
result.setting: Two week wait referrals, Somerset Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE recommendation of qFIT as replacement for faecal occult blood testing

cycle1.result: 74 patients eligible for qFIT, only 7 had it; 93 qFIT performed by GPs with 11 positive; 11 (3.8%) colorectal cancers identified

result.intervention: New 2WW referral form and qFIT made available to general practitioners

cycle2.result: 18 patients eligible for qFIT, all had it; 155 qFIT performed with 18 positive; 12 (5.4%) colorectal cancers identified

result.other_findings: qFIT use rose as 2WW referrals and qFIT-eligible patients fell.

result.setting: Monday-Friday emergency general surgery theatre lists (The Prince Charles Hospital, Brisbane, Queensland)
result.standard: Operating Theatre Efficiency Guideline: late start is time into operating room after the scheduled session start time

cycle1.result: 81% of morning lists delayed; afternoon lists 50% delayed; Mondays 77% and Thursdays 69% delayed

cycle2.result: 66% of morning lists delayed; afternoon lists 55% delayed; Mondays 56% and Thursdays 43% delayed

result.other_findings: No reasons were documented for morning delays; afternoon delays were mostly due to overrunning elective lists but poorly documented.

result.setting: On-call urology team (Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Trust guidelines: 10 documentation items for urethral catheterisation

cycle1.result: Only 28% (14/50) had all 10 items documented; indication best at 94% (47/50); chaperone and groin examination lowest at 44% (22/50)

result.other_findings: 72% (36/50) of catheters were inserted by the urology team.

result.setting: National trainee survey of UK renal transplant units
result.standard: not reported

result.topic: Surgical teaching programme for junior doctors

result.other_findings: 44.4% could not attend half the sessions because of clinical commitments; morning sessions before handover recommended.

result.setting: Regional hospital (Wexford General Hospital)
