result.standard: Local protocol for assessment and treatment of children on psychostimulants

cycle1.result: Protocol used appropriately in the majority of children.

result.other_findings: Children often had co-morbid psychopathology and family and psychosocial difficulties.

result.topic: Extended role of health care assistants
result.setting: Critical care unit, Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Staff questionnaire, 64% response; support for an extended HCA role but varied views on skills and training.

result.intervention: Initiatives from the initial survey to extend the HCA role

cycle2.result: 58% response; most staff aware of and positive about the changes but wanted more information and involvement.

result.other_findings: Survey of staff opinion rather than measurement against a standard.

result.setting: All UK radiotherapy centres, national audit
result.standard: Joint Collegiate Council for Oncology (JCCO) waiting time guidelines

cycle1.result: Not reported in detail.

cycle2.result: Waiting times lengthened in most centres; fewer patients in all categories treated within JCCO guidelines; no further rise in median palliative wait.

result.other_findings: Single-fraction palliation now common; no simple link between staff or machine numbers and waits.

result.setting: District general hospital, Scotland (about 3800 deliveries per year)
result.standard: Local guideline: single intraoperative IV antibiotic dose after delivery; target 90% coverage

cycle1.result: 14% received prophylactic antibiotics; infection-related morbidity 28.5%; wound infection 17.5%.

result.intervention: New guidelines requiring a single intraoperative IV antibiotic dose

cycle2.result: 81% received prophylaxis (difference 67%, 95% CI 60-74%); infective morbidity 16%; wound infection 9%.

result.other_findings: 90% target not met; postnatal stay significantly shorter (P < 0.0001).

result.setting: St George's Hospital, London teaching hospital
result.standard: Local targets: low rupture rates, high sonographic diagnosis, acceptable tubal conservation and laparoscopic surgery rates

cycle1.result: Not reported in detail.

cycle2.result: Substantial improvement, mainly in ultrasound diagnosis, with fewer ruptured ectopics; laparoscopic rate stable.

result.other_findings: More junior doctors performed laparoscopic surgery; laparoscopy shortened hospital stay.

result.setting: Children's hospital (Alder Hey, Liverpool)
result.standard: Criteria for a full audit

cycle1.result: 27.8% met criteria for a full audit; 22.2% were re-audited.

result.other_findings: Recommends audit methodology training and annual audit of audits.

result.setting: Dental polyclinic, St Thomas' Hospital, London (undergraduate dental students)
result.standard: Modified CRABEL scoring system

cycle1.result: Department where patient was seen most often missing, followed by illegible demonstrator and student signatures.

result.intervention: Tutorial presentation of results and teaching session on good record keeping to 20 students

cycle2.result: Almost all elements improved, most reaching 100%, except updated medical history and most recent complaint.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Multicentre GU clinics, North Thames region
result.standard: National guidelines for antibiotic treatment of chlamydia and test of cure

cycle1.result: Previous audit; figures not reported.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in centres following national antibiotic prescribing guidelines and offering test of cure when indicated.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Gynaecology department, Stobhill Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: Auditable standards from published guidelines on counselling for female sterilisation

cycle1.result: Long-term alternatives 33%; irreversibility 94%; failure rate 96%; ectopic risk 48%; intended method 39%; operative risks 67%; continuing contraception 37%.

cycle2.result: Proforma used in 62% (100% compliant when used); long-term alternatives 68%; irreversibility 78%; failure rate 78%; ectopic risk 66%; intended method 66%; operative risks 66%; continuing contraception 64%.

result.other_findings: Proforma led to both improvement and deterioration; irreversibility and failure rate documentation fell.

result.setting: Hull and East Yorkshire Multidisciplinary Thyroid Clinic, tertiary referral
result.standard: Best practice principles (not specified)

cycle1.result: Permanent vocal cord palsy 8%; haematoma 5%; permanent hypoparathyroidism 8%.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary thyroid clinic established and best practice principles implemented

cycle2.result: Permanent vocal cord palsy 0%; haematoma 2%; permanent hypoparathyroidism 2%.

result.other_findings: Caseload rose, preoperative investigations fell and surgery types were standardised; outcome comparison rather than audit against a standard.

result.setting: General practices in Lothian; CABG patients from the regional centre (Royal Infirmary, Edinburgh)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean systolic BP 142.5 (19.2) mm Hg.

result.intervention: Lists of CABG patients and first survey results sent to practices; Lothian Health recall project for cardiac patients (65 of 128 practices)

cycle2.result: 918 questionnaires (92%) on 875 patients: 17% smoked, 86% took aspirin; mean systolic BP 139.4 (19.1) mm Hg.

result.other_findings: Substantial improvements in risk factor management reported.

result.setting: Birmingham and Midland Eye Centre
result.standard: Ideal informed consent (patient knowledge assessed by interview)

cycle1.result: 37% understood what a cataract was; 48% understood surgery; 48% thought surgery risk-free; mean anxiety VAS 2.89.

result.intervention: Non-paternalistic consent approach with new patient consent forms

cycle2.result: 39% understood a cataract; 28% understood surgery; 43% thought surgery risk-free; mean anxiety VAS 5.00.

result.other_findings: 80% then 100% of second-eye patients believed surgery was risk-free.

result.setting: Urology department, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Trust, London
result.standard: Departmental guidelines for requesting urine cytology

cycle1.result: 33% of requests inappropriate; cost of unnecessary samples £2418.

result.intervention: Departmental request guidelines circulated with staff education
result.other_findings: Estimated annual saving £55,000.

result.setting: 13 Lasercare clinics (private and NHS)
result.standard: Documentation of six criteria: consent, Fitzpatrick skin type, appropriate laser, appropriate fluence, patient satisfaction, objective assessment

cycle1.result: Median 100% for consent, laser and fluence; skin type 90%; patient satisfaction 67%; objective assessment 53% (772 treatments overall).

cycle2.result: Nine clinics: significant improvement in patient satisfaction (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.15-0.78, P=0.01) and objective assessment (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.07-0.50, P=0.0003).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Otolaryngology department, Royal Surrey County Hospital, Guildford
result.standard: Department of Health High Impact Changes: day surgery as the norm

cycle1.result: Curettage adenoidectomy: PONV 21%; bleeding 9.7%; same-day discharge 40.3%.

result.intervention: Suction coagulation adenoidectomy plus an anaesthetic protocol to reduce PONV
result.other_findings: Mainly a comparison of surgical technique outcomes.

result.topic: CT image quality in abdominal trauma
result.setting: Radiology department, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: First 8 years after body CT installation
cycle1.result: 52% (64/122) unsatisfactory images, mainly inadequate IV contrast; 60% out of hours vs 45% in hours.

result.intervention: New dedicated CT system for all abdominal work and technique guidelines issued to radiographers and radiologists
result.other_findings: Dedicated body CT gave fewer unsatisfactory scans (42% vs 69%); abdomen-focused studies better (40% vs 67%).

result.setting: Adult emergency department, inner city teaching hospital (Bristol)
result.standard: Guidelines using a clinical scoring system for sore throat

cycle1.result: Inappropriate antibiotic prescribing 44%; correct antibiotic 60%; supportive advice documented 67.8%.

result.intervention: Proforma-based guidelines with clinical scoring system and staff education

cycle2.result: Inappropriate prescribing 11%; correct antibiotic 100%; supportive advice 58%.

result.other_findings: Documented supportive advice fell despite wider variety of advice.

result.setting: A&E department (St George's, London)
result.standard: All patients discharged from A&E with epistaxis given verbal and written advice

cycle1.result: Verbal advice 19%; written advice 2%; 11 (17%) re-attenders.

result.intervention: Presentation to A&E doctors on epistaxis management and advice leaflets placed in the department
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency department resuscitation room, large district general hospital (Portsmouth)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Temperature recorded in 13.4%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Large government hospital, Kampala
result.standard: Criteria developed by an expert panel

cycle1.result: Most standards rarely achieved.

result.intervention: Guidelines, extra supplies purchased, streamlined labour ward procedures and more staff

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in diagnosis, monitoring and treatment.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Medical admissions unit, General Infirmary, Leeds
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Patients discharged before resolution of withdrawal symptoms.

cycle2.result: Symptom duration significantly reduced; length of stay reduced (not significant).

result.other_findings: Most patients who had both regimens found symptom-triggered treatment more effective.

result.setting: Delivery suite, Kingston Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: Delivery suite protocol and national guidelines on breech presentation

cycle1.result: Low ECV success rate and deficient documentation of written consent for ECV; other care satisfactory.

result.intervention: Results presented to a multidisciplinary meeting and disseminated to stakeholders

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documented consent for ECV; good breech detection, optimal ECV offer rate and good neonatal outcome.

result.other_findings: ECV uptake and success rate still needed improvement.

result.setting: London Ambulance Service, catchment of four hospitals
result.standard: Service treatment protocols aligned with British Thoracic Society acute asthma guidelines

cycle1.result: Some under-recognition and under-treatment of severe asthma; poor documentation of on-scene condition; 58% of A&E-diagnosed asthma patients given nebulised salbutamol by crew.

result.intervention: Protocols widened in line with BTS guidelines, results disseminated and training for all operational staff

cycle2.result: 75% of A&E-diagnosed asthma patients given nebulised salbutamol; 43 asthma patients untreated; protocol adherence high.

result.other_findings: Pre-hospital documentation of key observations did not improve; salbutamol given to more non-asthma patients (15 to 161).

result.setting: General practices in the city of Chester
result.standard: Epilepsy quality marker in the new GP contract (regular review)

cycle1.result: 41% seen by a GP in the past year; 19% had regular review; 49% saw no doctor about epilepsy in the past year; 11% diagnostic uncertainty; 29.2% in documented remission.

result.intervention: Computerised template with suggestions produced for every patient; review left to each GP
result.other_findings: Of 109 women of child-bearing age, 37 were on sodium valproate; 43% of adults who should have shared care did not; re-audit planned in 2 years.

result.topic: Outcome audit in a secure rehabilitation unit
result.setting: 12-bed low-secure intensive rehabilitation unit, Pennine Care NHS Trust, Rochdale
result.standard: Standardised psychometric outcome measures (no standard stated)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes integrating an audit system into clinical governance; no numerical results given.

result.setting: Orthodontic departments, Southend and Basildon district general hospitals
result.standard: Regular attenders with unerupted palatal canines referred by age 12, with wait no longer than 20 weeks

cycle1.result: 98% seen within 20 weeks; 16.5% referred by age 12; 82% had retained deciduous canines.

result.intervention: Management algorithm distributed to all local dentists

cycle2.result: 98% seen within 20 weeks; 27% referred by age 12 (p = 0.09); 76% retained deciduous canines (p = 0.29).

result.other_findings: Referral practice remained generally poor.

result.setting: Emergency surgical admissions, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines for abdominal radiograph requests

cycle1.result: RCR guidelines followed in 73 of 225 (32%); positive findings 76.7% when guidelines followed vs 8.9% when not.

result.other_findings: No difference between July and August house surgeons (positive findings 22% vs 24%), refuting the 'August syndrome'.

result.setting: Glasgow hospitals (Effective Gynaecology in Glasgow Group)
result.standard: RCOG Green-top Guideline 25

cycle1.result: Not reported in abstract (given in Table I).

result.intervention: Results distributed to units and formal instruction in the RCOG guideline
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Patient prompt sheets in outpatient clinic
result.setting: Oncology outpatient clinic, Barnet and Chase Farm NHS Trust, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 254 of 300 (85%) received prompt sheets; 65% found them very helpful and 10% fairly helpful.

result.intervention: Introduction of a patient prompt sheet
result.other_findings: Satisfaction survey; one-third asked more questions; men with prostate cancer found it particularly helpful.

result.setting: General dental practices, Eastern England
result.standard: Contemporary antibiotic prescribing guidelines and agreed standards

cycle1.result: 43% of prescriptions error-free in dose, frequency or duration; 29.2% justified.

result.intervention: Education on prescribing guidelines, presentation of previous errors and agreed standards
result.other_findings: 212 practitioners took part; amoxicillin and metronidazole were most prescribed.

result.setting: King's College Hospital, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: One or two Dilapan dilators with or without misoprostol: nine cases of cervical and uterine damage.

result.intervention: Two or three Dilapan dilators on the day before the procedure

cycle2.result: Improved cervical preparation and reduced risk of uterine and cervical damage.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Head and neck cancer MDT, Charing Cross Hospital, London
result.standard: NHS Cancer Plan referral-to-treatment within 1 month

cycle1.result: Not reported in detail.

result.intervention: Trust-wide Intranet database for tracking patients with automated pathology and radiology worklists

cycle2.result: Highly significant reduction in patients whose treatment planning was delayed by unavailable investigations.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: ENT department, Derbyshire Royal Infirmary
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Primary haemorrhage 1.8% (8/441); secondary haemorrhage 15.4% (68/441).

cycle2.result: Primary haemorrhage 1.4% (6/416), p=0.666; secondary haemorrhage 5.8% (24/416), p<0.001.

result.other_findings: Retrospective outcome comparison of techniques.

result.setting: Maternity units in Glasgow (Princess Royal Maternity Hospital)
result.standard: RCOG guidelines on antenatal corticosteroids

cycle1.result: 0.64 courses per delivery at 24-36 weeks; repeat courses 5%; potentially effective courses 24%.

result.intervention: Report of findings disseminated to all Glasgow maternity units

cycle2.result: 1.18 courses per delivery; repeat courses <1%; potentially effective courses 35%.

result.other_findings: Few courses were potentially effective when given for pre-term labour.

result.setting: ENT department, Hull Royal Infirmary
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice guidelines

cycle1.result: Patient ID 94%; surgeon name 98%; postoperative instructions 94%; assistant 82%; operative diagnosis 46%; incision 87%; wound closure 83%.

result.intervention: Results shared with surgeons and printed RCS aide-memoire in all ENT theatres
result.other_findings: Time of surgery and emergency or elective status still poorly recorded.

result.setting: Consultant-led and nurse-led TOP clinics, south Glasgow
result.standard: National guidelines on counselling about complications and sequelae before induced abortion

cycle1.result: Adequate counselling documented in 98% of nurse-led and 43% of consultant-led clinics.

result.intervention: Integrated care pathway altered to list potential complications and sequelae

cycle2.result: Adequate counselling 100% in nurse-led and 64% in consultant-led clinics.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Wakefield general practices
result.standard: Public Health (Infectious Diseases) Regulations 1988: all doctors must notify suspected gastrointestinal infection and food poisoning

cycle1.result: Considerable variation in GP reporting behaviour and timeliness of notification of suspected gastroenteritis and food poisoning.

result.intervention: A series of local interventions to improve notification (not described in detail).

cycle2.result: Notification rates and timeliness had not improved; they had deteriorated.

result.other_findings: Authors conclude the notification system for gastroenteritis and food poisoning is not working and should be substantially revised or abandoned.

result.setting: Waiting list initiative cases at an alternative healthcare provider compared with a primary healthcare trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Secondary haemorrhage rate 17.8% in waiting list initiative cases at the alternative provider vs 3.9% in the primary healthcare trust (p 0.1).

result.other_findings: Described as a completed audit loop; authors conclude adequate analgesia for the first week after tonsillectomy is essential to keep secondary haemorrhage within an acceptable range.

result.setting: Emergency departments across the UK (national survey)
result.standard: Spinal boards should be used for extrication and transport, with usual removal after the primary survey

cycle1.result: Previous audit: 5% removed patients immediately; 52% removed after senior log roll clearance; 43% left patients on boards until radiological clearance; 48% placed patients on boards after arrival.

cycle2.result: 21% removed patients immediately; 58% removed after senior clinician clearance following log roll; 21% still left patients on boards routinely until radiological clearance; 45% placed patients on boards after arrival even if not on one pre-hospital.

result.other_findings: Number of boards per department was similar and in-house audits of usage remained largely unchanged at 22%.

result.setting: Intensive care unit, University College Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: ICU nurse-led enteral feeding algorithm (feed type, target volume by body weight, dietetic referral criteria)

cycle1.result: 90% (n = 43) of dietetic referrals met referral criteria; absolute compliance (correct feed type and volume, correct prescription and accurate documented weight) was 2% (n = 1); 60% of patients were receiving the correct feed regimen.

result.other_findings: Nursing staff need further support in assessing body weight; ongoing multidisciplinary education and regular re-audit recommended.

result.topic: Day-case inguinal hernia pain and patient information
result.setting: Day-case inguinal herniorrhaphy, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 10% of patients had poor understanding of postoperative complications; 38% had early postoperative pain.

result.intervention: Patient information leaflets introduced and intraoperative and postoperative analgesia standardised, including wound infiltration of local anaesthetic at the end of surgery.

cycle2.result: Early postoperative pain fell to 23% with wound infiltration of local anaesthetic.

result.other_findings: Prompted by a patient complaint; initial telephone survey of patient experience preceded the prospective audit.

result.setting: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Record keeping standards (not specified)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Audit recommendations and action plans with stakeholder involvement and senior nurse support.

cycle2.result: Improving audit data reported (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Keys to success were stakeholder involvement, senior nurse support and use of data for local and trust-wide purposes.

result.setting: ENT department, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough
result.standard: External dacryocystorhinostomy by a consultant ophthalmologist as gold standard (success rate 94%); success defined as watering 'better' or 'cured'

cycle1.result: Laser-assisted endonasal dacryocystorhinostomy success rate 64%, significantly worse than external dacryocystorhinostomy.

result.intervention: Changed technique of choice from laser-assisted to cold steel endonasal dacryocystorhinostomy.

cycle2.result: Cold steel endonasal success rate 79% (45/57); no difference from external dacryocystorhinostomy (p = 0.55).

result.other_findings: 93% of cold steel cases were day cases and 39% were under local anaesthetic; anaesthetic type made no difference to success (p = 0.93).

result.setting: Multicentre prospective audit of tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Postoperative haemorrhage rate well within acceptable range; Draffin rods, Boyle-Davis gag and bipolar diathermy forceps found poor quality and difficult to use.

result.intervention: Manufacturer redesigned the criticised single-use instruments.

cycle2.result: Haemorrhage rate within acceptable range; redesigned instruments judged as good as, or better than, re-usable instruments.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest single-use instruments may be more cost effective.

result.setting: Gastroenterology unit, Royal Alexandra Hospital, Renfrewshire (district general hospital)
result.standard: Published evidence-based management of hepatorenal syndrome

cycle1.result: All 11 patients with hepatorenal syndrome died.

result.intervention: Evidence-based protocol for diagnosis and management of hepatorenal syndrome introduced.

cycle2.result: Second group received more appropriate and aggressive therapy; 2 had renal function corrected and 1 was discharged.

result.other_findings: Renal impairment and liver disease stage were equivalent in both groups; alcohol was the cause of liver disease in all patients.

result.setting: ENT department, Colchester General Hospital (paediatric tonsillectomy)
result.standard: Gold standard for postoperative vomiting (not specified)

cycle1.result: Postoperative vomiting 27%.

result.other_findings: 107 patients across both cycles.

result.setting: Day surgery unit, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Glasgow
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Unplanned admission rate 3.7%.

result.other_findings: Commonest causes were nausea/vomiting 23.5% (n = 56), bleeding 13.9% (n = 34) and unexpected procedure difficulty 11.8% (n = 28); orchidopexy, circumcision and dental extraction most often involved.

result.setting: Acute medical services, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: Evidence-based falls and syncope algorithms

cycle1.result: 10.6% admitted with falls and syncope; readmission 12%; mortality 12%.

result.intervention: Evidence-based management algorithms for falls and syncope introduced.

cycle2.result: 8.2% admitted with falls and syncope; readmission 0%; mortality 12%.

result.other_findings: Length of stay unchanged; inappropriate investigations decreased and appropriate management strategies increased.

result.setting: 32 acute adult psychiatric inpatient services
result.standard: Clinical guidelines: single antipsychotic at standard dose

cycle1.result: High-dose prescribing 36%; combined antipsychotic prescribing 43%.

result.intervention: Feedback of benchmarked data and bespoke change interventions.
result.other_findings: p.r.n. prescriptions were the main cause of high-dose and combined prescribing on both occasions.

result.topic: Radiotherapy interruptions in head and neck cancer
result.setting: 48 of 57 UK radiotherapy centres (national audit)
result.standard: National guidelines on managing radiotherapy interruptions; completion within target; start within 4 weeks

cycle1.result: 62% of interrupted cases completed within 1 day of target; 41% started treatment within 4 weeks.

result.intervention: New national guidelines on management of interruptions.

cycle2.result: 397/631 (63%) had interruptions; 88% of interrupted cases completed within 1 day of target; 92% of all cases within 1 day and 95% within 2 days; 52% started within 4 weeks.

result.other_findings: Causes of interruptions similar to 2002; waiting times shortened but remained unacceptable.

result.setting: Glaucoma clinic, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: Glaucoma patients with bilateral field defects should be advised to inform the DVLA

cycle1.result: Driving status documented in 9%; 20% of drivers with bilateral field defects advised to inform DVLA, with 11.4% documentation.

cycle2.result: Driving status documented in 99%; advice given and documented in 97% of drivers with bilateral field defects.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Third and fourth degree perineal tear management
result.setting: Three Glasgow maternity hospitals
result.standard: RCOG Guideline No. 29

cycle1.result: Shortcomings in practice identified.

result.intervention: Findings circulated and an operative proforma introduced.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: ENT emergency clinic, Heart of England NHS Trust, Birmingham
result.standard: No gold standard for service

cycle1.result: Mean waiting time 70 minutes.

result.other_findings: Appropriateness of referrals improved; telephone survey of eight West Midlands trusts informed the model.

result.setting: 48 assertive outreach teams across the UK
result.standard: Evidence-based standards for screening for the metabolic syndrome (blood pressure, obesity, glucose, lipids)

cycle1.result: Baseline screening rates for all four aspects (figures not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Screening for all four aspects increased significantly (35 teams).

result.other_findings: Clozapine treatment and known diabetes or dyslipidaemia increased the likelihood of full screening.

result.setting: Colorectal clinics, St Thomas' Hospital, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Did-not-attend rate 21% (males 28.6%, females 16.9%; P = 0.001).

result.setting: Hypopacks across Northern Ireland emergency departments, neonatal units and Regional Children's Hospital
result.standard: Hypopack protocol for investigation of unexplained hypoglycaemia

cycle1.result: Problems: samples taken during dextrose, incomplete history, insufficient and haemolysed samples, poor filing of reports.

result.topic: Mental Health Review Tribunal report quality

result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists framework of 18 criteria for tribunal reports

cycle1.result: Current practice assessed against the 18 criteria (figures not given in abstract).

result.setting: 8 hospitals in three districts in Malawi

result.standard: Standards for PPH management based on WHO manuals

result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, Central Manchester University Hospitals

result.setting: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, Birmingham Women's NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Desired therapeutic vancomycin plasma concentration 15-25 mg/L

cycle2.result: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (first 60.8%, second 60%, subsequent 65.6%); 71.3% allowing 10% variability.

result.standard: Trust KPI: 85% of urgent items (TTAs) dispensed within 1 hour; 85% of non-urgent items within 3 hrs

result.other_findings: Labelling was the rate-limiting step; proposals include extra labelling staff at peak times and induction teaching; re-audit planned in 3 months.

result.setting: Oculoplastic day surgery theatres, Corneo-Plastic Unit, Queen Victoria Hospital, East Grinstead (tertiary centre)
result.standard: Operating list utilisation rate (anaesthetic plus surgical time as proportion of planned session time)

result.setting: Orthodontic diagnostic teaching clinics, King's College Hospital, London

result.other_findings: AES prescribing rates varied.

result.setting: Dublin Dental University Hospital (undergraduate teaching)
result.standard: Four radiographic criteria: no voids, filling termination 0-2 mm of apex, all roots filled, original anatomy maintained

cycle2.result: Acceptable in 23/40 (57.5%) single-rooted and 68/129 (52.7%) multirooted canals; 45.2% of multirooted teeth acceptable (P = 0.042).

result.setting: St Helens and Knowsley Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, Whiston, Merseyside
result.standard: not reported

cycle2.result: Post intervention errors 90/1677 in the intervention group vs 236/984 in the control group (p<0.005); mean change -11.5% intervention vs +5.9% control, mean difference 17.4% (95% CI -27.3 to -7.6), p<0.05.

result.other_findings: Controlled pilot study design with prospective prescribing audits.

result.topic: NSAID prescribing in chronic kidney disease

cycle2.result: Imaging within 24 h 47.7%, severity stratification within 48 h 75%, critical care admission for severe 63.6%, definitive treatment during index admission 38.5%.

result.other_findings: Survival 100% in this cycle vs 95% region-wide; care still did not reach BSG standards.

result.setting: Community palliative care, St Christopher's Hospice, London
result.standard: Local anticipatory prescribing guidance (four drug classes)

cycle1.result: 75/76 (99%) prescribed analgesic, antiemetic, antisecretory and anxiolytic; 49/76 (64%) given as-required medicines at home; haloperidol 88% of antiemetics

result.intervention: Updated local guidelines, teaching for medical and non-medical prescribers, sharing results nationally

cycle2.result: Antisecretory prescriptions reduced by 57% and antiemetic by 50%; antiemetics levomepromazine 47%, haloperidol 35%, cyclizine 14%, metoclopramide 3%

result.other_findings: Those without an antiemetic did not later need one dispensed; haloperidol cost about £2000/month.

result.setting: Urology outpatient clinic, Frimley Park NHS Trust
result.standard: GMC guidance on chaperone use and documentation for intimate examination

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Raising awareness among the 12 team members

cycle2.result: Documentation improved by 9.85% in clinical notes and 36.65% in clinic letters

result.other_findings: Scoring system used for team and individual performance.

result.setting: Medical unit, Southmead Hospital, North Bristol NHS Trust
result.standard: Patients consented before LMWH prescription considering religious and dietary preferences

cycle1.result: 95% (58/61) of healthcare professionals did not consider religious or dietary preferences when prescribing LMWH

result.intervention: Patient written and audiovisual information, staff eLearning, switching policy to a synthetic alternative, written consent prompt

cycle2.result: Proportion appropriately consented for LMWH increased (figure given only as 80%)

result.other_findings: Two QI cycles; positive feedback and high demand for a non-animal-derived alternative.

result.setting: UK radiotherapy departments, RCR national re-audit
result.standard: Guideline-recommended radical radiotherapy for NSCLC (RCR 2013 audit standards)

cycle1.result: Under-treatment and marked variability between networks; 4-dimensional planning used in 33%

result.intervention: Various national and local interventions (not detailed)

cycle2.result: 93% of centres returned data; radical radiotherapy up 70% since 2013; waits 20% longer (p = 0.02); 79% of PET/CT scans outside desirable timeframe; 4-dimensional planning 90%

result.other_findings: Considerable increase in clinical oncology workload with evidence of stress on the system.

result.setting: Banstead Primary Care Network, NHS Surrey Heartlands
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Several cases of inadvertent unopposed oestrogen exposure identified, due to prescribing, dispensing and patient understanding factors (no figures given)

result.intervention: Proposed EMIS IT changes (awaited), pharmacist education, alert stickers at dispensing, patient education and a short video for clinicians
result.other_findings: Re-audit results awaited; many flash points hard to detect or measure.

result.setting: Municipal hospital in Moscow, clinical health workers
result.standard: WHO hand hygiene guidelines

cycle1.result: Total hand hygiene compliance 52.3%

result.intervention: Action plan with monthly re-audits and feedback

cycle2.result: Total compliance 83.3% (p < 0.05); overall compliance 75% across 2,732 moments June to September

result.other_findings: Compliance highest among nurses (79.6%) and lowest among ancillary staff (69.7%); better adherence to before-moments than after-moments.

result.setting: Interventional radiology, The Christie NHS Foundation Trust (fluoroscopic and combined endoscopic procedures)
result.standard: 14 standards from the revised departmental sedation protocol based on national guidelines; BIS target 80-85

cycle1.result: Re-audit: three sedation standards missed; 84% had light or moderate sedation (BIS 70-89); no reversal, airway management or hypoxaemia

result.intervention: Revised sedation protocol with BIS-guided nurse titration of sedo-analgesia
result.other_findings: Only the re-audit data are reported; mean midazolam 3.99 mg and fentanyl 92.3 μg.

result.setting: High-volume general surgical unit, Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals Trust
result.standard: Documentation of five key areas: diagnosis, disease management, objective assessments, discharge planning and logistics

cycle1.result: VTE prophylaxis missing in 95.6%; current issues missing in 88.9%; pain scores missing in 46.7%; bowel function missing in 62.2%; fluid balance missing in 95.6%

cycle2.result: Most variables documented in all proformas; VTE prophylaxis and fluid balance documented in 95%

result.other_findings: Staff survey preceded the audit.

result.setting: Emergency department, Hunter New England, NSW Health
result.standard: Evidence-based work-up for psychiatric presentations

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Tool to standardise emergency assessment of psychiatric patients, with 2 months' implementation

cycle2.result: Stay time decreased by over 10% (p = .067); recommended work-up increased by almost 15%; triage change p = .0004

result.other_findings: Staff survey could not be assessed.

result.setting: Four GP surgeries in the North West (Paxton Medical Group)
result.standard: Standards extrapolated from current testosterone guidance

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Initiation and prescribing met all standards to 100%

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: All surgical specialties, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National SSI data

cycle1.result: 138 SSIs (14.5%) overall; general surgery 45/249 (18.1%)

result.intervention: Perioperative seven-point SSI reduction checklist in elective surgical theatres

cycle2.result: Elective general surgery SSI rate 1%; checklist completion 47%

result.other_findings: 38 additional SSIs (22.46% of SSIs) found only by telephone follow-up; the one SSI at re-audit had no completed checklist.

result.setting: Tertiary care hospital (De Soysa Hospital for Women, Colombo)
result.standard: Evidence-based practices for induction of labour

cycle1.result: Indications documented 59%; informed consent 2%; pre-induction assessment 30.8%; Foley catheter use 39%; caesarean section 22.3%

result.intervention: Provider training, unit protocols, patient safety checklists and patient information leaflets

cycle2.result: Indications documented 90%; informed consent 91%; pre-induction assessment 100%; Foley catheter use 68%; caesarean section 35.4%

result.other_findings: Initiative ran January 2019 to December 2022; caesarean rate rose, possibly due to staff shortages, drug availability and obesity; neonatal outcomes improved.

result.setting: UK cancer centres, RCR national re-audit (53/59 centres)
result.standard: Standards from national and international guidelines (casemix, dosimetry, minimum case numbers >25 per year)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: 25 centres performing brachytherapy; 79% (LDR) and 56% (HDR) of centres treated >25 cases per year; 43% (6/14 LDR) and 31% (5/16 HDR) of oncologists performed >25 procedures; all centres performing post-LDR implant dosimetry

result.other_findings: Overall brachytherapy numbers fell since 2012 while departmental skill mix increased.

result.setting: Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies Equine Hospital, University of Edinburgh
result.standard: National standards for checklist section completion

cycle1.result: Subsection completion 9% to 89%, median 64%

result.intervention: Checklist redesign with end users, education scheme, regular email reminders, senior champions, and policy to upload checklists to the medical record
result.other_findings: Veterinary equine hospital; sign-out section most likely to be incomplete.

result.setting: Primary elective surgical site, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean confidence recognising 2.94 and managing 2.62; prior training 49.1%; SCOOP protocol awareness 13.2%

cycle2.result: Mean confidence recognising 3.22 and managing 2.83; prior training 66%; SCOOP protocol awareness 66.7%

result.other_findings: Staff expressed demand for further teaching.

result.setting: Inpatient unit, Florence Nightingale Hospice, Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 74% hospital referrals (30% from ED); 54% non-malignant; average length of stay 4.7 days; 82% died, 18% discharged

result.other_findings: A re-audit in March 2025 confirmed the trends persisted; 75% of ED referrals died within 72 hours.

result.setting: ENT and audiology, Colchester Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean diagnosis to first ENT review 439.4 days; diagnosis to MRI 617.8 days

result.intervention: New streamlined protocol for managing permanent childhood hearing impairment

cycle2.result: Mean diagnosis to first ENT review 188.1 days; diagnosis to MRI 58.5 days

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: NABCOP fitness assessment in older breast cancer patients
result.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital breast service
result.standard: NABCOP fitness assessment form completion for patients over 70

cycle1.result: Form compliance 37%; AMTS documented in 11.9%

result.intervention: Form modified: AMTS optional, Age Gap Decision Tool outcomes added, tick-box for fitness for surgery
result.other_findings: Frailty scores strongly associated with treatment decisions; mean age 77 for surgery vs 84 for conservative management.

result.setting: Acute Medical Unit and Medical Same Day Emergency Care, Whiston Hospital, Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Clear clinical indication for coagulation screen requests; aim to reduce unnecessary coagulation screens by 90% within 12 months

cycle1.result: 34%-39% of coagulation screens were inappropriate across AMU areas; one-third of requests lacked a clear clinical indication

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: revised triage order sets, condition-specific electronic order sets, and a digital decision prompt requiring clinicians to confirm test indication

cycle2.result: Inappropriate testing reduced to 20% in mSDEC, 10% in AMU 1B and 15% in AMU 1C

result.other_findings: Projected annual reduction of 44 000 tests, saving £130 000, 367 staff hours and 3.6 tonnes CO2e; the 90% reduction aim was not stated as met.

result.setting: Tertiary university hospital (Fondazione Policlinico Tor Vergata), monocentric prospective cohort
result.standard: Four RESECT surgical quality indicators: detrusor muscle sampling, completeness of resection, accuracy of operative documentation, and single immediate intravesical chemotherapy

cycle1.result: Detrusor muscle presence 61.9% in the pre-audit phase; 70.7% during the prospective audit phase (128 patients across all phases, March 2023 to June 2025)

result.intervention: Participation in the RESECT audit and feedback programme

cycle2.result: Detrusor muscle presence 85.9% in the post-audit phase

result.other_findings: Improvements in quality indicators were sustained after programme completion but did not yield a detectable reduction in recurrence.

result.setting: District General Hospital pathology unit, single centre
result.standard: Sample adequacy of fine-needle aspiration cytology in non-thyroid head and neck masses

cycle1.result: 134 of 207 (64.7%) samples adequate (dry slides only)

result.intervention: From 2017, samples prepared as both dry slides and liquid cytology
result.other_findings: All four clinicians achieved higher adequacy rates in the re-audit cycle.

result.setting: Tertiary Neonatal Intensive Care and Special Care Nursery, Centenary Hospital for Women and Children, Canberra
result.standard: Recommended ISOAP (Introduction, Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) format for nursing handover reports

cycle1.result: 2% adherence to ISOAP format

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles (paper-based then digital health records): neonatal-specific ISOAP templates, education sessions, peer mentorship, visual reminders and ongoing staff support

cycle2.result: Adherence 78% by January 2022 and 100% by March 2022; after DHR transition adherence improved from 65% in May 2023 to 92% by July 2023

result.other_findings: Staff reported improved clarity, communication, reduced time for clinical reviews and greater satisfaction.

result.setting: Paediatric Department, Birmingham Dental Hospital, Birmingham Community Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Recording of vaccination status of new patients in clinical notes

cycle1.result: 0% adherence to recording vaccination status

result.intervention: Dissemination of results, prompts added to clinical templates and increased staff awareness
result.other_findings: Of records with vaccination information, 13% of children were not up to date with vaccinations.

result.topic: SABA overuse and MART in asthma
result.setting: Wickham Surgery, general practice, Fareham
result.standard: Guidelines recommending MART for patients aged 12 or over; target >50% of 12-18-year-olds issued 3 or more salbutamol inhalers in a year transitioned to MART by May 2025

cycle1.result: 22 patients identified; eight already on MART

result.intervention: Structured face-to-face consultations, adolescent-friendly education tool, personalised asthma action plans and MART initiation where appropriate

cycle2.result: 23 patients identified, 10 (43%) on MART; >50% target not reached

result.other_findings: 10 patients attended consultations, leading to five further MART initiations; some apparent overuse reflected duplicate inhalers for school or sports.

result.topic: SABA overuse and MART in asthma
result.setting: The Willows Medical Practice, general practice, Chigwell, Essex
result.standard: NICE and BTS/SIGN asthma guidelines recommending AIR and MART for patients over-relying on SABA

cycle1.result: 94 patients issued 2 or more SABA inhalers in 12 months; 72 (76.6%) contacted; 37 (51.4%) overused SABA 3 or more times per week

result.intervention: Asthma reviews, inhaler technique assessment and initiation of AIR/MART therapy where appropriate

cycle2.result: 35 patients identified (-62.8%); 23 (65.7%) contacted; 18 (78.3%) reported SABA overuse (overuse count down from 37 to 18, -51.4%)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Vascular surgery department, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, single centre
result.standard: Documentation standards derived from Royal College of Surgeons guidance

cycle1.result: Documentation incomplete across all four safety-critical fields; indication for surgery documented in 43.2%

result.intervention: Standardised procedure-specific operative note templates developed collaboratively and introduced at a departmental governance meeting

cycle2.result: Indication for surgery improved to 79.5% (OR 5.07, 95% CI 2.38-10.80); significant improvement in two of four domains

result.other_findings: Estimated blood loss and postoperative plan recording did not improve significantly.

result.topic: Admission glucose and ketone testing in diabetes
result.setting: Department of Acute and General Medicine, St James's Hospital, Dublin; admissions via emergency department
result.standard: JBDS-IP and ADA recommendations for glucose and ketone testing in all hospitalised diabetic patients

cycle1.result: Glucose measured on admission in 83% and ketones in 58%

result.other_findings: Four patients (4%) with neither test developed metabolic acidosis; education, workflow changes and re-audit are planned.

result.setting: District general hospital (Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust), radiology and emergency departments
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists 2024 major trauma guidance: six minimum data elements for WBCT requests and RCR WBCT criteria

cycle1.result: Mechanism of injury 74%, primary survey 94%, haemodynamic status 7%, preceding investigations 5%, past medical history 13%, trauma team leader contact 0%; 57% of requests met RCR WBCT criteria

result.intervention: Educational feedback to radiology and emergency medicine staff, RCR-derived electronic request proforma embedded in CareFlow EPR, and real-time radiologist feedback

cycle2.result: Mechanism of injury 100%; past medical history 18% (p = 0.329); preceding investigations 4% (p = 1.000); requests meeting RCR WBCT criteria 96%

result.other_findings: Preceding investigations and past medical history documentation remained low after intervention.

result.topic: Lipid management after acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: District general hospital (Wiltshire Cardiac Centre, Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Swindon)
result.standard: Guideline-based post-ACS lipid management: inpatient lipid profile, inpatient lipid-lowering therapy management and outpatient repeat lipid profile

cycle1.result: Baseline full lipid profile testing 10%; appropriate LLT management 65%; post-discharge repeat testing 37%

result.intervention: Structured intervention including updated blood testing panels, education and reference resources

cycle2.result: Full lipid profile testing 75%; appropriate LLT management 78%; post-discharge repeat testing 63%

result.other_findings: At one year post-ACS, 35% of patients remained subtherapeutic but medication changes were rare.

result.topic: Late GI toxicity after prostate radiotherapy
result.setting: Department of Clinical Oncology, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, academic centre
result.standard: National Prostate Cancer Audit severe late GI toxicity rate after EBRT; national average 10%

cycle1.result: Severe late GI toxicity confirmed in 16% (follow-up available for 281/290, 96.8%)

result.intervention: Protocol changes in 2020-2021: tighter rectal dose constraints, enema use, updated verification pathway and reduced CTV-PTV margins

cycle2.result: NPCA reported severe late GI toxicity reduced to 7.5%

result.other_findings: Higher rectal mean dose was associated with severe late GI toxicity (p=0.043); 36% of toxic cases had rectal diameters of 4.5 cm or more.

result.setting: Specialist cancer hospital (Royal Marsden Hospital, London)
result.standard: Palliative care unit recommendations for morphine prescribing

cycle1.result: Weaknesses included lack of breakthrough doses, prn oral morphine without regular oral morphine, and no guideline reference to co-prescription of aperients, antiemetics and night sedation

result.intervention: Education programme targeting the identified deficiencies

cycle2.result: Some improvement in prescribing practice (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: Persistent problems showed the need for an ongoing hospital-wide education programme.

result.topic: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
result.setting: Wessex regional radiology audit (multi-hospital)
result.standard: 100% demonstration and 100% diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma on barium enema performed in the 12 months before histological diagnosis

cycle1.result: Carcinoma demonstration rate 97%; reporting rate 85% (471 of 557 enema reports)

result.other_findings: Non-reporting due to failure to demonstrate (18 cases, 3%), failure to perceive (23, 4%) and failure to analyse a perceived lesion (45, 8%).

result.setting: All 147 Leicestershire general practices, audit led by a medical audit advisory group
result.standard: Agreed criteria for appropriate use of vitamin B12 injections

cycle1.result: Appropriate use 62%; 521 patients inappropriately receiving B12; correct frequency 58%; full pernicious anaemia diagnostic criteria established in 27%

result.intervention: Central analysis and feedback of anonymous aggregated data by the medical audit advisory group

cycle2.result: Appropriate use 72%; 352 inappropriately receiving B12 (32% reduction); correct frequency 72%; diagnostic criteria established in 28%

result.other_findings: 264 GPs (55%) completed both phases; only 10 of 37 singlehanded practices completed the audit.

result.setting: Institute of Biochemistry, Glasgow Royal Infirmary; GP and satellite hospital services
result.standard: Recommendations from an earlier laboratory turnaround time study

cycle1.result: GP reports reaching destination within one and two days: 13% and 68%; satellite hospital 25% and 60%; median total turnaround 50 hours (GP) and 69 hours (satellite)

result.intervention: Posting results directly from the laboratory, then a twice-daily courier service

cycle2.result: Within one and two days: GP 29% and 82%, satellite 78% and 82%; courier cut median turnaround to nine hours (GP) and 18 hours (satellite)

result.other_findings: Analytically old samples arriving the day after collection fell from 25% to 3%.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Written infection control guidelines such as Hospital Infection Society model guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on the audit cycle in infection control; recommends risk-adjusted nosocomial infection rates via repeated prevalence surveys.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Agreed antibiotic policy

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on choosing audit topics and standards for antibiotic use.

result.setting: Inpatients (Research Unit, Royal College of Physicians, London)
result.standard: Local guidelines in accordance with British Society for Haematology recommendations

cycle1.result: Confirmatory investigations in 93% (DVT) and 79% (PE); baseline coagulation screen 52%, platelets 95%, LFT 70%, renal 87%; 33% of APTT and 58% of INR subtherapeutic; 72% of 62 discharged with therapeutic INR; 74% had anticoagulant clinic appointments

result.other_findings: 37% stopped heparin without an INR that day or with INR under 2; only 6 of 25 (24%) with delayed clinic appointments had interim INR checks.

result.setting: Two dermatology units (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Criteria set of 18 questions devised by 66 dermatologists

cycle1.result: Centre B 60% satisfactory completion of the criteria set

result.intervention: Policy decisions and protocols established at centre B only; no changes at centre A

cycle2.result: Centre B 74% satisfactory completion (P < 0.0001); no improvement at centre A

result.other_findings: Doctors in training grades performed best and responded most to policy changes.

result.topic: Electronic study guide for problem-based learning
result.setting: Medical Education Unit, University of Liverpool
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes an electronic study guide for oncology using an educational audit loop; not a clinical audit.

result.topic: Cleft lip and palate service standards
result.setting: Surgical practices in England and Wales (Royal College of Surgeons Surgical Audit and Epidemiology Unit)
result.standard: Recommended minimum standards of care for cleft lip and palate produced by a multidisciplinary steering group

cycle1.result: Widespread involvement of low-volume operators, incomplete networks of associated professionals and non-standardised record keeping

result.other_findings: Further investigation planned to validate standards and provide a baseline for future audit cycles.

result.topic: Asthma guideline implementation and patient education
result.setting: Tertiary hospital (John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle, NSW)
result.standard: National asthma management guidelines

cycle1.result: Satisfactory emergency assessment and treatment but poor compliance with patient education aspects of the asthma management plan

result.intervention: Asthma education and management service developed

cycle2.result: Improvements in asthma control and management skills for attenders and reduced re-admission rates for referred patients (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: Non-attenders to the service remain a target; an area Asthma Health Outcomes Council was formed.

result.setting: Scotland: 132 consultant gynaecologists surveyed and casenote review in 12 representative hospitals
result.standard: 15 evidence-based criteria for good quality care in female laparoscopic sterilisation

cycle1.result: 6% of women under 25; over 85% documented counselling on failure and permanency; 88% by consultant or senior registrar; only 22% mentioned vasectomy discussion; 30% of gynaecologists provided local leaflets; day-case use 19% to 99%

result.other_findings: Questionnaire response rate 94%; four methods of tubal occlusion in use; re-audit planned after dissemination.

result.setting: Victoria Infirmary NHS Trust, Glasgow
result.standard: Agreed written protocols for prophylactic antimicrobials and parenteral co-amoxiclav and metronidazole

cycle1.result: 65% of courses appropriate; 16% of courses too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 30%

result.intervention: Agreed protocols distributed and explained to each resident; automatic stopping system

cycle2.result: 72% of 226 courses appropriate; 9% too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 68% and use 33% lower

result.other_findings: 82% of doses appropriate when written in the once-only Kardex section versus 51% in the general part; inappropriate choice rose to 19% owing to one-cephalosporin rule.

result.setting: Hospitals in South Thames (East) Region
result.standard: Standards set by the Regional Radiology Audit Committee at the end of the first cycle

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Standards set after the first cycle

cycle2.result: No significant difference in accuracy or false negative and false positive rates between screening and non-screening units; non-screening units more likely to issue equivocal reports (P = 0.000001)

result.other_findings: Recommends issuing an audit grade with reports and double reporting of equivocal images.

result.setting: Department of Radiology, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff
result.standard: Removal of antiscatter grid during filling phase of barium enemas

cycle1.result: Grid removed in 6 of 100 examinations

result.intervention: Data presented at local audit meeting; departmental policy changed to recommend routine grid removal

cycle2.result: Grid removed in 96 of 100 enemas; 46.5% dose reduction for filling phase (95% CI 38-61%)

result.other_findings: None of 22 trainee radiologists routinely removed the grid at baseline; further re-audit showed sustained practice.

result.setting: Department of General Practice, University of Glasgow; final year GP attachment
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Only two students completed the audit cycle in 4 weeks; 90.6% understood audit better and 78% of tutors found teaching audit valuable.

result.setting: Urology department, district general hospital (Torbay Hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Blood loss equivalent to Hb fall of 10-15 g/L (8-11%); overall transfusion rate 10.8%

cycle2.result: Overall transfusion rate 8.2%; 4.4% to 1% in smaller resections

result.other_findings: Resected weight was the main determinant of blood loss; regional anaesthesia associated with less blood loss.

result.setting: Nine maxillofacial units, prospective multicentre audit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 73 attended at 6 and 12 weeks; 41 had symptoms at 12 weeks; 50-85% correlation between clinician and external auditor radiographic findings

result.other_findings: Displaced fractures and dislocations had suboptimal outcome in nearly 30%; no gold standard exists to close the loop.

result.setting: Nuclear medicine departments in South Thames Regional Health Authority
result.standard: Guidelines set for ventilation-perfusion, bone, liver, thyroid and renal DMSA imaging

cycle1.result: Organisational audits in 10 departments found lack of facilities and space; high patient satisfaction in nine departments

result.other_findings: A programme of re-audit has commenced.

result.topic: Care of newly diagnosed childhood diabetes
result.setting: Eight districts of East Anglia, paediatric diabetes services
result.standard: Agreed indicators of good practice

cycle1.result: Good education on injection, blood testing and diet; variable home visits; poor school contact and support group introduction; only three units had adolescent joint clinics; 75% questionnaire return

result.intervention: Peer review and implementation of an action plan

cycle2.result: Modest improvements in problem areas (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: Confidence was best with a dedicated paediatric specialist nurse and adequate cover.

result.setting: District General Hospital (Glan Clwyd), all anaesthetic machines
result.standard: Extended checklist based on Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland checklist

cycle1.result: 236 faults found by 24 tests (range 1.1-64%); 65 (27.5%) day to day, 171 (72.5%) non-recurring

cycle2.result: Faults on 59 occasions by 20 tests (range 1.0-11.6%); 16 (27%) day to day, 43 (73%) non-recurring

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Haematology, consultant haematologists (Guy's Hospital, London)
result.standard: Guidelines on management of platelet refractoriness produced by a working group

cycle1.result: Clinicians differed on the definition of platelet refractoriness; non-immune causes considered less important

result.intervention: Guidelines on recommended practice produced and implemented

cycle2.result: More patients receiving HLA-compatible platelets tested for HLA antibodies; mean 50.9% reduction in HLA-compatible platelet use

result.other_findings: No apparent increase in haemorrhagic complications.

result.setting: Neonatal unit, City Hospital, Nottingham
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Three serious deteriorations in transit

result.intervention: Nine-person nursing transport team formed, improved training and upgraded monitoring

cycle2.result: Improved temperature and pH transport scores on completion; no serious deteriorations in transit

result.other_findings: Stabilisation before transfer took longer in 1994-95.

result.setting: District general hospital (Inverclyde Royal NHS Trust), main clinical specialties
result.standard: SIGN guideline on prevention of deep vein thrombosis; target 90% of at-risk patients prescribed prophylaxis

cycle1.result: 72.8% (n = 163) prescribed prophylaxis; 54% (n = 122) prescribed correct prophylaxis

result.intervention: Local prevention protocols developed or upgraded in line with SIGN guideline; seconded clinician coordinated implementation
result.other_findings: Low-cost initiative of approximately 3,800 pounds.

result.setting: Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: Local protocol for magnesium sulphate in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia

cycle1.result: Problems with time to therapeutic levels and clinical monitoring of magnesium levels

result.intervention: Protocol changes and introduction of an administration and monitoring chart

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in monitoring and adequacy of prophylaxis (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: OPAT documentation and bed days saved
result.setting: Acute Care at Home OPAT service, Cornwall Foundation Trust (referrals from primary care and RCHT)
result.standard: 100% of patients receiving IV antibiotics with an indication under OPAT; 100% with dose, frequency and administration method documented; 100% with an OPAT acceptance date

cycle1.result: 343 bed days saved and 302 OPAT treatment days; course lengths within range of NORS 2015-2020 data (compliance with documentation standards not reported)

result.other_findings: Ceftriaxone was the most prescribed antibiotic (27 patients); re-audit with a longer data collection period recommended.

result.setting: Tertiary burns and plastic surgery department
result.standard: Updated local plastic surgery infection guidelines

cycle1.result: Prescriber compliance with the guideline 50%

result.intervention: Guideline updated using local resistance data, departmental teaching, appropriate antibiotics made available in burns and plastics theatres, and all guidelines combined into one document

cycle2.result: Prescriber compliance 71% after three intervention cycles

result.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav and clindamycin were the most common non-compliant prescriptions, reflecting historical usage.

result.topic: Gentamicin level timing and dose administration
result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, NHS Lothian
result.standard: Gentamicin guidelines on level sampling window and dosing interval

cycle1.result: 23/31 (74%) levels taken within the recommended window; 23/31 (74%) second doses on time

result.intervention: Gentamicin labels placed in each AMU bay to raise staff awareness

cycle2.result: 31/40 (78%) levels within the window; 30/40 (75%) subsequent doses at the right interval

result.other_findings: Most delayed second doses were in patients whose first dose was given in the emergency department before AMU admission.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis review in recurrent UTI
result.setting: Three GP practices, Bridgend Locality, Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board; later Bridgend locality-wide
result.standard: NICE NG15 and NG112: clinical review within 6 months for patients on antibiotic prophylaxis for recurrent UTI

cycle1.result: Of 160 on prophylaxis for >6 months, 24% had a review within 6 months; 39% on prophylaxis >3 years; 82.5% continued on a potentially ineffective antibiotic after resistant MSU

result.intervention: Audit feedback to practices, co-designed action plan to review patients, pharmacist support; rolled out through Welsh GMS contract QI basket

cycle2.dates: Re-audit 6 months after review (Welsh GMS 2019/20, live until September 2022)
cycle2.result: 334 (77.5%) of 431 reviewed; 171 (51%) of those reviewed stopped; 40% locality reduction in rUTI prophylaxis

result.other_findings: 54.7% had at least one acute UTI while on prophylaxis; estimated 2223 fewer antibiotic prescriptions per year.

result.setting: Medical specialties, RCHT (Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE guidance to stop antibiotics at day 5 for CAP/HAP if clinically stable

cycle1.result: 10 (45%) received 5 or 6 days; 12 (55%) received 7 to 10 days despite meeting stop criteria; mean 6.5 and median 6.3 days

result.other_findings: Education and an EPMA day-5 alert are proposed; re-audit with a larger sample recommended.

result.topic: Early intervention in psychosis waiting times
result.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis team, Liverpool
result.standard: NICE access and waiting time standard: 60% of people with first episode psychosis treated with an approved care package within two weeks of referral

cycle1.result: Average referral pathway time 9.8 days

result.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (details not reported)

cycle2.result: Average pathway time 22.5 days, exceeding the NICE standard

result.other_findings: Main delays were referral assessment, care coordinator allocation and prescriber review, related to COVID-19 and a 50% rise in FEP patients.

result.setting: Behavioural Sciences Institute, Al Ain Hospital, inpatient and outpatient services
result.standard: Local Al Ain Hospital guidelines and Royal College of Psychiatrists ECT standards

cycle1.result: 16 (53%) had no capacity documentation on consent papers; 4 of 8 lacking capacity had reasons documented; 20 (67%) had no documented risk-benefit discussion

result.other_findings: Staff training and a risk-benefit section on the ECT consent form are proposed, with re-audit after one year.

result.setting: Community Mental Health Team, St Davnet's Hospital, Monaghan
result.standard: British Association for Psychopharmacology guidelines for metabolic syndrome monitoring

cycle1.result: 39.6% had MetS monitoring charts; 29.2% completed; BP, lipids and glucose documented in 31.3%; BMI/girth 29.2%

result.intervention: Psychoeducation for nursing staff on monitoring and documentation guidelines

cycle2.result: MetS charts 100% completed; glucose 95.7%; blood pressure 91.3%; BMI/girth and lipids 87%

result.other_findings: Colour-coded stickers and a MetS clinic proposed to sustain improvement.

result.setting: Inpatient adult intellectual disability assessment and treatment unit, New Craig's Psychiatric Hospital, Inverness
result.standard: NHS Highland Seclusion Policy

cycle1.result: Missing records included anxiolytic use before seclusion, respiration rate and appearance at 15-minute checks, plans to end seclusion at 2 hours, consultant informed at 4 hours, and Datix submission

result.other_findings: Results shared via working group, teaching and governance forum; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Prolactin monitoring on antipsychotics in children
result.setting: Child psychiatry outpatient clinic, Al Ain Hospital
result.standard: NICE CG155: prolactin at baseline, 12 weeks and every six months in children on antipsychotics

cycle1.result: No baseline prolactin measured; 10 (7%) checked at 12 weeks; none checked six-monthly

result.other_findings: Local guidance, staff training and electronic monitoring alerts recommended, with re-audit after one year.

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Samphire ward, acute inpatient psychiatric facility (Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: NSFT Physical Healthcare Policy (C84): 100% baseline bloods, physical examination and ECG within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Physical examination 34.5%; ECG 53%; bloods 68% (correct bloods 4.5%); all three components 0%

result.intervention: A3 visual aid placed on the ward

cycle2.result: Physical examination 47%; ECG 61%; bloods 71% (correct bloods 33%); all three components 33%

result.other_findings: Ward doctors adhered to the standard significantly more than duty doctors.

result.topic: Depression screening in chronic physical illness
result.setting: Acute medical services, North Middlesex University Hospital
result.standard: NICE clinical guideline 91

cycle1.result: 85% with past depression reported current symptoms; 48% with chronic physical condition reported low mood or anhedonia

result.intervention: Screening questions added to the medical clerking proforma, new referral pathway with liaison psychiatry, and departmental teaching on CG91

cycle2.result: Clinician completion of screening questions 65%; 44% with chronic physical problems reported depressive symptoms; 84% of identified patients had a planned referral

result.other_findings: not reported

result.standard: not reported

result.standard: not reported

result.setting: Acute stroke admissions
result.standard: not reported

result.setting: Three adult inpatient mental health sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: not reported

result.setting: Mental health services across the London and South region (Cygnet Health Care)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported
