cycle2.result: 34 RT events in 17 patients; de-escalation 62%; oral medication offered first 71%; physical monitoring fully completed 50%

result.other_findings: IMRT events fell by 49%; 119 inpatient records were reviewed in 2019.

result.setting: Acute mixed inpatient psychiatry unit, south Manchester, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local GMMH medication chart policy standards, plus capacity assessment and consent to treatment forms

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment form 22 (71%); consent to treatment form 16 (52%); route recorded in 40% of depot prescriptions; regular medications date of administration 84%, signature 29%; allergy reaction recorded in 6/21 (29%)

result.other_findings: PRN administration details were 100% complete; patient identifiers were not maintained beyond page 1. Re-audit planned in 3-6 months.

result.setting: Ardenleigh blended women's secure unit, Birmingham
result.standard: Locally set standard: pregnancy testing within one month of admission (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Only 54% of women with unknown pregnancy status screened within one month of admission; 43% in under-25s and 0% in those aged 36-45

result.intervention: Planned: add pregnancy testing to the admission checklist
result.other_findings: Unscreened women were mostly admitted from other hospitals or medium secure units, and 2 admitted from prison were not tested; 92% of tests were urine hCG and none were positive. Re-audit recommended 6 months after checklist introduction.

result.topic: Depression pathway compliance in children and young people
result.setting: 26 community children and young people's teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust depression pathway derived from NICE QS48, CG28 and NG134 (comprehensive assessment, parent/carer mental health assessment, psychological therapy first line in mild depression)

cycle1.result: ICD-10 diagnosis recorded in 19%; RCADS symptom tracking under 40%; identification or referral to other pathways for mild depression in 16-18 age group 0%; 29% of teams did not respond

result.intervention: Action plan following the initial audit (details not reported)

cycle2.result: Over 90% compliance for comorbidity, social and educational context; 100% offered psychological interventions; ICD-10 diagnosis 30%; RCADS tracking over 50%; identification and referral for mild depression in 16-18s 82% and 100%; only 1/26 teams (4%) did not respond

result.other_findings: Weekly monitoring of medication side effects in the first 4 weeks (43%) and referral of parents/carers to mental health services (40%) remained poor.

result.topic: Pregnancy and contraception assessment on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Mixed-sex acute adult inpatient psychiatry ward, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists and local guidelines: all female inpatients asked about sexual health within seven days of admission

cycle1.result: 57% asked about contraception; possibility of pregnancy explored in less than half

result.intervention: Planned: discussion at clinical governance meeting for recommendations
result.other_findings: Minimal variation by age group (18-26, 27-35, 36-45). Re-audit planned.

result.setting: Addictions service, Plummer Court, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: NICE: all patients completing alcohol detoxification should be considered for acamprosate or oral naltrexone

cycle1.result: Anti-craving medication considered in 47%; acamprosate offered in all but one case; accepted in all but one case where offered

result.intervention: Monthly follow-up with addictions services for six months, template letter to GPs requesting acamprosate prescription, audit presented to medical team and treatment pathway amended to specify medical role at initial appointment
result.other_findings: Follow-up of prescriptions was unclear and several GPs declined to prescribe acamprosate citing an outdated local policy. Re-audit planned in six months.

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Mill Lodge Tier 4 CAMHS inpatient unit, York
result.standard: Tier 4 CAMHS service specification standard 2.6.3: initial assessment including physical examination within 24 hours of admission (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Among patients who did not refuse, within 24 hours: physical examination 85%, bloods 82%, ECG 84%; during admission bloods and ECG 100%, physical examination 90%

result.other_findings: No reason documented for missing procedures in several patients (3 examinations, 2 bloods, 3 ECGs); one blood test delayed by lack of tubes. Re-audit planned in twelve months.

result.setting: Child and Family Clinic, tier 3 outpatient CAMHS, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: Belfast Trust CAMHS Antipsychotic Medication Monitoring Schedule (2015), based on CAMESA, NICE CG185, CG155 and Maudsley guidelines

cycle1.result: Baseline bloods (or declined) 92%; baseline ECG (or declined) 75%; complete monitoring bloods 33%; physical health parameters complete 42%; monitoring schedule present and current 42% (0% on PARIS)

result.intervention: Standardised recording of monitoring using PARIS clinic letters and the schedule at the front of clinical notes; baseline ECG made mandatory

cycle2.result: Baseline bloods (or declined) 89%; baseline ECG (or declined) 67%; complete monitoring bloods 44%; parameters complete 56%; schedule present and current 38%, present but not current 50% (0% on PARIS)

result.other_findings: Small re-audit numbers limit interpretation; further recommendations are an initiation checklist, central bloods diary and a co-produced care-pathway booklet.

result.setting: ECT clinic, Bolton Directorate, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: WHO surgical safety checklist modified for ECT including NPSA advice, per ECT accreditation service standards (target 100% completion)

cycle1.result: 19/20 (95%) completed; 5/20 (25%) not signed; 75% complete and valid; checklists present in all case notes

result.other_findings: A repeat audit was recommended.

result.topic: Appropriateness of referrals to community mental health team
result.setting: Oxford City and NE Oxon Adult Mental Health Team
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 21% of referrals inappropriate

result.intervention: Team remodelled in January 2020 into separate assessment and treatment functions

cycle2.result: 19.5% (546/2803) of referrals inappropriate; 14.7% (97/658) pre-COVID-19 vs 20.9% (449/2145) during the pandemic; 32.9% returned to GP after a single assessment

result.other_findings: Students made up 26% of referrals, with more ADHD (17.7% vs 3%) and neurodevelopmental referrals than non-students. Automated logging of referral outcomes is planned.

result.setting: Community forensic supported accommodation, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust medicines reconciliation guidance: 100% concordance between mental health and general practice records for medication and allergies

cycle1.result: Allergy status discrepancy in 2 patients (25%); medication discrepancy in 2 patients (25%), both vitamin D omitted from mental health records

result.other_findings: Allergies were documented in ward discharge summaries but not in GP records; primary care asked to update. Re-audits every four months planned.

result.topic: Eating disorder referrals from primary care
result.setting: Manchester Foundation Trust Community Eating Disorders Service, Greater Manchester
result.standard: NICE: children and young people with suspected eating disorders referred immediately and directly to specialist services at first presentation

cycle1.result: 35% of referrals made correctly; 43.5% not initially made to MFT-CEDS; 58% made immediately; North and South Manchester 10% and 8% correct

result.intervention: Recommended: information document and video, GP referral template and interviews with GPs
result.other_findings: Most of the 10 GP survey respondents did not know the referral guidelines or feel confident identifying eating disorders. Re-audit planned after 6 months.

result.topic: Psychosocial assessment after self-harm in children
result.setting: Service for Adolescents and Families in Enfield, for paediatric inpatients at North Middlesex and Barnet hospitals, London
result.standard: NICE self-harm quality standard QS34: comprehensive psychosocial assessment, assessment within 24 hours if high risk, collaborative risk management plan and follow-up

cycle1.result: 100% had comprehensive psychosocial assessment; 93% seen within 24 hours of referral; 97% documented risk assessment; 92% had 7-day follow-up review

result.intervention: Assessment protocol and safety plan, daily liaison with hospitals, paediatric nurses trained in the Time to Talk programme and a full-time crisis liaison nurse employed
result.other_findings: Hospital referrals rose 141% from 2014/15 to 2018/19; 74% of presentations were girls and 87% involved self-harm, suicidal ideation or attempt. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, general hospital, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project target: handover time under 30 minutes within one month, with improved handover quality

cycle1.result: Average handover 44 minutes; 7 interruptions; key information available 69%; staff member allocated 80%; review date allocated 83%

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles of change ideas shaped by team human factors (limited number of changes, flexible handover system, extra administration taken on by medical staff); specific changes not detailed

cycle2.result: Average handover 30 minutes; 2 interruptions; key information available 92%; staff member allocated 95%; review date allocated 95%

result.other_findings: Average patients per handover unchanged at 15; burnout, understaffing and COVID-19 pressures were key human factors. Re-audit planned at 6 months and 1 year.

result.setting: West Glasgow CAMHS team, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: Junior MARSIPAN guidelines for content and physical measures in GP referrals of suspected eating disorders

cycle1.result: 73.1% of referrals recorded height and weight; mean referral to diagnosis 44.1 days

result.intervention: Duty clinicians screened referrals and prompted GPs for physical parameters, weekly board round meeting for new and existing patients, and weekly physical health monitoring clinic

cycle2.result: 82.1% recorded height and weight; 53.8% required prompting; written content unchanged (risk 46.2%, estimated onset 51.3%, body image 56.4%); mean referral to diagnosis 34.2 days

result.other_findings: Staff stress scores (MHPSS) stayed high; the board round received positive feedback from 10 staff. A GP referral proforma was recommended.

result.topic: Physical health information in discharge summaries
result.setting: Sheffield Home Treatment Team, Sheffield Health and Social Care
result.standard: Criteria and standards for physical health review information in discharge summaries, derived from a team questionnaire

cycle1.result: Only 49% of service users with physical health reviews had any information provided on discharge; content varied and was inconsistent

result.intervention: Proposed solution to be implemented (not described)
result.other_findings: There was no official system to ensure physical health review results were communicated to GPs. Re-audit planned.

result.topic: STOMP psychotropic medication review in learning disability
result.setting: CAMHS Learning Disability Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHS England STOMP pledge and local Trust guidelines for antipsychotic physical health monitoring

cycle1.result: 66 (62%) prescribed medication and eligible for STOMP review; 35% undergoing reduction plan, 35% reduction not deemed suitable, 30% no review or reduction plan; 64 had a behavioural support plan

result.intervention: Recommendations made in the report (not detailed)
result.other_findings: 60% of those on psychotropics were on antipsychotics, 38% were on more than one psychotropic and about 80% had been on psychotropics for over 12 months. Re-audit planned in a year.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in COVID-19 patients
result.setting: Forensic secure inpatient services, Roseberry Park Hospital, Teesside
result.standard: TEWV 2019 'Risk assessment for Venous Thromboembolism (VTE)' policy (CLIN-0085-v1.2)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: VTE risk assessment and recording after a COVID-19 positive result was less than 100%

result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit following a scheduled quality improvement re-audit of VTE assessment; other results were in the poster only.

result.topic: Trainee confidence in acute physical health care
result.setting: Maudsley core psychiatry training programme, South London and the Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Likert-scale confidence and 'rustiness' ratings from 10 of 30 trainees (figures not given)

result.intervention: Monthly 10-minute 'Bite-Sized Medicine' teaching slot on acute physical health issues

cycle2.result: Confidence and rustiness improved significantly on Mann-Whitney U tests (p value truncated in abstract)

result.other_findings: Survey of trainee opinion with small samples; trainees found the sessions useful.

result.topic: Missing person rapid risk assessment completion
result.setting: General adult, older adult and learning disability wards, Royal Cornhill Hospital, NHS Grampian
result.standard: Missing Person Protocol Rapid Risk Assessment proforma completion, in line with the National Framework for Missing Persons

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Teaching on the RRA and weekly review of the RRA at MDT meetings

cycle2.result: 100% of notes contained the RRA proforma; average completion of all sections 87.5%; 21% improvement since 2017 and 14.5% improvement in section completion versus previous audit

result.other_findings: Brief Admission Details was poorly completed and no ward had completed the Return to Ward questionnaire; completion was worst in general adult and best in learning disability wards.

result.setting: Mixed sex inpatient psychiatric wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: Acute care group standard: patients with known risk to the opposite sex not admitted to mixed sex wards; comprehensive risk assessment on admission and escalation of risks to MDT

cycle1.result: Full risk assessment documented in 50%; historical risks 40%; admission clerking contained risk assessment in 70% and risks to others in 60%; 30% had risks to the opposite sex but none were escalated to the MDT

result.intervention: Recommended: specific guidance for documenting risk assessments and teaching for healthcare professionals
result.other_findings: Prompted by a serious incident on a mixed sex ward. Re-audit scheduled for March 2022.

result.topic: Mental Health Act consent to treatment documentation
result.setting: All inpatient wards, Park House Hospital, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust Consent to Treatment policy

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Interactive consent to treatment teaching for core trainees, presentation to the Trust MHA/MCA quality improvement group, and consultation with pharmacists and consultants on ward recording systems

cycle2.result: No ward had 100% capacity forms documented, kept in charts and uploaded; 7/9 wards 100% for completing T2/T3/S62 forms; 6/9 wards 100% for retaining them in charts; 78% uploaded to PARIS; 80% of medication charts matched T2/T3 forms

result.other_findings: Only 24% of trainees felt confident about consent to treatment and 32% checked forms before prescribing; 91% said teaching helped. Ward round proformas and monthly ward auditing were proposed.

result.topic: Anticholinergic burden recording in memory services
result.setting: West Leeds Memory Assessment Service, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Anticholinergic burden (ACB) score documented for patients referred to the memory assessment service

cycle1.result: No documented ACB scores at referral; calculated scores varied by tool, with the lowest suggesting 20.4% (n = 10) had a raised ACB score

result.intervention: Planned: standardised ACB tool for all new referrals and improved awareness across the memory pathway
result.other_findings: Amitriptyline was the commonest contributor to anticholinergic burden in all three scoring systems. Re-audit planned in 3 months.

result.setting: Mixed adult acute psychiatric inpatient ward, London, Barnet, Enfield and Haringey Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: Aim that every newly admitted unvaccinated patient has vaccination status documented and is offered the appropriate COVID-19 vaccine dose

cycle1.result: 33/41 not fully vaccinated or no record; only 6/33 offered the next dose and 3/33 received one

result.intervention: Early identification of unvaccinated patients on admission as a prompt to offer vaccination, with counselling and re-offer if refused

cycle2.result: Initial data: 5/10 unvaccinated patients offered vaccines in January

result.other_findings: 21/33 patients without a full set of vaccinations were BAME; second cycle data collection was incomplete.

result.topic: Admission blood tests in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Norbury House psychiatric intensive care unit, St George's Hospital, Stafford
result.standard: Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust guidelines on routine admission blood tests

cycle1.result: TFTs 71%, glucose 6%, prolactin 77%, calcium 94%; unnecessary tests requested in 88% of patients (23 tests in total)

result.intervention: Staff education programme on trust admission blood test guidelines

cycle2.result: 69% had the appropriate admission blood tests; TFTs 100%, glucose 69%, prolactin 100%, calcium 92%; unnecessary tests in 21% (3 tests in total)

result.other_findings: All mandatory tests rose or stayed at 100% except calcium. Further re-audit planned for spring 2022.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry, NHS Grampian
result.standard: MHRA guidance and Pregnancy Prevention Programme: Annual Risk Acknowledgement Form completed for women of childbearing potential on valproate

cycle1.result: Only one patient (3%) had an Annual Risk Acknowledgement Form completed; 97% in contact with psychiatry services

result.intervention: Teams contacted by telephone and email and encouraged to complete the documentation

cycle2.result: ARAF completed for 21 patients; completion rose from 3% to 54%

result.other_findings: 66% of women in the first cycle were aged 45-60.

result.topic: Driving risk assessment and DVLA advice
result.setting: Adult acute inpatient wards at one hospital, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local policy: leave risk discussion capturing driving risk before home leave, and DVLA driving advice documented in notes and discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Leave risk discussion compliance 73%, below target; only 5% of drivers given written DVLA guidance on discharge letters

result.intervention: Regular MDT communication during leave risk discussion, one professional assigned to advise and document, junior doctor induction on DVLA advice, MDT driving discussion at discharge meetings and driving advice added to discharge meeting checklist

cycle2.result: 100% compliance in use and quality of leave risk discussion; 56% had DVLA driving advice recorded on discharge summary

result.other_findings: 19 of 48 patients were drivers in the initial audit and 9 of 27 at re-audit.

result.setting: North West Edinburgh Community Mental Health Team, NHS Lothian
result.standard: SIGN guidelines: annual physical health monitoring for all patients on antipsychotic medication (9 domains)

cycle1.result: Domains achieved in 8% (lipid monitoring) to 51% (glucose monitoring)

result.intervention: Physical health questionnaire and staff training in phlebotomy and ECG, followed by a dedicated physical health monitoring clinic

cycle2.result: Decline in all domains from 2020, but 66% of domains still improved compared with 2019

result.other_findings: At the 2020 re-audit (74 patients) 77% of domains had improved, including blood pressure 9% to 37%, ECG 20% to 43% and lipids 29% to 46%; the later decline was attributed to COVID-19.

result.setting: Personality Disorder forums, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance and two audit standards and four treatment targets from the POMH-UK personality disorder audit

cycle1.result: Crisis plan 87%; documented reason for antipsychotic 43%; antipsychotics over 4 weeks without psychosis 86%; Z-hypnotics over 4 weeks 13%; benzodiazepines over 4 weeks 28%; medication reviews 90%

result.intervention: Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' published and circulated in December 2020

cycle2.result: Crisis plan 79%; documented reason for antipsychotic 69%; antipsychotics over 4 weeks 91%; Z-hypnotics over 4 weeks 37.5%; benzodiazepines over 4 weeks 38%; medication reviews 100%

result.other_findings: Compliance with treatment targets worsened and quality of medication reviews was unchanged. Findings to be presented with re-emphasis on guidelines; re-audit in 2 years.

result.topic: Cardiometabolic risk monitoring in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: All-male acute psychiatric ward, Livewell Southwest, Plymouth
result.standard: Lester UK Adaptation: Positive Cardiometabolic Health Resource screening and action for red-zone risk factors

cycle1.result: 50/63 had a Rethink template; of 41 smokers 15 not offered cessation support; 28 of 31 with BMI over 25 had no documented support; 8 of 12 hypertensive had no further action; 27 of 32 with dyslipidaemia had no intervention; 25 had no bloods

result.intervention: Changes to admission physical health assessments, well-man clinics and improved inpatient-community communication on discharge
result.other_findings: 9 patients had no smoking status and 15 had no blood glucose test. Re-audit pending.

result.setting: Victoria Ward, old age psychiatry, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BMA, BNF and trust prescription writing standards (GMC number, signature, doctor name, drug, indication, dose, route, frequency, dates, timings)

cycle1.result: Errors found in all parameters except medication timings

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and re-training on prescription writing

cycle2.result: Errors increased: GMC number errors up 20.33%, doctor name 16.87%, indication 12.94%, original start date 5%; name of drug improved by 10.88%

result.other_findings: After the audit the trust issued stamps with GMC number and doctor's name; re-audit planned 6 months after stamps and quarterly training for new trainees.

result.setting: Community Mental Health Team, Glasgow, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: NICE: weight, blood pressure and heart rate monitored every 6 months on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: Weight recorded 15%; heart rate 8%; blood pressure 19%

result.intervention: First cycle results presented at a local meeting with relevant clinicians

cycle2.result: Weight recorded 45%; heart rate 40%; blood pressure 50%; NICE standard still not met

result.other_findings: 30 patients were identified but 10 did not engage and were excluded; fewer face-to-face reviews during COVID-19 likely affected monitoring.

result.setting: Early Intervention Team, Warrington and Halton
result.standard: NICE psychosis and schizophrenia guidance: physical health monitoring at defined intervals after starting antipsychotics (e.g. BP at 12 weeks and 1 year)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 51%; weight/BMI and waist circumference 0%; pulse and BP 43% (90% by 1 year); lipids 48% (86% within a year); prolactin 52%; FBC 86%, U&E 86%, LFT 90%; glucose/HbA1c 48%; ECG at 1 year 67%

result.intervention: Recommended: disseminate results through the team, add waist circumference to the physical health assessment form and create blood sample sets
result.other_findings: COVID-19 limiting in-person appointments, staff redeployment and disengagement may have lowered compliance. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: Three acute general adult inpatient wards, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists HDAT guidance: documented rationale, risk-benefit discussion or capacity/legal process, and ECG, BMI and blood monitoring

cycle1.result: 3/49 (6%) on HDAT, with no documented rationale and variable physical health monitoring

result.intervention: Education sessions for rotational junior doctors in the six months after the initial audit

cycle2.result: 11/47 (23%) on HDAT; only 2 of 7 MDT/consultant-initiated cases noted HDAT initiation; 8 had ECG within a month before HDAT; only 3 had repeat ECG within 7 days

result.other_findings: Three patients gained at least 5 kg on HDAT; teaching had limited impact due to doctor turnover. Planned: departmental teaching, HDAT stickers on medication charts and ward round template.

result.setting: Acute female psychiatry inpatient ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health Trust
result.standard: Pregnancy status assessed and documented on admission for women of childbearing age (local practice)

cycle1.result: 7/15 (47%) had urine pregnancy test on admission; of 8 untested only 1 had documented contraceptive use and 7 had no LMP or contraception notes

result.intervention: Recommended: nursing admission checklist with LMP, contraception and sexual activity form if urine sample refused, reviewed by medical team before medication
result.other_findings: No pregnancy test strips were available on the ward for about a month; one untested patient was found pregnant a month later. Re-audit planned January-June 2022.

result.setting: Wolverhampton Older Adult Enhanced Community Mental Health Teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BCHFT standard operating procedure: 15 standards for depot prescription writing

cycle1.result: Standard 3 (signed, dated, name printed) 75%; Standard 7 (interval using 'every') 19%

result.intervention: Memory aid for prescribers placed at the front of depot card folders
result.other_findings: Standard 3 failures were mainly from no printed name, likely due to no space on the card; depot cards to be revised with signature and name columns and harmonised across the trust.

result.topic: Resuscitation and physical health equipment checks
result.setting: Four acute adult inpatient wards, mental health hospital, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists 'Physical Health in Mental Health' and Resuscitation Council UK mental health inpatient equipment and drug lists, in line with trust standards

cycle1.result: 90.0% of standards met; physical health equipment available and functional 83.8%; resuscitation equipment 94.2%

result.intervention: Awareness presentations at clinical governance meetings, complete equipment sets on each ward, registration on the maintenance database, engineering maintenance, and weekly (previously monthly) resuscitation equipment checks

cycle2.result: 90.0% of standards met (144/160 items in stock and functional); physical health equipment 76.6% (49/64); resuscitation equipment 99.2% (95/96)

result.other_findings: Physical health equipment availability fell; a named staff member, a physical health equipment checklist and an electronic checking platform (My Kit Check) were proposed.

result.setting: Buckinghamshire Early Intervention Service, Oxford Health, outpatient
result.standard: NICE antipsychotic monitoring guidelines (updated September 2021); 80% compliance target per National Clinical Audit of Psychosis

cycle1.result: First three months after initiation: 6/9 parameters met standard (range 2% to 100%), failing weekly BMI, pulse, BP and one-month HbA1c; only 2 parameters met for outpatient initiations; after three months only 3/9 met (lipids, HbA1c, side effects)

result.intervention: Planned: checklist for medical and nursing staff and home monitoring of blood pressure and weight by patients
result.other_findings: Barriers included reduced contact during the pandemic, poor awareness, poor documentation of declined screening and impractical guidance such as weekly BMI. Re-audit in 6 months.

result.setting: Two community treatment teams, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: CNTW Trust policy and BNF prescribing guidance (compliant if 90-100% of prescriptions meet the standard)

cycle1.result: Prescribing rate 7%; indicated use documented in 61.65%

cycle2.result: Prescribing rate 10.8%; 100% within BNF limits, no diazepam 10 mg and none in pregnant/post-partum women; indicated use documented 80.8% (still non-compliant)

result.other_findings: Earlier audits in 2009 and 2017 were also compared. Planned: educational email, posters and quiz, with re-audit in one year.

result.topic: Driving risk assessment and DVLA advice
result.setting: Two acute adult psychiatric units and one old age mental health ward, Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Driving status confirmed on admission (target 100%) and driving advice given to all patients unfit to drive (target 100%), with documentation

cycle1.result: Driving status confirmed in 42% (15)

cycle2.result: Driving status confirmed in 47% (24); 6% improvement in drivers told they were unfit; 22% increase in DVLA advice given; DVLA notifications up 18%

result.other_findings: 15 current drivers were identified in the second cycle.

result.topic: Risk assessment documentation in forensic services
result.setting: Low Secure Services Unit, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust standards for completion of the Formulation Information Risk Management (FIRM) assessment (5 criteria)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Current/historical risks 100%; formulation 89%; Staying Safe/Staying Well care plan 73%; service user involved 16%; updated since last CPA 70%

result.other_findings: Significant improvement in formulation and care plan completion compared with October 2021; low patient involvement was often because assessments were done at night. Review at each 6-monthly CPA recommended.

result.topic: STOMP psychotropic medication review in learning disability
result.setting: Specialist Support Team (Lancashire and Greater Manchester), Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Psychotropic prescribing guidelines for people with intellectual disability and challenging behaviour (STOMP): indication and rationale, consent to treatment, monitoring of response and side effects, review of continuation

cycle1.result: Indication and rationale stated 50%; consent to treatment, monitoring and review of continuation each under 10%

result.other_findings: Compliance was counted generously, so true practice may be worse. An early re-audit was recommended.

result.topic: Blood pressure control in chronic kidney disease
result.setting: Primary care practices supported by University Hospitals of Leicester; 20 practices with adult population 121,362 analysed
result.standard: Blood pressure management targets for CKD and coding of CKD (targets not specified)

cycle1.result: Most significant change in clinical markers occurred during cycle 1; increases in coded CKD prevalence, BP recording and CKD patients achieving BP targets (exact figures not reported in abstract)

result.intervention: IMPAKT IT tool used by a CKD nurse at primary care practices to identify CKD patients with uncontrolled hypertension and disseminate this to clinical staff

cycle2.result: Improvement maintained through cycle 2; an additional 345 individuals with CKD achieved better blood pressure control by end of project

result.other_findings: Estimated 9 cardiovascular events prevented and £320,000 saved across 20 practices. A large proportion of high-risk patients remained above ideal blood pressure.

result.topic: Early aspirin after coronary artery bypass grafting
result.setting: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital, specialist cardiothoracic centre
result.standard: EACTS 2007/AHA 2011 guidelines: medium dose aspirin 6 hours after CABG

cycle1.result: Early aspirin prescribed in 23% and administered in 17%

result.intervention: Educational presentations, leaflets and posters, pharmacy liaison and modification of e-prescription order sets

cycle2.result: Early aspirin prescribed in 55% and administered in 48%

result.other_findings: Intermediate cycle (January 2016, n=65) showed 48% prescription and 38% administration. Omission despite clear indication fell by 50%.

result.topic: Neutropenic sepsis door to needle time
result.setting: Belfast Health and Social Care Trust: acute cancer centre assessment areas, emergency departments and inpatient wards
result.standard: First dose empirical intravenous antibiotics within one hour (national door to needle target)

cycle1.result: 15% received antibiotics within 60 minutes

result.intervention: Integrated care pathway, later replaced by compact care pathway; ward-based documentation, patient group direction for nurse-led first dose antibiotics, multidisciplinary education and better access to regional guidelines

cycle2.result: 95% received first dose within 60 minutes (100% in July 2016)

result.other_findings: Re-audits showed 62% in June 2012 and 50% in January 2013; from November 2013 consistently over 80% met the one-hour target.

result.setting: General practice, Harrow CCG
result.standard: NICE antibiotic guidelines for sore throat based on Centor criteria; target 90% compliance

cycle1.result: Over 50% given antibiotics; 27% of those did not meet NICE criteria; 85% immediate prescriptions; Centor documented in 2%; correct course length 15%; choice 94%, dose 92%, frequency 100% correct

result.intervention: Oral and poster presentations, guideline dissemination by email, and an automated sore throat template and information page in EMIS

cycle2.result: Compliance with NICE criteria 87%; immediate prescribing 66%; Centor documentation 42%; correct course length over 30%; choice, dose and frequency 100%

result.other_findings: Two PDSA cycles completed. Correct antibiotic course length remained poor.

result.topic: Duodenal biopsies for suspected coeliac disease
result.setting: Endoscopy service at a single UK institution
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: at least four duodenal biopsy specimens when coeliac disease suspected

cycle1.result: 21.9% had at least 4 biopsy specimens

result.intervention: Measures to raise awareness among endoscopy users
result.other_findings: Taking fewer than 4 specimens may lead to missed coeliac disease diagnoses.

result.setting: Paediatric emergency plastic surgery, Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital, London
result.standard: WHO Safer Surgery checklist completion

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 88%; sign-in 85%, time-out 92%, sign-out 86%

result.intervention: Raised awareness at an audit meeting
result.other_findings: Around one in four checklists were not scanned in both periods.

result.setting: University Hospital of North Midlands, tertiary centre general surgical take
result.standard: NELA average mortality 11.1% and median length of stay 16.3 days (comparison benchmark)

cycle1.result: 30-day mortality 21%; median length of stay 16 days; anastomotic leak rate 16.6%

result.intervention: Addition of a second consultant to the daily general surgery on-call rota

cycle2.result: 30-day mortality 10.50%; median length of stay 11 days; anastomotic leak rate 4.2%

result.other_findings: Second on-call consultant associated with 2.231 times greater chance of survival (p = 0.031); lower ASA, female sex, younger age and no ITU admission also associated with survival.

result.topic: Appropriateness of referrals to surgical assessment clinic
result.setting: One stop emergency surgical assessment clinic, Royal Shrewsbury Hospital
result.standard: Clinic referral criteria (new referral guidelines)

cycle1.result: 42.9% of referrals appropriate

result.intervention: New referral guidelines distributed to the local Care Coordination Centre handling GP referrals
result.other_findings: 75.8% of appropriate referrals managed as urgent outpatients; 97.8% of inappropriate referrals were admitted.

result.topic: Cancer diagnostic intervals in primary care
result.setting: 439 general practices in England, National Cancer Diagnosis Audit
result.standard: not reported (baseline for future audit of 2015 NICE suspected cancer guidance)

cycle1.result: Median diagnostic interval 40 days (IQR 15-86); median primary care interval 5 days (IQR 0-27); safety netting recorded for 44%; primary care-led investigation in 45%

result.other_findings: GPs judged diagnostic delay in 22% of cases, attributed to patient (26%), clinician (28%) or system (34%) factors. 76% had at least one comorbidity.

result.topic: Medication optimisation with STOPP/START in dementia
result.setting: Six specialist dementia in-patient wards, Cynon Valley Hospital
result.standard: STOPP/START criteria

cycle1.result: Benzodiazepines, antipsychotics and opiates most commonly prescribed inappropriately; statins, calcium and vitamin D most commonly unprescribed

cycle2.result: Overall 7% reduction in comorbidities and 8% reduction in prescriptions (average prescriptions per patient P = 0.022)

result.other_findings: No significant change in patients receiving polypharmacy (P = 0.084) or high-risk medication (P = 0.092).

result.setting: Paediatric inpatients, Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre
result.standard: Provider initiated testing and counselling for all inpatients not tested in previous 3 months

cycle1.result: 85 (63%) of 135 children had documented HIV tests

result.intervention: Bedside diagnostic HIV testing service with counsellors, supervision and remuneration

cycle2.result: 110 (94.8%) of 116 children had documented HIV tests

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Otolaryngology department, Northern Health and Social Care Trust, Antrim; hospital first-time attenders
result.standard: NICE guideline for otitis externa

cycle1.result: Ear swabs sent in 14 of 19 cases; Sofradex most popular empirical eardrop

result.intervention: Recommendation of Betnesol-N and swabs only for refractory cases, disseminated by posters and email reminders

cycle2.result: Ear swabs sent in 3 of 25 cases; Betnesol-N used in 24 of 25 cases

result.other_findings: 11 of 14 initial swabs grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Staphylococcus aureus, sensitive to empirical treatment.

result.setting: High-volume general surgery department, Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians, General Medical Council and Imperial College London standards (16 items)

cycle1.result: Checking of drug chart, IV fluid chart, analgesia, antiemetic, enoxaparin and TEDs ranged from 0% to 6%

result.intervention: Ward round sticker introduced, then redesigned after questionnaire feedback

cycle2.result: Noticeable improvement from baseline in all items when stickers used; entries without stickers similar to baseline

result.other_findings: Compliance and sustainability need ongoing promotion.

result.setting: Glasgow Royal Infirmary inpatients with diabetes
result.standard: 'CPR for Feet' (Check, Protect and Refer) campaign guidelines

cycle1.result: 28% had evidence of foot assessment; 13% of staff aware of the campaign

result.intervention: Staff education and 'CPR for Feet' assessment checklist, then a 'CPR for Feet' care bundle after staff feedback (four PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: 72% had feet assessed and managed correctly; all staff aware of the campaign

result.other_findings: 52% after the second PDSA cycle.

result.topic: Hyperemesis gravidarum management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Princess Royal University Hospital, Orpington
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Admissions to O&G reduced by 68.7% compared with before the proforma

result.intervention: ED clinical pathway and treatment protocol proforma for hyperemesis gravidarum

cycle2.result: Admissions to O&G reduced by 70.5% compared with before the proforma

result.other_findings: Estimated saving of £265 700 and 235 bed days per year.

result.setting: Routine 18+0 to 22+6 week anomaly scans at a UK hospital (Oxford)
result.standard: Recommended clinical image-acquisition standards: scan completeness and objective image quality scoring

cycle1.result: 103 501 images from 6257 examinations by 22 sonographers; departmental median scan completeness 72%

result.intervention: Targeted actions in response to audit findings (not detailed in abstract)

cycle2.result: 153 557 images from 6406 scans by 25 sonographers; departmental median scan completeness 78%

result.other_findings: Scan quality also improved. Analysis restricted to the 20 sonographers in both cycles; authors suggest automation because large-scale audit is time consuming.

result.setting: High-volume tertiary centre, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Standards derived from the Bologna guidelines for adhesive small bowel obstruction

cycle1.result: not reported (retrospective baseline audit)

result.intervention: Protocol based on Bologna guidelines including Gastrografin administration

cycle2.result: More patients managed conservatively, fewer had first-line surgery or surgery after 72 h conservative management, shorter length of stay, marked improvement in appropriate blood tests and CT use (figures not reported)

result.other_findings: Documentation of history and examination did not change between audits.

result.setting: Medical inpatients, Whittington Health NHS Trust, London
result.standard: National guidelines on VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary educational meetings and electronic email prompts to prescribers

cycle2.result: Number of patients with inappropriately suspended VTE prophylaxis significantly reduced (figures not reported)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Time to antibiotics in inpatient sepsis
result.setting: Urology inpatient ward, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh
result.standard: Prompt and complete sepsis treatment; primary outcome median time to antibiotic administration

cycle1.result: Median time to antibiotics 3.6 (1.9-6.9) hours

result.intervention: Targeted quality improvement interventions addressing identified causes of delay (not detailed)
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Acute mental health inpatient unit, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust policy 'Physical Examination of Service Users during Admission to Hospital'; target 100%

cycle1.result: One in four patients had no physical health checks

result.intervention: Simplified paper documentation, then combined with the history taking proforma (PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Compliance 90%, maintained at 90% at 1 month post implementation

result.other_findings: First cycle (simplified documentation) gave only 5% improvement; 100% target judged unrealistic due to cultural issues.

result.setting: General surgery, Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2014: 19 operation note items

cycle1.result: 0 of 19 items had 100% compliance before EPR

result.intervention: Introduction of an electronic patient record; results presented at local governance meeting

cycle2.result: Compliance improved by almost 19% (p=0.0003) between periods 1 and 5; 11 of 19 items (57.9%) reached 100% compliance post-EPR

result.other_findings: 250 notes across five periods. Antibiotic use, VTE prophylaxis and estimated blood loss remained poorly documented.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer time to treatment decision
result.setting: Head and neck disease management group, Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai, tertiary cancer centre
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Treatment decision by weeks 1-4: 28.32%, 63.88%, 80.8%, 89.87%; dropout rate 26%

result.intervention: Changes to patient work-up recommended by the head and neck DMG

cycle2.result: Treatment decision by weeks 1-4: 51.26%, 77.42%, 89.46%, 94.31%; dropout rate 17.57%

result.other_findings: About 50% of patients planned for surgery could be treated within the institution.

result.topic: Respiratory distress syndrome management in preterm infants
result.setting: Participating neonatal units in Wales (level two and three), infants born under 34 weeks
result.standard: Wales Neonatal Network national RDS guideline (2016)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of a national RDS guideline by the Wales Neonatal Network in 2016

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in targeted tidal volume ventilation, caffeine use, oxygen therapy post-surfactant and early parenteral nutrition (figures not reported)

result.other_findings: PEEP levels and timing of enteral feeds were worse; gestational age independently affected several practices.

result.topic: HbA1c testing in suspected heart failure
result.setting: General practice partnership, Creffield Medical Group, Colchester (about 29,000 patients)
result.standard: NICE 2018 heart failure guideline: HbA1c in investigation of suspected heart failure

cycle1.result: 31.6% had HbA1c measured; 36.8% had no diabetic investigation

result.intervention: Oral presentation and illustrated guide for GPs

cycle2.result: 59.3% had HbA1c measured; 20% had no diabetic status assessment

result.other_findings: Lack of GP awareness of the guideline update was identified.

result.setting: Six medical wards, district general hospital (Medway Maritime Hospital)
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons handover guidelines

cycle1.result: Likert survey showed significant junior doctor dissatisfaction with weekend handover

result.intervention: Standardised weekend handover proforma trialled for six months

cycle2.result: 67% increase in ease of identifying outstanding jobs; 57% better understanding of diagnosis and plan; 53% easier to identify patients needing review; 55% reported increased safety (p<0.01)

result.other_findings: Outcomes measured by doctor questionnaire.

result.setting: Papworth Hospital, specialist cardiothoracic hospital
result.standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology; ten standards in local Protocol for the Management of Massive Blood Loss in Adults

cycle1.result: 'Code Red' activated 18 times (0.83% of emergency surgeries)

cycle2.result: Activated 9 times (0.26%); 6% increase in appropriate activation, 26% increase in prompt haematology notification, 30% increase in timely blood product delivery, 25% decrease in blood transfused before activation

result.other_findings: Target timeframe reduced from 30 to 15 minutes between 2015 and 2018.

result.setting: Interventional radiology department, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, tertiary hospital
result.standard: Locally developed minimum criteria for angiographic procedure documentation (14 parameters; targets 80% and 100% completeness)

cycle1.result: Paper records: 8 of 14 parameters over 80% complete; 2 parameters at 100%

result.intervention: Conversion to electronic records, then a standardised procedure-specific electronic proforma

cycle2.result: After electronic proforma: 12 of 14 parameters met 80% threshold; 6 of 14 at 100%

result.other_findings: 99 records over three audits 6 months apart. Unstructured electronic records alone reduced parameters over 80% to 4 of 14.

result.setting: Children's inpatient unit, University Hospital Limerick, regional paediatric centre
result.standard: Full compliance with comprehensive biopsychosocial history documentation for all medical admissions

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Teaching interventions, educational sessions and a survey of NCHDs
result.other_findings: First re-audit showed a net 53% increase with 95% compliance, which fell to 82.5% but stayed above baseline.

result.topic: Epistaxis management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department with off-site ENT cover, Connolly Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Project measures: reduced re-bleed after nasal packing, longer packing duration, 100% ENT trolley stock

cycle1.result: Minimal vasoconstrictor use; mean nasal pack duration 7 hours; re-bleed rate after packing 39%

result.intervention: Stocked ENT trolley, atraumatic epistaxis ED pathway and staff education (repeated PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Re-bleed rate 14%; mean packing duration 8 hours; full trolley stocking achieved

result.other_findings: Re-bleed rates 20%, 40%, 21% and 25% in cycles 1-4; packing duration 9, 10, 10 and 12 hours.

result.topic: Cervical screening in women with substance use disorders
result.setting: Consultant outpatient clinic, National Drug Treatment Centre, Dublin
result.standard: NDTC Cervical Screening guidelines (derived from CervicalCheck)

cycle1.result: Adherence 33% (14/43)

result.other_findings: All 46 women had opioid use disorder; 59% homeless and 80% had a chronic medical condition.

result.setting: Operating theatres, Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Adapted WHO Surgical Safety Checklist; target 90% compliance and engagement by April 2019

cycle1.result: 'Sign In' compliance 55%; 'Time Out' compliance 91%; whole-team engagement 58%

result.intervention: Wall-mounted checklist replacing paper checklist, refined items, and 'Time Out' moved to immediately before knife to skin
result.other_findings: First re-audit after September 2018 introduction showed 'Sign In' 91%, 'Time Out' 94% and engagement 100%. Checklist used across all Trust theatres since April 2019.

result.setting: Second Surgical Propedeutic Department, Hippocration Hospital, Thessaloniki; elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, inguinal hernia repair and thyroidectomy
result.standard: American Society of Health-System Pharmacists guidelines on perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Compliance with number of prophylaxis doses 0% for hernia repair and laparoscopic cholecystectomy; 25% for thyroidectomy

result.intervention: Poster and training of medical staff on the guidelines

cycle2.result: Dose-number compliance 68.8% for hernia repair, 53.1% for laparoscopic cholecystectomy and 50% for thyroidectomy (not significant)

result.other_findings: No significant change in antibiotic choice or timing. Hospital stay fell and antibiotic costs significantly decreased.

result.setting: Breast clinic, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: GMC and Irish Medical Council: chaperone for intimate examinations, clearly documented

cycle1.result: Chaperone present 100% when male doctor examined female patient, but documented in 0/126 charts

result.intervention: Chaperone stamp in medical notes, educational email with GMC/IMC guidance and posters in clinic rooms
result.other_findings: At 1 week documentation was 80% (51/64). Survey: 50% of doctors did not know documentation was necessary and 25% forgot.

result.setting: Hospitals and community centres across the Gaza Strip (online survey of auditors)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: Survey 12 October to 2 November 2018, covering audits 2015-2018
cycle1.result: Audit cycle completed in 13 projects (20.9%), 7 reporting improvement; only 32 (51.6%) presented to local staff

result.other_findings: Clear standards identified in 54 audits (90%); students involved in 74% of audits and practising doctors in 47%.

result.setting: Neonatal unit, Harare Central Hospital
result.standard: Local WHO-derived guidelines for antibiotic use in neonatal sepsis

cycle1.result: Sepsis was the admitting diagnosis in 81%

result.intervention: Intern training programme on antimicrobial stewardship and distinguishing 'at risk of' from clinically suspected sepsis, with performance feedback

cycle2.result: Sepsis admitting diagnosis 59%; substantial decrease in antibiotic use (figures not reported)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: General surgical wards, Princess Royal University Hospital, Orpington
result.standard: Target 0% therapeutic duplication

cycle1.result: Baseline therapeutic duplication 9%

result.intervention: Presentation of data and education at surgical meeting, with repeated reminders
result.other_findings: Cycle averages 8.77% (with a 22% spike on one Friday) and 5.29%. Authors suggest an EPR alert for sustainability.

result.setting: Intra-abdominal surgery, tertiary hospital, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Single pre-operative antibiotic dose prophylaxis guidelines

cycle1.result: 100/205 (48.8%) received extended antibiotics beyond single-dose prophylaxis

result.intervention: Daily ward round 'ABBDDOMM' checklist, antimicrobial stewardship education and better guideline accessibility
result.other_findings: Interviews and surveys identified barriers; uptake of pre-operative induction antibiotic guidelines needs further work.

result.topic: Primary biliary cholangitis quality of care
result.setting: 11 NHS hospitals in England, Wales and Scotland (national pilot audit)
result.standard: EASL 2017 PBC management guidelines

cycle1.result: Majority of hospitals did not meet all EASL standards; lowest achievement for optimal UDCA dosing, bone density assessment and symptom assessment

result.other_findings: Significant variation between trusts in these standards and in assessment of biochemical response to UDCA. PBC Review tool developed for future re-audit.

result.setting: Emergency Department, University Hospital Aintree, Liverpool
result.standard: Target: CO exposure considered in 50% of non-traumatic headache presentations

cycle1.result: CO considered in 0.8% of non-traumatic headache presentations

result.intervention: Verbal reminders, then CO posters, then CO COMA sticker placed in patient notes (three 2-week PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: CO considered in 42.1% after sticker cycle

result.other_findings: 1.7% after verbal reminders and 10.0% after posters; average 61 patients per cycle.

result.topic: Vitamin B12 deficiency diagnosis and treatment
result.setting: Urban general practice, midwest Ireland
result.standard: Royal United Hospital Bath 'Guidelines for the Investigation & Management of B12 deficiency'

cycle1.result: Compliance 17% (n = 6)

result.intervention: Patients recalled for follow-on investigations (21) and switched from IM to oral replacement (10)
result.other_findings: Annual reduction of 46 nurse consultations (30%) for IM B12, saving €1,340.

result.setting: COVID-19 inpatients, The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidelines for initial blood investigation of COVID-19 inpatients

cycle1.result: FBC 99.7%, U&E 99.2%, CRP 98.7%, LFT 96.6%, coagulation 72.8%, appropriate D-dimer 19.9%, inappropriate troponin 38.9%

result.intervention: Results presented locally and a COVID-19 blood request panel with prompts added to the electronic system

cycle2.result: FBC, U&E, CRP and LFT 100%; coagulation 90% (p = 0.09); appropriate D-dimer 50% (p = 0.001); inappropriate troponin 26.3% (p = 0.23)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn, district general hospital
result.standard: Completed accurate MUST within 6 hours of AMU arrival (80%); dietitian referral within 48 hours for MUST ≥2 (100%)

cycle1.result: MUST correct in 111/150 (74%); 1/9 (11%) high-risk patients referred to dietitians

result.intervention: Face-to-face training, e-learning module in induction and ward MUST troubleshooting booklets

cycle2.result: MUST correct in 77/101 (76%); 2/4 (50%) high-risk patients referred

result.other_findings: Nurses (n = 19) felt confident but averaged 67% on an objective assessment; targets not met.

result.setting: King's Mill Hospital
result.standard: BTS Acute NIV standards: NIV initiated within two hours of admission

cycle1.result: 31% had a delay in initiation of acute NIV

result.intervention: Acute NIV e-learning packages sent to medical staff

cycle2.result: 77% had a delay in initiation of acute NIV

result.other_findings: Delays worsened after intervention but did not appear to adversely affect patient outcomes.

result.setting: Neurosurgery department, Jinnah Hospital, Lahore, public tertiary hospital
result.standard: Comparison with contemporary international literature on theatre time utilisation

cycle1.result: 56% of theatre time used operating; anaesthesia team arrival delay 4.7%, patient transfer delay 9.7%, intubation and preparation 23%, extubation 5.7%

result.other_findings: Most delays judged avoidable; strategies developed with anaesthesia and ward staff and a re-audit is planned.

result.setting: St James's Hospital, Dublin; patients after gastrectomy 2010-2020
result.standard: Vitamin B12 supplementation and surveillance guidelines post-gastrectomy

cycle1.result: 91.9% (79/86) total gastrectomy patients adherent with parenteral B12; 53.8% (21/39) subtotal gastrectomy patients checking B12

cycle2.result: 5/8 (57.5%) previously non-adherent total gastrectomy patients now adherent; 7/17 (41.2%) subtotal gastrectomy patients received or arranged B12

result.other_findings: Only 53.6% knew supplementation was important and 14.4% knew complications of deficiency.

result.setting: Children's hospice services (UK)
result.standard: Recording of mouth care provision (Mini Mouth Care Matters)

cycle1.result: not reported (audit of hospice records before Mini Mouth Care Matters)

result.intervention: Mini Mouth Care Matters assessment tool and virtual interactive training session for hospice colleagues

cycle2.result: Increase in mouth assessment, earlier identification of problems and improved daily mouth care (figures not reported)

result.other_findings: Almost 30% of colleagues had never had mouth care training; 11% of children had never visited a dentist and nearly half brushed less than twice a day.

result.setting: District general hospital, UK (Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust)
result.standard: European Association of Urology 2022 guidelines for TURBT documentation

cycle1.result: Tumour size 46%, tumour description 59%, depth of resection 36%, chemotherapy 21%, perforation assessment 22%, completeness of resection 59%, pre-op EUA 47%, post-op EUA 14%

result.intervention: Standardised TURBT operation note template with staff training

cycle2.result: Tumour size 89%, description 89%, depth 89%, chemotherapy 46%, perforation 68% (p=0.001), completeness 68% (p=0.42), pre- and post-op EUA 89%

result.other_findings: Completeness of resection improvement was not statistically significant.

result.topic: BMI recording and healthy weight conversations
result.setting: Specialist paediatric dental service, City HealthCare Partnership, Hull; general anaesthetic assessments for caries extractions
result.standard: All GA assessment patients should have BMI calculated, healthier weight conversation and signposting when needed

cycle1.result: BMI recorded in 7%; no healthier weight conversations recorded

result.intervention: Results shared and discussion of how to have healthy weight conversations

cycle2.result: BMI calculated for 65%; healthier weight conversations held when necessary

result.other_findings: Clinicians reported forgetting and discomfort about raising weight.

result.setting: UK specialist stroke unit
result.standard: Internally agreed standardised ward round documentation criteria

cycle1.result: Overall documentation of criteria 48.7%

result.intervention: Stroke-specific ward round proforma designed with the multidisciplinary team
result.other_findings: Largest gains in neurological examination, mechanical VTE prophylaxis and blood results; proforma updated after MDT feedback.

result.topic: PPI co-prescription with dual antiplatelet therapy
result.setting: Cardiology ward, tertiary cardiac unit, Royal Wolverhampton Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: European Society of Cardiology: PPI for patients on DAPT; target 100%

cycle1.result: 56% of patients on DAPT co-prescribed a PPI

result.intervention: Education sessions for junior doctors, nurses and pharmacists, posters, and pharmacy protocol to check PPI before discharge summary finalised

cycle2.result: 100% of patients on DAPT co-prescribed a PPI

result.other_findings: Three audit cycles; improvement sustained across a subsequent cohort of junior doctors.

result.setting: General surgery hot clinic (ambulatory care), UK
result.standard: Hot clinic ambulatory care standards; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 19% seen by on-call team before hot clinic; 19% met eligibility criteria; median 7 patients per day

result.intervention: Specific criteria-based hot clinic guideline and a monitoring programme led by an on-call junior doctor

cycle2.result: 100% seen by on-call team first and 100% met eligibility criteria; median 1 patient per day

result.other_findings: First re-audit (January 2019, n=40) also showed 100% for both standards.

result.setting: Emergency department, Queen's Hospital, Romford
result.standard: GMC and RCP standards: date, time, full name, GMC number and signature

cycle1.result: Low documentation of all parameters, especially GMC number and signature

result.intervention: Presentation of results and awareness raising among ED staff

cycle2.result: Significant rise in all parameters; relative improvement 40% for GMC number and 65% for signature

result.other_findings: GMC number and signature documentation remained below acceptable levels.

result.topic: Perioperative variable rate intravenous insulin infusion prescribing
result.setting: Vascular surgery ward, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Established standards for perioperative VRIII prescribing

cycle1.result: 'Refer to paper chart' safety check used in 33%; rescue medication prescribed in 0%

result.intervention: VRIII prescribing checklist, education of junior doctors and ward staff, and electronic prescribing updates

cycle2.result: 'Refer to paper chart' used in 77% (p=0.046); rescue medication prescribed in 65%

result.other_findings: Post-intervention period (n=18) showed 67% and 50%. Sustained improvement in adjustment of oral diabetes medicines and insulins; some VRIII use unnecessary in type 2 diabetes.

result.setting: Urology, Princess Royal University Hospital, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Average cancellation rate 9.57/40 (23.92%) per month

result.intervention: Specialist urology nurse-led preassessment clinic reviewing urine cultures and arranging lead-in antibiotics, backfilling slots, and new preassessment guideline
result.other_findings: First month after change 4/124 (3%); 2%-16% of patients started on antibiotics each month.

result.setting: General practice (Sheffield)
result.standard: MHRA Drug Safety Update Vol 5 Issue 5, December 2011 on citalopram and escitalopram

cycle1.result: Incorrect dose in over 65s 8; dangerous interactions 44; unsafe prescribing overall 47

result.intervention: Prescriber teaching on safer citalopram use and an EMIS safety prompt

cycle2.result: Incorrect dose in over 65s 1; dangerous interactions 8; unsafe prescribing overall 9

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 30 acute hospitals in the Republic of Ireland, Irish National Audit of Dementia Care (INAD-2)
result.standard: Audit tool adapted from the England and Wales National Audit of Dementia (Royal College of Psychiatrists)

cycle1.result: 83% on psychotropics at admission; 40% given new or increased psychotropics; antipsychotics for NCSD in 11.8-17.6% and benzodiazepines in 4.5-7.7%; type of dementia specified in 52%

result.other_findings: Poor documentation of risk/benefit and family discussion, and inadequate review for efficacy and tolerability. Baseline before a national clinical guideline.

result.topic: Disposable instrument use in laparoscopic appendicectomy
result.setting: Large teaching hospital, University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 109 disposable instruments in 25 appendicectomies (median four per case); estimated £49,656 and 692 kg CO2e annually

result.intervention: Revised laparoscopic appendicectomy set with additional reusable instruments and reusable ports

cycle2.result: Median one disposable instrument per case, a significant reduction

result.other_findings: Projected financial and CO2e savings over the seven-year lifecycle of reusable instruments.

result.topic: Actionable reporting and alert notification in CT
result.setting: Major trauma centre, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham; A&E and inpatient body CT
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists standards for communication of radiological reports and fail-safe alert notification

cycle1.dates: not reported (two cycles within three months)
cycle1.result: 95/100 reports met RCR criteria

result.other_findings: One inpatient and two A&E reports failed criteria in cycle 2.

result.topic: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease referrals
result.setting: GP Healthlink referrals to vascular surgery, University College Hospital Galway (Saolta region)
result.standard: Best medical therapy: antiplatelets, statins, smoking cessation, blood pressure and glycaemic control

cycle1.result: 34.5% (n = 40) on antiplatelets and 52% (n = 60) on statins; 31% no smoking status; only eleven letters mentioned risk factor optimisation

result.intervention: Information leaflet on best medical therapy posted to all GP practices (re-audit planned at 6 months)
result.other_findings: Suspected critical limb ischaemia not associated with BMT prescription (p = 0.664); 28% active smokers.

result.setting: Mohammed Bin Khalifa Bin Salman Al Khalifa Specialist Cardiac Centre, Bahrain Defence Force Hospital
result.standard: ESC/EACTS 2017 valvular heart disease guidelines (23 parameters)

cycle1.result: Fully adherent to 12 of 23 standards; 13/82 (15.85%) patients compliant with all standards

result.intervention: Checklist created to ensure guideline adherence (re-audit planned)
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Flumazenil use after midazolam conscious sedation
result.setting: Sedation and Special Care Department, dental hospital (King's College London)
result.standard: High-quality record keeping and clinical justification before administering flumazenil in conscious sedation (no named guideline or target stated)

cycle1.result: 21 of 665 patients receiving midazolam conscious sedation were given IV flumazenil; the commonest reason was prolonged recovery (9, 42.8%).

result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit, but the earlier audit's results are not given in the abstract. Flumazenil was mostly used in non-emergency circumstances in certain patient groups.

result.topic: Negative appendicectomy rate and preoperative imaging
result.setting: District general hospital, emergency general surgery
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 17%; adult NAR 13%.

result.intervention: Diagnostic pathway for suspected appendicitis placing greater emphasis on preoperative imaging (CT or ultrasound).

cycle2.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 16%; adult NAR fell to 9%.

result.other_findings: All patients over 21 had preoperative CT in the re-audit; the NAR stayed high in younger patients, where CT radiation is harder to justify and ultrasound sensitivity and specificity was about 60% in previous local audits.

result.setting: General Surgery Unit, Khyber Teaching Hospital, Peshawar
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) guidelines for operative note documentation

cycle1.result: Peri-operative findings recorded in 56 (70.8%) notes; operative diagnosis in 65 (82.3%).

result.intervention: Implementation of the RCS operative note guidelines.

cycle2.result: Peri-operative findings 68 (95.7%); operative diagnosis 69 (97.2%); operation type, date and time 67 (94.4%); complications 66 (92.9%); additional procedures 64 (90.1%); tissue alterations 60 (84.5%); prosthesis 65 (91.5%); closure 66 (92.9%); DVT prophylaxis and time out 68 (95.8%); postoperative orders 70 (98.6%); signatures 69 (97.2%).

result.other_findings: 150 notes in total were assessed; the abstract does not describe how the guidelines were implemented.

result.setting: Single centre, general surgical theatres (Bradford Teaching Hospitals)
result.standard: Intercollegiate Green Theatre Checklist, 'preparing for surgery' and 'intraoperative equipment' subsections

cycle1.result: Reusable trolley covers 96%, drapes 100%, gowns 90%; alcohol-based scrubbing 15%; carbon footprint 128.27 kgCO2e.

result.intervention: Dissemination of results at clinical governance meetings and poster displays.

cycle2.result: Reusable trolley covers 78%, drapes 92%, gowns 46% (procurement issues); alcohol-based scrubbing 17%; carbon footprint 117.71 kgCO2e.

result.other_findings: No unnecessary catheter use and loose skin preparations used throughout; unnecessary non-sterile glove use in over 30% of procedures and all laparoscopic ports and scissors were single use.

result.topic: Lens exclusion on non-contrast head CT
result.setting: Newham University Hospital, two CT scanners
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standard for lens exclusion in non-contrast head CT

cycle1.result: Lens exclusion compliance 0/63 (0%).

result.intervention: Presentation of results and a three-month radiographer re-education period emphasising gantry tilt and patient positioning.
result.other_findings: The RCR standard was still not met; variability in radiographer practice, near misses, time constraints and staff turnover limited compliance.

result.setting: Department of Surgery, University Hospital Galway (Model 4 hospital), elective and emergency general surgery
result.standard: HSE National Consent Policy 2022 and RCSI standards for written consent

cycle1.result: Patient name, DOB and board number recorded in all forms; 66% (n=63) documented without abbreviations or acronyms.

result.intervention: In-person educational session for surgical non-consultant hospital doctors on informed written consent and legal criteria.

cycle2.result: Name, DOB and board number recorded in all forms; 84% (n=122) documented without abbreviations or acronyms (p=0.0017).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of general surgery (Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh / East Lancashire hospitals)
result.standard: GMC Good Medical Practice, NICE and Royal College of Nursing guidance on verbal and written information for patients with acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Development of patient information leaflets and encouraging healthcare professionals to distribute them and give information to patients and families.

cycle2.result: Improvement in all aspects of information provided; more than 100% improvement in patient satisfaction with information.

result.other_findings: Data were collected with an 11-question patient questionnaire.

result.setting: Newcastle Eye Centre, Royal Victoria Infirmary, orthoptic service
result.standard: Visual acuity outcomes from the previous 2011-12 audit (VA of 0.250 logMAR or better in the amblyopic eye)

cycle1.result: 59% of patients achieved VA of 0.250 logMAR or better.

cycle2.result: 60% achieved VA of 0.250 logMAR or better; no statistically significant difference from previous outcomes for any amblyopia type.

result.other_findings: 62% completed treatment within two years; one adverse event (atropine); only 18/174 (10%) could stop occlusion after six to eight weeks, suggesting first follow-up could be extended.

result.topic: Gender-based violence enquiry in mental health services
result.setting: Home treatment team, drug and alcohol service and in-patient ward, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Documented enquiry about exposure to gender-based violence in female and non-binary patients' records (no target stated)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Brief, cost-neutral staff engagement and education interventions at service, borough and trust levels.

cycle2.result: Documented GBV enquiry increased by 30% (HTT), 15% (ward) and 7% (D&A).

result.other_findings: Up to 56% of records identified psychiatric symptoms related to GBV; quality of response was harder to measure.

result.topic: Head injury assessment and CT times in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Sandwell General Hospital
result.standard: Over 90% of high-risk head injury patients assessed by an ED clinician within 15 minutes of arrival

cycle1.result: 31% assessed within 15 minutes; average time to CT head 69 min; CT reporting 98 min; time to decision 6 hours 48 min.

result.intervention: New adult head injury pathway with risk stratification, modified imaging and patient transport, and early decision making (PDSA cycles).

cycle2.result: 63% assessed within 15 minutes; average time to CT head 53 min; CT reporting 71 min; time to decision 4 hours 24 min.

result.other_findings: The 90% target was not reached; a re-audit at 3 to 6 months was planned.

result.setting: Regional oncology centre, Hull University Teaching Hospitals (interventional radiology and gastroenterology procedures)
result.standard: Hospital peri-procedural antibiotic guidelines

cycle1.result: 6/82 (7.3%) did not receive correct peri-procedural antibiotics; adherence 93%.

result.intervention: Formal and informal teaching on peri-procedure antibiotics and ensuring the full guideline was available in clinical areas.

cycle2.result: 1/25 (4%) did not receive antibiotics per guideline; adherence 96% (p = 0.50).

result.other_findings: The improvement was not statistically significant.

result.topic: Histopathology review and communication after appendicectomy
result.setting: Single UK centre, emergency general surgery
result.standard: NHS England 2016 patient safety guidance on timely review and communication of histopathology results

cycle1.result: 207 (49.52%) reviewed within 15 days and 47 (11.24%) at 16-30 days; 116 (27.75%) unreviewed; communication documented in 67 (16.02%).

result.intervention: Presentation at clinical governance meeting and implementation of agreed recommendations and protocols.

cycle2.result: 38 (77.55%) reviewed within 15 days and 10 (20.4%) at 16-30 days; communication documented in 16 (32.65%).

result.other_findings: Documented communication with patients or GPs remained low after the change.

result.setting: Tertiary regional ENT department, Liverpool University Hospitals
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons standards for operative notes (18 criteria)

cycle1.result: Lack of adherence to RCS standards (figures not reported in abstract).

result.intervention: Operative note proforma modified to include the 18 RCS criteria.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documentation quality and adherence to standards (P value truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis after assisted vaginal birth
result.setting: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust, labour ward and theatre
result.standard: National recommendation for a single dose of prophylactic antibiotics after assisted vaginal birth

cycle1.result: Prophylactic antibiotic administration 13.2%.

result.intervention: Evidence-based journal clubs for doctors in training, presentations of results after each audit cycle, and expedited change of local guidelines.

cycle2.result: Prophylactic antibiotic administration 90.7%; over 90% in both labour ward rooms and theatre.

result.other_findings: Three audit cycles (n=287) 2020-2023; the interim audit showed antibiotics often omitted after labour ward room deliveries (59.3%) vs 100% in theatre. Maternal infection 18.2% with prophylaxis vs 22.2% without, but overall postnatal infection rates rose gradually.

result.topic: Dementia recording in ambulance patient records
result.setting: South Central Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust, electronic patient record
result.standard: Recording of dementia on ambulance ePRs for patients aged 65 or over (no target stated)

cycle1.result: Dementia recorded in 13.5% of patients aged 65 or over and 16.5% of those aged 75 or over.

result.intervention: A dedicated dementia section (tab) with a diagnosis button and free-text field added to the ePR.

cycle2.result: Dementia recorded in 16.5% (n = 18,515) aged 65 or over and 19.9% aged 75 or over; 69.9% of these used the dementia button and 25.4% the tab free text.

result.other_findings: Dementia was recorded only in other free-text fields in 29.7% of records, across 18 other fields.

result.setting: Acute Senior Health Unit, St George's University Hospital
result.standard: NICE delirium guidelines

cycle1.result: Full delirium assessment 1.9%; formal diagnosis 5.8%.

result.intervention: Posters and education-based multidisciplinary team interventions developed after literature analysis and ward discussion.
result.other_findings: 128 patients in total across both cycles; authors propose a 5-step framework and a repeat audit to check sustainability.

result.topic: Gastrografin protocol in adhesive small bowel obstruction
result.setting: General surgery, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Non-operative Gastrografin success 77% (24/31); median conservative management two days; median CT to Gastrografin 24 hours; Gastrografin to first radiograph 9 hours.

result.intervention: Hospital-wide protocol standardising Gastrografin use in adhesive small bowel obstruction.

cycle2.result: Success 88% (15/17); median conservative management two days; median CT to Gastrografin 19 hours 22 minutes; Gastrografin to first radiograph 6 hours 25 minutes.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: CT KUB for suspected renal colic
result.setting: Barts Health NHS Trust, radiology referrals from A&E and primary care
result.standard: Institutional guidance: CT KUB as the investigation for renal colic (100% target) within 24 hours, diagnostic yield minimum 44%-64%

cycle1.result: 42 (56%) appropriately investigated with CT KUB; 50 (66.7%) investigated within 24 hours; 17 (40.5%) CT KUBs positive for calculi.

result.intervention: Presentation of results with recommendations to each department, re-education and raising awareness of guidelines, emphasising thorough clinical history on requests.

cycle2.result: 55 (73.3%) investigated with CT KUB; 36 (65.5%) positive for calculi; 24 (32.0%) delayed beyond 24 hours.

result.other_findings: No significant improvement in investigation within 24 hours; a third cycle with posters, lectures and streamlined referral pathways is planned.

result.setting: Two general surgical wards, Royal Blackburn Teaching Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: British Thoracic Society guideline: all inpatients should have a valid oxygen prescription with a target saturation range (target 100%)
