result.standard: Nine JBI audit criteria for post-operative pain assessment and management

cycle1.result: Poor compliance with best practice (figures not given).

result.intervention: Strategies to address non-compliance, including health education for patients and caregivers and use of validated pain scales.

cycle2.result: Health education up to 80%; pain measurement on admission and post-surgery 91%; pre-operative assessment guiding pain management at discharge below 50%.

result.other_findings: Three follow-up audits with 34, 40 and 46 patients.

result.setting: Paediatric unit, Marqués de Valdecilla University Hospital, Santander
result.standard: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for promoting sleep and rest in hospitalised children

cycle1.result: Staff trained in paediatric sleep 4%; multi-faceted sleep promotion 21%; relaxation techniques 0%.

result.intervention: Evidence-based strategies including staff training on paediatric sleep.

cycle2.result: Staff trained 80%; multi-faceted sleep promotion 87%; relaxation techniques 80%.

result.other_findings: 27 multidisciplinary staff involved; yearly follow-up audits recommended.

result.setting: Taibah University Dental Hospital, Madinah; paediatric patients
result.standard: Guidelines on appropriate antibiotic prescribing in dental practice

cycle1.result: 119 antibiotic prescriptions; inappropriate prescribing prevalent.

result.intervention: Action plan with guidelines and educational sessions.
result.other_findings: Amoxicillin then Augmentin were most prescribed; pulpal diseases and periradicular complications accounted for most prescriptions in both cycles.

result.setting: Rural health clinic, southern United States (University of Mississippi Medical Center)
result.standard: JBI best practice for heart failure management (enrolment in disease management programme)

cycle1.result: 0% compliance with best practice.

result.intervention: Policy/protocol for a disease management programme and a virtual multidisciplinary team.
result.other_findings: Recommends using the electronic health record to identify heart failure patients and 6-monthly chart audits.

result.topic: Prevention and management of contrast media reactions
result.setting: Medical imaging centre of a nearly 5,000-bed tertiary hospital (enhanced CT)
result.standard: Four JBI best practice audit criteria for prevention and management of allergic-like reactions to iodine contrast media

cycle1.result: Emergency equipment management 37.50%; overall reaction rate 0.56%.

result.intervention: Strategies designed from audit feedback to address identified barriers.

cycle2.result: More than 60% compliance with the four criteria; emergency equipment management 100%; reaction rate 0.19%.

result.other_findings: Smallest improvement was in pre-procedure prophylactic treatment of high-risk patients (27.66%).

result.setting: Neurology ward of a tertiary psychiatric hospital, Tabriz
result.standard: JBI best practice audit criteria for fall prevention and management

cycle1.result: Ward transfer fall risk assessment 87%; patient participation in risk assessment 95%; revising fall risk status 50%; person-centred staff education 78%; patient engagement in goal-setting 100%.

result.intervention: Improvement strategies addressing gaps identified at baseline (details not given).

cycle2.result: Ward transfer risk assessment 90%; patient participation 96%; revising fall risk status 86%; person-centred staff education 96%; patient engagement in goal-setting 94%.

result.other_findings: 20 health care professionals also audited at baseline; other criteria were unchanged.

result.setting: Río Hortega University Hospital, Valladolid; labour ward, midwives
result.standard: 13 JBI best practice audit criteria for intrapartum care of occiput-posterior fetal position

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Improvement strategies addressing barriers, including midwife training.

cycle2.result: Improvement in all structure criteria (1-3), five process criteria (4-6, 8, 10) and all results criteria (11-13); criterion 8 at maximum compliance in all audits.

result.other_findings: Recording of upright positions (criterion 7) and CTG interpretation (criterion 9) remained inadequate. Two follow-up audits at 4-month intervals.

result.setting: Primary care nurses, Gran Canaria
result.standard: JBI best practice criteria on discharge planning and telephone follow-up for COPD patients

cycle1.result: 30-day readmission 2.78%; 30-day ED presentation 25% (compliance figures not given).

result.intervention: Improvement strategies addressing five barriers, including education.

cycle2.result: 100% for criteria 1 and 2 (discharge plan, plan includes telephone follow-up); 4.88% improvement for criteria 3 and 4 (prompt call, validated questionnaire).

result.other_findings: 30-day readmission rose to 4.88% while 30-day ED presentation fell to 9.76%.

result.setting: Long-term care unit, Hospital José Luciano de Castro, Anadia
result.standard: Three JBI audit criteria: communication training, teamwork/conflict training and use of a structured tool (ISBAR) at handover

cycle1.result: Communication training 0%; teamwork and conflict training 21%; ISBAR use at handover 43.6%.

result.intervention: Educational sessions and a focus group; ISBAR adapted for the unit.

cycle2.result: Communication training 78%; teamwork and conflict training 50%; ISBAR use 91%.

result.other_findings: Baseline included 250 observed handovers and a questionnaire of 14 nurses.

result.setting: Stroke unit, hospital in northern Portugal (Alto Minho Local Health Unit)
result.standard: Four JBI audit criteria for oral hygiene in stroke patients

cycle1.result: Low compliance with all four criteria; criterion 1 (nurse training) 0%.

result.intervention: Nurse training on oral hygiene assessment and management and co-created strategies.

cycle2.result: Criterion 1 100%; criterion 2 improved by 40%; criteria 3 and 4 improved by 36.7%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Gastroenterology and Pulmonology wards, Lady Reading Hospital, MTI Peshawar (HMIS electronic record)
result.standard: 100% allergy documentation per HMIS reading manual

cycle1.result: No documented allergies in 70% (n=7) in Gastroenterology and 60% (n=6) in Pulmonology.

result.intervention: Recommended interventions after identifying gaps (details not given).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Dongola Specialized Hospital
result.standard: Compliance with standardised discharge documentation format

cycle1.result: Compliance with format 66%.

result.intervention: Standardised discharge card with training sessions for healthcare providers.

cycle2.result: Compliance 92%; completeness of patient information 100%; clinical summaries improved by 40% and discharge plans by 30%; medication list accuracy 88%.

result.other_findings: Preliminary 15% reduction in readmissions; incomplete sections and time constraints remained.

result.topic: ABCDE assessment in the emergency department
result.setting: Internal emergency departments of two university hospitals
result.standard: 29 criteria based on World Health Organization guidelines for the ABCDE approach

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Findings presented locally and recommendations formulated.

cycle2.result: Improvement in compliance at both hospitals: hospital A 17.2% and hospital B 20.6% in the second cycle.

result.other_findings: 160 patients across both cycles. Barriers included glove wearing and patient privacy.

result.topic: Ovarian cancer quality of care indicators
result.setting: Gynaecological units treating ovarian cancer in the Piemonte Regional Cancer Care Network
result.standard: Key recommendations and indicators from international guidelines (global adherence)

cycle1.result: Global adherence to guidelines 51.3%.

result.intervention: Audit and feedback with quarterly feedback meetings.

cycle2.result: Global adherence rose to 70.4% (2.1% increase every 6 months, 95% CI 1.6 to 2.6).

result.other_findings: Treatment in high-volume centres and MDT discussion increased; a 10% increase in adherence was associated with improved 5-year survival (HR 0.91). Earlier regional audit in 2009.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: ERAS protocols for emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only; described as a closed-loop audit in a conflict zone.

result.topic: Lymph node yield in colon cancer surgery
result.setting: Department of Surgical Gastroenterology, tertiary care centre (AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad)
result.standard: ≥12 lymph nodes retrieved (high-yield lymphadenectomy)

cycle1.result: Mean LN yield 15.4 ± 7.8; high-yield cases 69%.

result.intervention: Structured surgical preceptorship programme: didactic sessions, hands-on training and standard operating protocols.
result.other_findings: Junior consultants improved significantly (14.6 to 17.69, P = 0.014); no difference between open and laparoscopic groups.

result.topic: Medication error prevention after root cause analysis
result.setting: King Abdulaziz Medical City, Riyadh
result.standard: Implementation of RCA2 recommendations after a hydralazine overdose

cycle1.result: Lapses identified in RCA2 recommendations at re-audit.

result.intervention: Changes to computerised physician order entry and medication preparation/disposal instructions in guidelines and CPOE order sets.

cycle2.result: No medication errors recurred for over a year.

result.other_findings: Describes RCA3, adding sustainability audits to RCA2.

result.setting: Perinatology/Reproduction and Internal Medicine Units, Veterinary Teaching Hospital, University of Bologna; hospitalised horses
result.standard: International guidelines recommending antimicrobial stewardship programmes

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Review and implementation of antimicrobial use and biosecurity policies.

cycle2.result: Significant reduction in overall resistant bacterial colonisation (foals OR 0.27, p = 0.03; adults OR 0.39, p = 0.01) and in MRS colonisation (foals OR 0.30).

result.other_findings: 328 horses across both cycles; no genotypic analysis and surgery unit excluded.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: National Cancer Control Programme 2024 melanoma imaging guidelines

cycle1.result: Staging imaging 92% (11/12); surveillance PET-CT 55% (6/11); MRI/CT brain 27% (3/11).

cycle2.result: Staging imaging 100% (12/12); surveillance PET-CT 87.5% (7/8); MRI/CT brain 50% (4/8).

result.other_findings: Gaps in follow-up imaging attributed to organisational constraints and health service pressures.

result.setting: Outpatient clinics, dental interns, public university (Taibah University)
result.standard: Modified CRABEL scoring system

cycle1.result: 78% of records missing at least one essential component; missing medical history 54%, incomplete dental exam 46%, unsigned 42%; mean CRABEL 56.31 ± 28.2; 21.6% scored ≥80%.

result.intervention: Group presentation, one-to-one instruction and monthly review sessions.

cycle2.result: Missing medical history 16%; unsigned 22%; mean CRABEL 85.47 ± 16.6; 84.6% scored ≥80%.

result.other_findings: 20 interns, averaging 367.8 records reviewed per month.

result.setting: Inpatient child and adolescent psychiatric ward, Child and Adolescent Health Service, Perth
result.standard: 100% adherence to the agitation and arousal chart

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Staff education; results presented in multiple formats.

cycle2.result: Overall improvement across all chart areas; 100% standard met only for medication choice and dose as per guideline.

result.other_findings: 53% to 64% of inpatients were prescribed PRN medication across the two cycles.

result.topic: Appropriate use of serum drug level monitoring
result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Criteria for appropriate use of serum drug assays (digoxin, theophylline, gentamicin, phenytoin) defined by the audit committee and a clinical pharmacist

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Two housestaff conferences, educational materials, an SDA report form for each order and pharmacist discussion with prescribers.

cycle2.result: Appropriate overall use increased significantly (p<0.05), with significant improvement for each criterion.

result.other_findings: An estimated $2500 in patient charges saved against about $260 of pharmacist time over the five-month study.

result.setting: Philadelphia General Hospital Emergency Department
result.standard: Physician panel criteria for management of six chief complaints (provisional standards)

cycle1.result: Cases not meeting standards: chest pain 51% (36), abdominal pain 35% (35), wounds 51% (51), sore throat 43% (22).

cycle2.result: Being tabulated; preliminary findings indicate an improvement in cases meeting criteria.

result.other_findings: Non-physician auditors reviewed records against criteria, with implicit physician review of variances.

result.topic: Superficial cultures in neonatal sepsis work-up
result.setting: Intensive care nursery, secondary level perinatal facility (St Joseph's Hospital, Hamilton, Ontario)
result.standard: Evidence-based hospital protocol to discontinue superficial cultures in neonatal infection assessment

cycle1.result: Superficial cultures performed in 50.5%.

result.intervention: Evidence-based protocol, opinion leader, CME rounds, immediate feedback to physicians and barriers to accessing microbiological tests.
result.other_findings: Cost saving of $4454.84 without patient morbidity.

result.setting: Community leg ulcer clinics, South Bedfordshire
result.standard: Adaptation of the Riverside model (Doppler ABPI assessment and four-layer high compression)

cycle1.result: Average consumable cost per patient £8.53.

result.intervention: Research-based implementation: community clinics, Doppler assessment, compression by ABPI and staff training.

cycle2.result: Average consumable cost £10.14; 111 patients (134 limbs) in high compression had 54% healing at 12 weeks and 68% at 24 weeks.

result.other_findings: Clinic consumable costs £7.91 versus £10.78 at home; weekly treatments and nursing time fell. Healing rates were lower than the Riverside project.

result.topic: Discharge letter quality in acute asthma
result.setting: Specialist respiratory unit, King's Cross Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: Recommendations from a previous audit of acute asthma discharge letters

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Implementation of recommendations from the previous audit.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documentation of precipitating factors (p<0.001), previous admissions (p<0.01), admission ABG (p<0.001), admission peak flow (p<0.05), discharge peak flow (p<0.001), corticosteroid and beta-2 agonist prescription (p<0.01) and inhaler device (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: No change in documentation of acute therapy or follow-up plan; continuing deficiencies identified.

result.setting: District general hospital (Torbay Hospital, Torquay)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 6.4 nights, median 5 nights.

result.intervention: Increased regional anaesthesia, earlier catheter removal and pre-planned discharge.
result.other_findings: Older age, larger resections and late suprapubic catheter removal prolonged stay; social circumstances and detrusor underactivity caused 44% (28/63) of longer stays.

result.setting: Neonatal screening programme, Bath clinical area
result.standard: Locally agreed clinical standards, including treatment of congenital hypothyroidism or phenylketonuria by 28 days

cycle1.result: All eligible babies offered screening; affected babies treated by the 28-day standard.

result.intervention: Annual reports with recommendations communicated to service representatives.
result.other_findings: Areas for improving efficiency were identified.

result.setting: Specialist respiratory centre, King's Cross Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: Documentation of acute asthma severity markers

cycle1.result: PEFR 52%, respiratory rate 44%, ABG 72%, air entry 58%, speech 27%, exhaustion 4%; no patient received FiO2 >0.35.

result.intervention: Severity marker stamp in case notes.

cycle2.result: PEFR 83%, respiratory rate 81%, ABG 80%, air entry 86%, speech 86%, exhaustion 86% (p = 0.001 to 0.04); 66% received FiO2 0.60.

result.other_findings: Mean admission five days; time for pulse to fall to 80/min best predicted length of stay.

result.setting: 22 pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Significant inter-laboratory variability.

result.intervention: Recommendations to improve consistency and national and regional training workshops for laboratory staff.

cycle2.result: Most variables had a coefficient of variation under 5%; improvements for predicted FEV1, TLC, TLCO, FVC, FRC and RV and measured FEV1 and FVC.

result.other_findings: Predicted values from hypothetical subjects still varied unacceptably due to computer algorithm inconsistency; variation increased for predicted KCO and actual RV.

result.topic: Natriuretic peptide testing for heart failure
result.setting: University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust and Devon primary care
result.standard: NICE recommends a stable biomarker such as NTproBNP to detect heart failure

cycle1.result: BNP <100 correctly identified 96% as low likelihood of heart failure with LVSD; 4% (five patients) later had LVEF <50% on echocardiogram.

result.intervention: Switch from BNP to NTproBNP from January 2022.
result.other_findings: Samples had borderline 6-8 hour delays before analysis; re-audit planned.

result.setting: Acute assessment unit, Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 100% of critical medications prescribed within 24 hours of admission (NICE medicines reconciliation)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Posters in medical areas of AAU and A&E.

cycle2.result: 63 (74.1%) had critical medications prescribed by a doctor within 24 hours; 13 of the remaining 22 prescribed by pharmacy; overall compliance 89.4%, a decrease of 5.4%.

result.other_findings: Doctor prescribing improved but pharmacy input fell; opiates, steroids and insulin were most often missed.

result.setting: Adult general psychiatry inpatient unit (Sheffield/Rotherham)
result.standard: DVLA and GMC guidance on fitness to drive

cycle1.result: Driving status established 73% (n = 22); 90% (n = 9) of drivers advised to tell DVLA; 9% (n = 1) advised to tell insurer.

result.intervention: Results presented at Trust-wide teaching and driving status added to the MDT template.

cycle2.result: Driving status established 67% (n = 20); 100% (n = 11) of drivers advised to tell DVLA; 64% (n = 7) advised to tell insurer.

result.other_findings: Discharge letter template later changed to prompt driving assessment; third cycle ongoing.

result.topic: Antipsychotic prescribing in first episode psychosis
result.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis CMHT, Southwark (South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: RCPsych gold standard for treatment of first episode psychosis

cycle1.result: 33% (N = 172) of those on medication not in remission; 85% (N = 68) of these below licensed maximum; 50% (N = 52) treatment resistant; 3.8% (N = 26) of treatment-resistant on clozapine.

result.intervention: One-page flowchart for the multidisciplinary team with an education session.

cycle2.result: 37% (N = 147) not in remission; 76% (N = 55) below licensed maximum; 56% (N = 55) treatment resistant; 9.7% (N = 31) of treatment-resistant on clozapine.

result.other_findings: Clozapine remained underused in treatment-resistant patients.

result.setting: Ritson Outreach (drug and alcohol) Service, Royal Edinburgh Hospital, general psychiatric wards
result.standard: Team-agreed referral criteria and details; target 90% appropriate referrals by March 2025

cycle1.result: Appropriate 55%; contact number 55%; reason for admission 60%; community addictions input 30%; patient aware 20%; drug screen 5%; estimated discharge date 5%.

result.intervention: Referral form with criteria and prompts, sent via automatic email reply.

cycle2.result: Appropriate 80%; contact number 100%; reason for admission 80%; community addictions input 80%; patient aware 60%; drug screen 20%; estimated discharge date 40%.

result.other_findings: Only 10% of surveyed staff felt confident about referral criteria before the form; 90% target not yet met.

result.setting: Male inpatient slow-stream rehabilitation ward, Cumbria Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Practical and pharmacological management options for clozapine-induced hypersalivation from the literature

cycle1.result: All six had hypersalivation; five tried hyoscine tablets first; practical measures such as raising the pillow and chewing gum were not routinely tried.

result.other_findings: Re-audit planned in a year using hypersalivation rating scales.

result.topic: Carer communication in inpatient mental health
result.setting: Junction 17 CAMHS inpatient unit
result.standard: Trust policies on carer contact

cycle1.result: Assigned staff member 58% (7/12); consent documented 8% (1/12); contact within 72 hours 100%; after medication changes 66% (2/3); after incidents 73% (132/180); after home leave 87%; after ward round 47% (51/108).

result.other_findings: Recommendations: key family link staff, standardised PARIS documentation, protected time for carer contact and induction training; re-audit in three months.

result.setting: Acute adult and PICU wards and inpatient drug/alcohol units across four boroughs, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: POMH-UK Quality Improvement Programme 14c standards (five standards, 12 criteria, three targets)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Four of 12 criteria (liver function and glucose tests, acute withdrawal prescription, parenteral thiamine) and all three targets under 60% compliance and below the national sample.

result.other_findings: Second re-audit in the cycle; practice across the trust was variable. Recommends a standard junior doctor admission checklist and breath testing at admission.

result.setting: Children and young people's Community Eating Disorders Service (CEDS), East London NHS Foundation Trust (Tower Hamlets, Newham, City & Hackney)
result.standard: Commissioned target of routine assessment within 2 weeks (urgent within 5 days); national standards 1 week urgent and 4 weeks routine. Aim: reduce routine referral wait from 17 weeks to 2 weeks in 12 months.

cycle1.result: Average wait from routine referral to assessment 17 weeks; 73 patients on psychiatry wait list; 50 families on therapy wait list; 65 inactive cases.

result.intervention: QI with PDSA cycles: weekly referral meeting with referral tracker and 2-week deadline for referrers; single-clinician triage and assessment; revised co-designed referral form; psychiatry wait list review, clinics three mornings a week, joint reviews and medication/prescription clinics; therapy wait list review and capacity planning; monthly caseload audit; shorter 2-page discharge letter; staff recruitment campaign.

cycle2.result: Average routine wait fell to 2 weeks (88% reduction), sustained; psychiatry wait list 73 to 0 by December 2022; therapy wait list 50 to 0 by April 2023; inactive cases 65 to 0.

result.other_findings: Agency staff spend fell from about £130,000 a year to 0 by February 2024; staffing rose from 64% (July 2022) to 77% (April 2023) with no current vacancies.

result.setting: Neurodevelopmental Team, outpatient CAMHS, Brent, Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project aims: reduce time-to-treatment initiation (TTI) for ADHD medication by 10% and increase proportion initiated on medication by 5% by February 2024; NICE NG87 recommends medication as part of a treatment plan.

cycle1.result: Mean TTI 86 days; 64% (n=76) of young people started on ADHD medication; satisfaction 4.13/5 (n=13).

result.intervention: Online post-diagnostic psychoeducation platform (videos, Q&A, e-form medication decision portal with physical health e-form, useful links), emailed to families; QR code posters; text message prompts (PDSA 2); patient experience video (PDSA 3).

cycle2.result: Mean TTI fell to 43 days (n=82) after PDSA 3 (reported elsewhere as 51 days, 41% reduction); 70% (n=52) started on medication; satisfaction 4.37/5 (n=21).

result.other_findings: TTI fell stepwise from 86 to 60 (PDSA 1), 54 (PDSA 2) and 43 days (PDSA 3); about 8 hours of clinician time saved over 2 months.

result.topic: Clinical Frailty Scale accuracy in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (acute general hospital)
result.standard: NHS England CQUIN 05 (2023/24): identify frailty in ED patients aged 65+ using the Clinical Frailty Scale, CGA if CFS 6 or above. SMART target 70% correct identification of CFS 6+ by November 2024; ED nurse scores compared with frailty intervention team scores.

cycle1.result: Correct identification of moderate frailty (CFS 6+) 45–51%; exact CFS accuracy 17%.

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles of ED nurse training: CFS lanyard card to standardise scoring, 1:1 brief teaching (135 sessions), group/virtual sessions, posters, newsletter and emails (cycle 1, November 2023); plus quizzes, scenarios and individual feedback (cycle 2, September to October 2024).

cycle2.result: Correct identification of CFS 6+ rose to 74–78% (78% at 9–13 October 2024); exact CFS accuracy up to 42%.

result.other_findings: After cycle 1 correct identification rose to 70% then ranged 58–68%; exact accuracy rose to 30% but fell back to 17%, so sustainability of accuracy is uncertain.

result.topic: Follow-up chest imaging after community-acquired pneumonia
result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, district general hospital, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston (Weston-super-Mare)
result.standard: BTS and NICE guidance: follow-up chest imaging within six weeks of diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia (patients aged 50 and over and higher-risk patients) to exclude malignancy.

cycle1.result: 22/42 had repeat imaging (X-ray or CT) within six weeks; 16 had none and 4 died before six weeks; 2 cancers found.

result.intervention: Emails to medical and nursing staff summarising audit results and guidelines, posters and banners in clinical areas, patient leaflets in discharge folders, and standardised discharge summary templates with a follow-up imaging prompt.

cycle2.result: 37/50 had repeat imaging; 13 did not; 3 cancers found (all in men).

result.other_findings: Across both cycles 57.89% had chest X-ray as per guidelines and nearly 9% of those re-imaged were diagnosed with cancer; no significant association of follow-up with age or sex.

result.topic: Renal colic imaging and management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: NICE NG118/QS195 (CT-KUB within 24 h, serum calcium), BAUS (CT-KUB within 14 h, calcium and urate, avoid repeat CT within 3 months), RCR iRefer and RCEM four-hour standard. Local targets: four-hour compliance ≥90%; CT-KUB request and report ≤90 min each; >90% scans within imaging windows; STONE score documentation ≥75%; calcium ≥65%, urate ≥20%; ≥30% reduction in repeat CT.

cycle1.result: Median urine dip turnaround 144 min, CT-KUB request 166 min, CT report 124 min; RCEM four-hour compliance 16.7% (19/114); calcium tested 50.9% (58/114); urate 0% (0/114); STONE score 5.3% (6/114); repeat CT within 3 months 19.3%; median ED stay 7.5 h.

result.intervention: 'Straight to CT' pathway with registrar-requested scans, mandatory STONE score prompts in ICE/iRefer requests, three staff training sessions with prompt cards and intranet guides, dedicated porter slots and fast-track radiology queue with hot reporting, early SAU/CDU transfers.

cycle2.result: Urine dip 68 min, CT request 75 min, CT report 70 min (all p<0.001); four-hour compliance 57.0% (65/114; p<0.001); calcium 65.8% (75/114; p=0.022); urate 25.4% (29/114); STONE score 78.9% (90/114); repeat CT 9.6% (p=0.038); ED stay 3.9 h.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic yield rose non-significantly from 57.9% to 68.4% (p=0.090) and alternative diagnoses fell from 11.4% to 7.0%; four-hour compliance remained below the 90% target.

result.setting: Urology operating theatres, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Preston)
result.standard: Trust waste management guidelines (in line with Department of Health guidance), assessed by a pictographic staff question sheet.

cycle1.dates: December 2022 for anaesthetic gas review; question sheet date not stated
cycle1.result: No staff member placed all waste items correctly; commonest score 5/9 (32%); most common error was putting all items in the yellow clinical bin. Of 39 general anaesthetics, sevoflurane used in 30 and desflurane in 7.

result.intervention: 20-minute in-person educational update on waste disposal and the new waste stream during audit days and drop-in sessions, plus wall signage; planned switch from yellow clinical to orange waste stream.

cycle2.result: After education 81% of staff scored 80% or higher (8/10: 24%, 9/10: 36%, 10/10: 21%).

result.other_findings: Trust produced 850 tonnes of clinical waste a year; switching waste stream estimated to save 483,650 kg CO2 and £467,500 a year. Desflurane still used in 18% of general anaesthetics.

result.topic: Nasal bone fracture timeliness of review and manipulation
result.setting: ENT hub (email referrals with telephone triage and rapid access clinic), Ulster Hospital, Dundonald, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: ENT UK and BAOMS guidance: patients requiring reduction of nasal bone fractures assessed and managed within 7–14 days of injury.

cycle1.result: 93% (52/56) referred within 7 days of injury; 63% (35/56) contacted within 7 days of referral; 74% (25/34) seen in clinic within two weeks of injury (82% in abstract); 68% (13/19) had manipulation within 14 days.

result.other_findings: Telephone triage avoided clinic attendance for 39% (22/56). All three paediatric patients needing manipulation under general anaesthetic exceeded 14 days due to theatre capacity.

result.topic: CT sinus reporting for endoscopic sinus surgery (CLOSE criteria)
result.setting: Radiology departments, Victoria Hospital, Kirkcaldy and Queen Margaret Hospital, Dunfermline (NHS Fife health board)
result.standard: CLOSE criteria (Cribriform plate, Lamina papyracea, Onodi cell, Sphenoid sinus pneumatisation, anterior Ethmoidal artery) for pre-FESS CT sinus reports; RCR principle that reports be accurate and complete.

cycle1.result: Full documentation of all CLOSE components 8/51 (15.7%); full compliance in reports with surgically relevant high-risk variants 5/51 (9.8%).

result.intervention: Educational CLOSE poster emailed and displayed in radiology reporting areas (after cycle 1); presentation at departmental radiology meeting and wider poster circulation including to a teleradiology company (after cycle 2).

cycle2.result: Full documentation of all CLOSE components 11/21 (52.4%); high-risk variant compliance 9/21 (42.9%) (χ2=10.375, p<0.01).

result.other_findings: Cycle 2 (July to August 2025, n=20) showed intermediate results. Sphenoid sinus pneumatisation remained least often fully documented (23.81% in cycle 3); 45% of surveyed ENT consultants felt CLOSE only partly sufficient.

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Whiston Hospital, Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (tertiary centre)
result.standard: GIRFT national 30-day readmission benchmarks: 6.1% for elective colonic resections and 8.8% for elective rectal cancer resections.

cycle1.result: 30-day readmission rate 14.2% (4/28), above GIRFT benchmarks; median length of stay 6 days. Causes: blocked catheter/urinary retention, port-site hernia, collection near anastomosis, gastrointestinal symptoms.

result.intervention: Proposed/initiated: ERAS refresher training with quarterly compliance audits, pilot prehabilitation pathway for high-risk patients, virtual telephone follow-up within 7 days of discharge, revised discharge checklists and updated patient leaflets.
result.other_findings: All readmitted patients had length of stay 6 days or less and had robotic anterior resections. Model Health System data showed 12.6% (colonic) and 17.5% (rectal) readmissions in July–September 2024 and 13.1% and 17.6% in October–December 2024; formal re-audit planned.

result.setting: Two Diabetes and Endocrine wards (D1 and D3), Royal Blackburn Teaching Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Nursing documentation standards for daily bowel movement recording using the Bristol Stool Chart (frequency, consistency, correct chart format, escalation/clinical action).

cycle1.dates: April to October 2025 study period (cycle 1 date not stated)
cycle1.result: Daily bowel documentation 8/30 (27%); Bristol Stool Chart used 17 (57%); stool frequency 9 (30%); correct chart format 14 (47%); consistency 15 (50%); clinical action taken 15 (50%).

result.intervention: 'Bowel Matters' reminder posters at workstations, ward areas and toilets; summary to ward manager to cascade; staff advised to add bowel documentation to shift handover checklist and daily nursing care bundles.

cycle2.result: Daily documentation 18 (73%) (χ2 p=0.0092); Bristol Stool Chart 27 (87%) (p=0.0035); frequency 16 (60%); correct chart format 21 (70%, reported elsewhere as 87%); consistency 23 (87%) (p=0.0321); clinical action taken 15 (50%).

result.other_findings: Nurse questionnaire (n=12) identified time constraints and forgetfulness as main causes. Changes were then spread to older people's, rehabilitation and stroke wards.

result.topic: Critical care follow-up and recovery experiences
result.setting: Adult Critical Care Unit, Royal London Hospital (large adult critical care service), within evaluation of a pilot follow-up service
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews with 16 survivors and 7 clinicians; shared themes of uncertain recovery, fragmented care and psychological impact, with differing perceptions of timing and responsibility.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend earlier discussion of recovery expectations, clinicians acting as care navigators, and better integration of health and social care.

result.topic: Antibiotic use for suspected early onset neonatal infection
result.setting: Neonatal unit and transitional care unit, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary neonatal service)
result.standard: NICE NG195 neonatal infection guideline and Kaiser Permanente Neonatal Infection Calculator (KPNIC); aim to reduce antibiotic initiation and duration in low-risk infants.

cycle1.result: 13% of live births started on antibiotics for suspected EONI in 2018; 12.4% of live births >35 weeks in 2019; 1089 transitional care cefotaxime care days in 2019.

result.intervention: Five PDSA cycles: CRP threshold raised to 20 mg/L to stop antibiotics at 36 hours in well culture-negative infants ('20 is the new 10'); GBS-positive mothers added to KPNIC; use of KPNIC risk after clinical exam rather than risk at birth; background EONI rate changed to 1/1000; KPNIC extended to 34 weeks. Supported by guideline updates, teaching, posters, emails and newsletters.

cycle2.result: 6.8% of live births >34 weeks on antibiotics in 2024 and 6.6% in 2025 (to 30 June); transitional care cefotaxime days fell to 270 in 2024 (75% reduction).

result.other_findings: No infant given a shortened course with CRP 10–20 or not started on antibiotics re-presented with infection within 14 days. Neonatal unit antibiotic care days stayed static at 110–120 a month.

result.topic: Topical lidocaine for paediatric airway procedures
result.setting: Paediatric anaesthesia department, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary paediatric centre); survey of consultant paediatric anaesthetists
result.standard: Advocated standards based on APAGBI guidance and published evidence: maximum topical lidocaine dose 4.0 mg/kg at concentration ≤4%; nil-by-mouth 60 minutes after topicalisation; mucosal atomisation device as standard.

cycle1.result: Median self-reported maximum dose 3.0 mg/kg (range 2.0–9.0); 2/22 (9.1%) used the 4.0 mg/kg standard; median NBM time 120 minutes (range 60–360), 8/22 (36.4%) adherent; Jelco device 18/22 (81.8%), MAD 14/22 (63.6%).

result.intervention: 45-minute structured teaching session within mandatory departmental teaching presenting survey findings, complications and advocated guidelines.

cycle2.result: Median maximum dose 4.0 mg/kg; 8/15 (53.3%) used 4.0 mg/kg (p=0.006); median NBM 60 minutes, 11/15 (73.3%) adherent (p=0.045); Jelco 12/15 (80.0%), MAD 10/15 (66.7%), unchanged.

result.other_findings: Wide dose variation (2.0–9.0 mg/kg) persisted and device choice did not change. No respondent used concentrations above 4%; incidents were rare and not linked to practice variables.

result.setting: Post-Anaesthesia Care Unit (main and burns theatres), Chelsea and Westminster Hospital (large tertiary hospital)
result.standard: NICE delirium guidance: high-risk patients (age over 65, cognitive impairment, hip fracture) screened with a validated tool (4AT or CAM) before PACU discharge. Target at least 50% adherence within 1 month of launch.

cycle1.result: 3/130 (2.3%) at-risk patients screened for delirium in PACU; nurse confidence median 7/10 and guideline clarity median 4/10.

result.intervention: PDSA 1: new trust-wide perioperative delirium guideline. PDSA 2: 4AT made easily accessible on electronic systems, PACU discharge checklist updated to require screening, simplified guidance signposted, daily list review at morning huddles to flag at-risk patients, staff education, and leadership engagement using coding/funding data.

cycle2.result: 48/67 (71.64%) at-risk patients screened (p<0.0001); 81.50% in final week; nurse confidence and guideline clarity both median 10/10 (p<0.0001).

result.other_findings: PDSA cycle 1 (29 March to 12 April 2025) screening 15/49 (30.61%). Of 63 screened, 11 (17.46%) scored 4+ suggesting delirium; medical team pathway for positive screens not yet formalised.

result.setting: Learning disability female low secure forensic unit, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust and national guidelines on psychotropic prescribing and monitoring (indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment and capacity forms, annual health check, blood monitoring, annual valproate risk acknowledgement form).

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment forms, annual health check and psychotropic blood monitoring; MHA capacity assessment form 71%; annual valproate risk acknowledgement form in women of childbearing age 0%.

result.other_findings: Investigation results were hard to locate. Recommendations: care plans for all patients on valproate with review dates for risk acknowledgement forms and consistent filing of results.

result.topic: PTSD treatment in people experiencing homelessness
result.setting: Inner-city homelessness health service (University of Manchester affiliation)
result.standard: National guidance recommending trauma-focused psychological therapies for PTSD.

cycle1.result: 11% of individuals received some form of psychological therapy; medication was the main treatment.

result.other_findings: Commonest reasons for unsuccessful therapy were lack of contact or engagement, discharge because of substance misuse, and missing records or follow-up.

result.topic: Ethnic inequalities in perinatal mental health service access
result.setting: Perinatal Mental Health Services, Southwark (South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists gold standards for equitable access to perinatal mental health care.

cycle1.result: Ethnicity not documented in 6.6% of referrals; no clear inequity at referral, but 3 of 4 admissions (75%) were Black women and all detained; only 2/35 Asian and Mixed ethnicity women referred for psychology; 83% (5/6) of antipsychotics prescribed to Black women; 48% of 31 safeguarding alerts involved Black women.

result.other_findings: Authors concluded the service was not meeting RCPsych gold standards for equitable care.

result.standard: NICE NG97 (June 2018) Dementia guideline and local trust guidance on antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring.

cycle1.result: 88% had assessment of sources of distress; 42% had non-pharmacological intervention before antipsychotic (58% after starting); 63% risk discussion documented; 63% baseline bloods; 54% baseline ECG; 33% of those treated over 12 weeks had discontinuation or dose-reduction trial; under 22% had physical health monitoring at one year.

result.other_findings: Random sample of 24 from 55 patients. Recommended a pre-prescribing checklist and a system to flag when monitoring and review are due.

result.setting: Adult inpatient psychiatry ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health trust (Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust affiliation)
result.standard: NICE guidance on monitoring patients on long-term antipsychotics (14 standards: BMI, ECG, blood pressure, lipids, prolactin, urea and electrolytes at baseline, set time points and dose changes).

cycle1.result: 5 of 14 standards attained, 7 not attained, 1 partially analysed and 1 (12-month monitoring) not analysable.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: comprehensive admission proforma, reminder tool for 3, 6 and 12-month rechecks, and regular ECG machine maintenance.

result.topic: Baseline physical health checks before starting antipsychotics
result.setting: Intensive Home Treatment Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust Antipsychotic Physical Health Monitoring Shared Care Guidelines.

cycle1.result: 32% had a full physical health check before antipsychotic initiation, 56% incomplete; no individual investigation fully compliant; BMI/weight least completed, HbA1c least completed blood test; 40% had results reviewed by a relevant professional.

result.other_findings: Diet and physical activity were recorded less often than illicit drug use and smoking status. Results shared with the team.

result.setting: Pine Ward, 17-bed male low secure forensic inpatient ward, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidance: mandatory ALL-Physical Health Assessment on admission and six-monthly (14 categories).

cycle1.result: 76.4% of patients had ALL done; 67.2% of completions green, 15.5% amber, 17.2% red; QRISK 70%, alcohol 58%, diet 82%, exercise 70%, diabetes 58%, smoking 76%.

cycle2.result: 15/17 (88%) had ALL in last 6 months; 89.9% of completions green, 4.6% amber, 5.5% red; QRISK, alcohol, diet and exercise 100%; diabetes 82%, smoking 88%.

result.other_findings: Some areas still below expected standard; authors recommend raising importance of the assessment with trainees.

result.topic: Safety plans for high intensity users of mental health services
result.setting: Section 136 suite, liaison psychiatry and inpatient wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: Aim that high intensity users of acute mental health services have a person-centred safety plan in place.

cycle1.result: More than 80% had a safety plan but plans lacked detail to avert crisis; EUPD commonest diagnosis (77%); 93% on CPA.

result.intervention: QI with process mapping, driver diagram, co-production and focus groups: additional 'HIU response plan' template, best practice example for care coordinators, process to flag HIUs to community teams.

cycle2.result: HIU response plans incorporated into the safety plans of 20/26 HIUs.

result.other_findings: PDSA ongoing; quality and effectiveness of changes still to be reviewed.

result.setting: Stroud Recovery community mental health service, Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance: antipsychotics not recommended for EUPD and should be reviewed with aim of reducing and stopping.

cycle1.result: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication; mean duration 36.79 months; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic; only 10 (42%) had prescriptions reviewed to stop or reduce; none offered routine physical review.

result.other_findings: Subgroup without licensed indication mostly female (75%) and aged 20–29 (46%); quetiapine most used.

result.setting: Community Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service team, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Licensed use per Summary of Product Characteristics and NICE, BAP and BNFc guidance.

cycle1.result: 177 prescriptions: 25% prescribed within licence; 42% compatible with NICE, 62% with BAP, 67% with BNFc; 12% deviated from all guidance (mirtazapine 1, melatonin 9, quetiapine 6, risperidone 1, olanzapine 4).

result.other_findings: 88% of prescriptions were supported by licence or at least one guideline; unsupported prescriptions were linked with higher comorbidity.

result.setting: Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust, five-borough mental health trust
result.standard: Aim to improve trainee confidence in remote psychiatric assessments by at least 40%; local audit of consent documentation against NHS England remote consultation guidance

cycle1.result: 2/34 had accessed previous remote consultation training; 12/35 had telepsychiatry experience. Pre-induction confidence: extremely uncomfortable 16%, not confident 31%, neutral 47%, confident 6%, very confident 0%

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: trust-wide video presentation of a 'top tips' article, targeted August 2020 induction session, then February 2021 induction with presentation and video-simulated remote consultation, with real-time app data collection

cycle2.result: Post-induction confidence: extremely uncomfortable 0%, not confident 22%, neutral 52%, confident 26%, very confident 0%; 'confident' improved from 6% to 26%

Mean wait for initial appointment 22 days (range 0-65); mean 20 days from starting medication to follow-up (range 8-37)

result.setting: Clock View Hospital, adult inpatient unit, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Mersey Care EUPD prescribing guidelines

cycle1.result: With comorbidities (n=25): 80% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication, 4 of 7 new prescriptions followed guidelines. result.other_findings: Antipsychotic prescribing higher without comorbidities (72% vs 60%); benzodiazepines were the most common PRN medication. Suggested promethazine as first-line PRN and psychological interventions before medication.
