result.topic: Mental Health Act assessment and bed delays
result.setting: Liaison and Diversion Service, Willesden Magistrates Court, North West London
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice: up to 14 days between medical recommendation and conveyance to hospital; local standard that all defendants liable to detention are admitted on the same day

cycle1.result: 42 MHA assessments requested; 25 detained under Section 2. Referral-to-assessment time (available in 25/42) ranged 1.5 to 22 hours; 2 remanded overnight as assessment not same day. Beds not available same day in 7/25; 4 remanded in prison custody for lack of bed

result.other_findings: Medical recommendations completed within 5 days and admissions within 14 days, so Code of Practice standards met, but defendants still remanded to custody. Data missing for some referrals.

result.setting: Carseview Centre psychiatric hospital (3 adult wards, 1 intensive psychiatric care unit, 1 learning disability unit), NHS Tayside
result.standard: Local NHS Tayside Emergency Equipment Protocol (updated November 2020)

cycle1.result: Resuscitation trolleys often lacked ligature packs; masks generally not by oxygen cylinders; hypoglycaemia dextro-tablets not readily available; learning disability unit had no emergency resuscitation trolley

result.intervention: Feedback to wards, multidisciplinary meetings, amendment of the local protocol (not reviewed since 2012) finalised November 2020, and a list of recommendations

cycle2.result: All first-cycle recommendations implemented; some equipment still incomplete or missing on individual wards but none consistently missing across the site

result.other_findings: Additional items (nebuliser and non-rebreather masks) were mostly stocked but difficult to locate. Numbers not reported.

result.setting: 14-bed specialist dementia ward, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: NICE dementia guidance: structured assessment, psychosocial interventions first line, antipsychotics second line for shortest time and reviewed at least every 6 weeks

cycle1.result: Mean psychotropics per patient 2.30 on admission, 2.30 at midpoint, 2.05 at discharge; mean diazepam equivalent fell from 3.20 mg to 2.10 mg; mean haloperidol equivalent rose from 1.11 mg to 2.27 mg at midpoint then fell to 0.78 mg at discharge

result.other_findings: 95% (n = 19) admitted under the Mental Health Act. Authors state changes in antipsychotic and benzodiazepine use were consistent with NICE guidelines.

result.setting: Four Teesside Child and Adolescent community teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: TEWV ADHD prescribing guidelines and NICE NG87 (2018)

cycle1.result: Verbal information 92% and written 58%; pre-treatment assessment in all but 3 cases; methylphenidate not first line in 4 cases (3 atomoxetine by parental choice, 1 contraindication); lisdexamfetamine used second line in 75%

result.other_findings: Good practice in diagnostic recording and non-medication interventions. Updated NICE-compliant trust guidance and a trust-wide re-audit planned.

result.setting: Cardiff Health Access Practice, primary care for refugees and asylum seekers
result.standard: All Wales / Cardiff and Vale Traumatic Stress Service pharmacological PTSD prescribing algorithm (based on NICE and ISTSS guidelines)

cycle1.result: 10/130 started on first-line medication; 117 on fourth-line medication; none on second- or third-line

result.other_findings: Algorithm not yet fully introduced; discussion of results and teaching for clinicians planned.

result.setting: English national audit (University Hospitals of Bristol, Croydon, Imperial, UCLH)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only; no abstract available.

result.setting: 750-bed acute hospital, south-west England (Royal Cornwall Hospital), medical specialties
result.standard: APRHAI national audit tool for appropriate antibiotic prescribing

cycle1.result: 184/647 (28%) patients audited; total 1658 days of therapy of which 403 (24%) excess. Excess by timepoint: initiation 112 (28%), pre-72 h review 184 (46%), course length 107 (27%). 94 of 187 (50%) had zero excess days

result.other_findings: Most excess antibiotic days occurred at the pre-72 hour review.

result.topic: Management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
result.setting: Pyrland Two ward, organic old age psychiatry inpatient unit, Somerset NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE criteria for BPSD management and antipsychotic prescribing

cycle1.result: 4/14 formally diagnosed with BPSD; 6/14 on antipsychotics, of which 1/6 fully met NICE standards; 2/14 had structured assessment tools used

result.intervention: PDSA cycles with a ward-round checklist and staff education

cycle2.result: 8/8 formally diagnosed with BPSD; 7/8 on antipsychotics, of which 4/7 fully met NICE standards; 7/8 had structured assessment tools used

result.other_findings: Small numbers; further PDSA cycles suggested for sustainability.

result.topic: CAMHS crisis team activity during COVID-19
result.setting: Alliance CAMHS team, West London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 188 referrals; 55% (102) minority ethnic; 26% (49) male; 58% (109) seen within 24 hours; 6% had telephone support; 44% (72) signposted

cycle2.result: 161 referrals; 50% (80) minority ethnic; 18% (30) male; 61% (99) seen within 24 hours; no telephone support; 52% (85) signposted

result.other_findings: Descriptive comparison of service activity; no standard or intervention. Recommended annual audits and improved data collection.

result.setting: 8 acute adult inpatient wards, Nottingham Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and local guidance on prolactin monitoring and management of hyperprolactinaemia

cycle1.result: Of 41 on regular antipsychotics, 19 had no prolactin assay during admission; 44.4% of antipsychotic-naive patients had baseline prolactin; hyperprolactinaemia in 9; 9.1% with hyperprolactinaemia had symptoms assessed; 27.3% had actions taken

result.other_findings: 78 records screened. Need to raise clinician awareness of prolactin monitoring.

result.topic: Smoking cessation in mental health services
result.setting: Community secondary mental health service, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 44% (n = 40) smokers; 31 offered smoking cessation advice (2 recorded as wanting to quit); NRT offered to 13; 5 referred to stop smoking services

result.other_findings: Survey: 20/31 smokers wanted to reduce or quit. Local GPs did not prescribe NRT and targeted services existed only for inpatients.

result.setting: 17-bed functional Old Age Psychiatry ward, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 90% compliance with each section of the electronic admission pro forma based on Royal College of Psychiatrists admission guidelines

cycle1.result: Pre-pandemic baseline; figures by domain not reported

result.intervention: No planned intervention; repeated across early (2020, n = 29) and late (2021) pandemic periods

cycle2.result: All domains improved from 2019 to 2021 except mental state examination (9.09% decrease, not significant); 4 domains significantly improved; 9 domains still below the 90% standard

result.other_findings: Late pandemic better than early pandemic in 10 domains, worse in 4 and equal in 6.

result.setting: Medium secure forensic hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE: all patients with psychosis offered CBTp with at least 16 sessions

cycle1.result: 68% (19/28) offered CBTp; 85% (11/13) completed at least 16 sessions

result.other_findings: Barriers to offering: not mentally well enough (7/9), in other therapies (2/9); barrier to completion: patient refusal (2/2).

result.setting: Forensic community mental health team, supported accommodation, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE Guideline (2014) Obesity: identification, assessment and intervention

cycle1.result: 10/12 (83%) overweight or obese; waist circumference measured in 4; all overweight or obese patients received lifestyle advice; QRISK calculated for most eligible patients except two

result.other_findings: One patient pre-diabetic and one diabetic identified.

result.setting: 20-bed acute mixed adult inpatient ward, South West London and St George's NHS Mental Health Trust
result.standard: NICE: 4-6 week trial of antipsychotic at optimal dosage before change

cycle1.result: Mean time from start of inpatient treatment to first change 11.6 days, first to second 13.8 days, second to third 16.0 days; changes due to inadequate response 84.6%, side effects 9.6%, adherence 5.8%; counselling attempted for initial changes in 73%

result.other_findings: Antipsychotics were changed more quickly than NICE advises. Olanzapine (33%) was the most commonly initiated antipsychotic.

result.setting: Acute adult psychiatric wards (male, female, PICU), Highbury Hospital, Nottingham
result.standard: Trust policy: all eligible patients should be offered COVID-19 vaccine

cycle1.result: 31% (n = 105) vaccinated or planned before admission; 43% (n = 100) of 234 unvaccinated patients offered vaccine; 59% (n = 59) of those offered accepted; 92% (n = 55) of acceptors received it

result.other_findings: Sectioned patients and those in psychotic clusters were more likely to refuse. Acceptance (59%) lower than national (80%).

result.setting: Male and female acute inpatient units, Zinnia Centre, Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Foundation Trust
result.standard: BSMHFT admissions policy standards for pre-referral assessment

cycle1.result: Assessed by full MHA team 49%, senior psychiatric doctor 34%; up-to-date assessment summary 67%; risk assessment 82%; detailed plan of care meeting standards 35%; capacity assessment with outcome 13%; bed type considered 13%

result.other_findings: 83 male and 82 female admissions reviewed.

result.setting: Burlington House, Sefton community CAMHS, Alder Hey NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE (sleep hygiene and behavioural therapy first line; CG170) and BNFC (review melatonin every 6 months)

cycle1.result: 18 insomnia with ASD, 26 without ASD, 3 likely ASD; all received melatonin at recommended dose with 6-monthly reviews; sleep hygiene documentation unclear

result.other_findings: 36 reviewed by specialist CAMHS, 9 by community paediatrics, 2 by GP.

result.setting: James Cook University Hospital acute hospital and South Tees Liaison Psychiatry team
result.standard: Trust lithium guidelines; target 100% staff awareness

cycle1.result: Aware renal and thyroid checks needed 96% (24/25); impact on eGFR 84% (21/25); toxicity signs 68% (17/25); referral to liaison psychiatry 60% (15/25); interacting drugs 40% (10/25); checking lithium level on admission 24% (6/25). Average 57% positive responses

result.other_findings: Staff knowledge questionnaire rather than case-note review. Teaching sessions planned.

result.setting: West Kent community perinatal mental health team, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: JCVI and RCOG guidance recommending COVID-19 vaccination in pregnancy

cycle1.result: 59% (n = 51) had both doses, 12% (n = 10) a single dose, 29% (n = 25) unvaccinated (17 pregnant, 8 postnatal)

result.intervention: Unvaccinated women contacted and offered the RCOG information sheet and decision aid

cycle2.result: After contact, 39% (n = 9) accepted the vaccine, 52% (n = 12) refused and 26% (n = 6) were uncertain

result.other_findings: Hesitancy reasons included lack of trust, rapid development, side effects in associates and doubts about efficacy.

result.topic: Psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
result.setting: Crisis Team, Fieldhead Hospital, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines on psychotropic prescribing, baseline investigations and monitoring

cycle1.result: 100% for indication, dosage, discussion and side-effect monitoring; 46/50 responded to treatment. Of 22 on antipsychotics, 11 had ECG and bloods by the Crisis Team, 4 by others, 3 bloods but no ECG, 2 no physical health monitoring with no reason documented

result.other_findings: 8/50 reported side effects, mostly with antidepressants. Physical health monitoring needs improvement.

result.setting: Early Intervention for Psychosis team, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: DVLA guidance on documenting driving status and advice

cycle1.result: Diagnosis documented 95% (n = 38); driving status 67.5% (n = 27); among drivers, vehicle type 33% (5), told condition may affect driving 33% (n = 5), driving restrictions advice 67% (n = 10), legal duty to inform DVLA 47% (n = 7)

result.other_findings: Recommended training, including driving in structured initial assessments, and patient leaflets.

result.topic: High risk care plans in liaison psychiatry
result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local guidance: 100% completion of appropriate high risk care plans with all mandatory fields (no national guideline)

cycle1.result: 11 plans completed with 2 more required but missing; non-pharmacological de-escalation 2/11; regular medication 5/11; rapid tranquillisation advice 8/11; absconsion risk 8/11; observation level 10/11

result.other_findings: Plans appropriate for 4.6% of caseload but present for 3.9%. Staff survey showed unfamiliarity with the document.

result.setting: Wards D15, D17 and D27, City Hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Liaison referral pathway and NHS England guidelines on referral structure

cycle1.result: Insufficient presenting complaint 77.8% (n = 14); no past psychiatric history 22.2% (n = 4); insufficient MSE 94.4% (n = 17); no detailed risk assessment 83.3% (n = 15); no drug/alcohol history 27.8% (n = 5); no consent 22.2% (n = 4)

result.other_findings: Possible knowledge gap among non-psychiatric trainees in psychiatric history, risk and MSE.

result.topic: Psychotropic medication review in learning disability and autism
result.setting: Scottish GP practice (NHS Tayside)
result.standard: Annual medication review for antipsychotics and antidepressants in patients with learning disability or autism (Public Health England concern)

cycle1.result: 10/12 on antipsychotics and 19/20 on antidepressants had a medication review within 12 months

result.other_findings: Further audit of annual blood tests suggested.

result.setting: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, psychiatry, GP and foundation trainees
result.standard: Severn Deanery and trust recommendation: one hour of supervision per week

cycle1.result: Response rate 63%; 17% meeting supervisor only sometimes; 89% able to complete WPBAs; QI/audit discussed 66%; 42% of psychiatry trainees had some discussion of psychotherapy competencies

result.intervention: Results presented at local teaching and audit meetings

cycle2.result: 9/27 responded (33%); 11% meeting supervisor only sometimes; WPBAs 88%; QI/audit discussed 60%; 75% discussing psychotherapy competencies

result.other_findings: Most trainees satisfied, but supervision needs protecting from clinical work.

result.setting: Small district general hospital, Southport and Ormskirk Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours for biliary colic and cholecystitis, within 2 weeks for gallstone pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Biliary colic (9 pre-COVID, 5 during COVID): none had LC within 72 hours. Cholecystitis (20 pre-COVID, 16 during COVID): none within 72 hours; 5 per group had LC, with longer waits during COVID. Gallstone pancreatitis: only 1 had LC within 2 weeks

result.other_findings: Delays caused readmissions and complications; limited ultrasound, staff and theatre access. A hot gallbladder service with dedicated theatre slots recommended.

result.setting: IBD service, St Mark's Hospital, London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Locally agreed standards for extended 6-monthly blood monitoring during COVID-19 (ECCO advises 3-monthly)

cycle1.result: 54% (n = 50) had extended blood monitoring, of whom 43 (86%) were eligible; one had raised ALT that improved after a treatment break; one advice-line call for side effects; no admissions due to deranged bloods or adverse effects

result.other_findings: Temporary relaxation of monitoring did not appear to affect safety; repeat with larger sample suggested.

result.topic: Pain education in sickle cell disease
result.setting: Department of Haematology, Cambridge University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only; no abstract available.

result.topic: Psychological needs assessment in sickle cell disease
result.setting: North Middlesex University Hospital and Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only (baseline audit of ASCQ-Me psychometric tool use); no abstract available.

result.setting: University Hospitals Leicester
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only: retrospective comparison reporting weekly bortezomib better tolerated and equally efficient as twice-weekly; no abstract available.

result.topic: Pancreatic enzyme replacement in pancreatic cancer
result.setting: National primary care records, OpenSAFELY-TPP platform (24 million records)
result.standard: UK guidelines: PERT for all people with unresectable pancreatic cancer (100% standard)

cycle1.result: National PERT prescribing rates rose from 41% in 2015 to 48% in early 2023 (about 1% per year); highest regional rates 50% to 60% in West Midlands

result.other_findings: Prescribing was not affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. An automated audit allowing regular updates was developed.

result.setting: Secondary mental health care, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Technical feasibility study of the VIEWER electronic audit and feedback platform tested in three psychosis clinical use cases.

result.setting: 188 UK hospital sites accepting unplanned medical attendances (Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 29.8% of unplanned medical attendances initially assessed in SDEC, increasing over time; 82.4% of SDEC patients discharged without overnight admission

result.other_findings: SDEC assessment less likely in men, frail and older patients. Participation higher in England than other UK nations.

result.setting: Christie Cancer Centre, Manchester, and referring hospitals
result.standard: National and international guidelines for initial surgery and staging of ovarian cancer

cycle1.result: 92% presented via outpatient clinic (elective surgery); up to seven consultants per hospital operated; less than half underwent the recommended surgical procedure

result.other_findings: Surgery was spread across many consultants, each treating few patients.

result.topic: Breast cancer in family history clinic attenders
result.setting: Aberdeen Genetic Clinic
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only; no abstract available.

result.setting: 28 specialist cancer centres
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 33% required at least one transfusion (19% breast to 43% lung); 16% more than one; proportion with Hb < 11 g/dl rose from 17% before the first cycle to 38% by the sixth; 25% of transfused patients needed inpatient admission

result.other_findings: 3206 chemotherapy courses for breast, ovary, lung or testis tumours; descriptive audit with no standard.

result.setting: North and South Staffordshire Acute and Community Trusts, maternity services
result.standard: Established standards for childbirth complications (not specified)

cycle1.result: Questionnaire response 48% (470/970). At 9-14 months: dyspareunia 29% (102/347), urinary incontinence 35% (133/382), faecal incontinence 4% (17 women)

result.other_findings: High obstetric intervention rates and different instrumental delivery rates between hospitals. Recommended better patient information, communication and management of third degree tears.

result.setting: Antenatal clinic, North Staffordshire Maternity Hospital, Stoke on Trent
result.standard: Set audit standard on women's awareness of blood transfusion in pregnancy (CEMD report); target not stated

cycle1.result: Response rate 100%; 43% aware of possible need for transfusion in pregnancy; 92% would accept transfusion; 4% would refuse for religious reasons or infection risk; 4% gave no reason

result.other_findings: Recommended identifying women who would refuse transfusion at booking for counselling and a management plan.

result.setting: 15 UK centres
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 29% had a neutropenic event; only 5.2% received G-CSF; 17% did not achieve 85% of planned dose intensity (11% due to neutropenia)

result.other_findings: Patients with one neutropenic event had a higher risk of a second.

result.topic: Critical care case mix and outcomes database
result.setting: 128 adult general critical care units in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (ICNARC Case Mix Programme)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean database quality level 3.4 of 4 against Directory of Clinical Databases criteria; unit mortality 20.3% and hospital mortality 30.8%; mean APACHE II 16.5

result.other_findings: Describes data collection and validation methods of the national database.

result.setting: Accident and Emergency departments of two northern district general hospitals in one NHS trust
result.standard: NICE head injury guidelines, CT scan indicators

cycle1.result: GCS recorded in 58%; 33 (8%) admitted; only four of ten CT indicators routinely assessed, complete for only one (age) and largely absent for vomiting

result.other_findings: Applying three indicators suggested a likely 4-fold increase in CT demand.

result.setting: East of Scotland (Tayside) Cancer Registry
result.standard: Histopathology records as gold standard for ICD coding

cycle1.result: Few major coding errors; minor and moderate differences due to coding system structure and data retrieval

result.other_findings: Level of detail required by the registry needs evaluation.

result.topic: Hospital palliative care team quality assurance
result.setting: Nine hospital palliative care teams, Trent region (Trent Hospice Audit Group)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Development of standards and audit tools for hospital palliative care teams over three rounds of consultation and piloting.

result.setting: Urology outpatient clinics, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Management changed in 47 patients, most often due to PSA trend; change in DRE findings led to earlier review in 2

result.other_findings: Supports nurse-led follow-up reserving DRE for PSA change or new symptoms.

result.setting: West of Scotland Cancer Centre, Beatson Oncology Centre, Glasgow
result.standard: Builds on Clinical Resource and Audit Group (CRAG) work; standard not specified

cycle1.result: Poor pain assessment, poor ambulatory status on admission and no clear mobilisation or rehabilitation plans for most patients

result.other_findings: Recommended regional guidelines and a care pathway, taken forward through the West of Scotland Cancer Network.

result.topic: Thrombolysis times and secondary prevention after myocardial infarction
result.setting: All hospitals in the Myocardial Infarction National Audit Project (n = 230)
result.standard: National Service Framework standards for door-to-needle and call-to-needle times and aspirin, beta-blocker and statin use

cycle1.result: 163 hospitals met door-to-needle standards; 116 fell outside call-to-needle standards (28 below lower control limit); 16 failed aspirin standard (24 below lower control limit); 49 outside beta-blocker standard (30 below lower control limit); statin use comparable

result.other_findings: Demonstrates funnel plots for comparing hospital performance.

result.setting: Scottish breast cancer family clinics
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 28 invasive breast cancers observed vs 14.4 expected (relative risk 1.94), above the 1.7 cut-off for surveillance

result.other_findings: Highest risk at ages 45-59; NICE criteria appeared more accurate than SIGN for defining moderate risk.

result.topic: ICU outcome prediction scores after in-hospital cardiac arrest
result.setting: Two adult ICUs (Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge; Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Hospital mortality 58.6%; ICNARC AUC 0.734 vs APACHE II 0.706; both weaker in patients aged 69 or under (ICNARC AUC 0.655 vs 0.810; APACHE II 0.660 vs 0.759).

result.other_findings: Retrospective observational comparison of scoring systems, not an audit against a standard.

result.setting: European COPD audit, 384 hospitals in 13 European countries
result.standard: GOLD 2010 recommendations for antibiotic use in COPD exacerbations

cycle1.result: 86% of admissions received antibiotics but only 61.4% of cases met the GOLD recommendations.

result.other_findings: Patients on a respiratory ward were more likely to receive GOLD-compliant antibiotic management; antibiotics were more likely if received before admission, with apparent overuse overall.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: No abstract available; title describes the value of clinical audit to improve cataract quality.

result.setting: Two tertiary ophthalmology institutions in a large South African city
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews: quality assurance relied on trainee logbooks and subjective senior observation; self-audit encouraged but not obligatory.

result.other_findings: No structures were described to detect surgeons with higher than expected complication rates; audits were not enforced.

result.setting: Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Surrey, acute hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Piperacillin/tazobactam (n=98) vs amoxicillin+temocillin (n=94): clinical success 80% vs 82% (P = 0.86); significant diarrhoea 34% vs 4% (P < 0.0001); CDI 7% vs 0% (P < 0.0028).

result.intervention: Formulary change replacing piperacillin/tazobactam with amoxicillin+temocillin for empirical treatment of severe hospital-acquired pneumonia.
result.other_findings: Retrospective comparison of outcomes of two regimens (192 episodes in 188 patients) rather than compliance with a standard.

result.setting: Four public and private primary health-care facilities, Eastern Region, Ghana
result.standard: WHO/International Network for the Rational Use of Drugs rational drug use indicators

cycle1.result: Mean 4.01 medicines per encounter; 59.9% of prescriptions had antibiotics and 24.2% injections; 79.2% of medicines were generics and 88.1% from the national essential medicines list.

result.other_findings: 400 prescriptions sampled per facility; facility type, age, number of medicines, no malaria drug and upper respiratory tract infection diagnosis were associated with antibiotic prescription.

result.setting: Tertiary breast service unit, North West London, single centre
result.standard: Professional guidelines on medical chaperones (documentation of chaperone offer, patient preference, chaperone identity and clinician gender)

cycle1.result: not reported (baseline figures not given in the abstract).

result.intervention: Cycle 1: presentation and discussion of chaperone guidelines, reminder posters and introduction of a note stamp; cycle 2: note stamp alone.

cycle2.result: After first intervention (November 2013) documentation of chaperone offer was 69.95%; final cycle result not given in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Three-stage project (baseline October 2013, re-audits November 2013 and October 2014), at least 155 encounters per cycle; authors conclude a proforma stamp embedded in documentation is effective.

result.topic: Core outcome set for breast reconstruction
result.setting: BRAVO study, multicentre UK stakeholders
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 303 participants (51.4%) returned round 1; 259 (85.5%) completed round 2; core outcome set of 11 key outcomes agreed.

result.other_findings: Delphi consensus study, not an audit.

result.setting: European COPD Audit, 384 hospitals in 13 European countries
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 2,714 (19.2%) had consolidation; these patients were more likely to receive antibiotics, oxygen and NIV and had lower survival to 90 days.

result.other_findings: Secondary analysis of audit data reporting outcomes and associations only.

result.topic: Cardiovascular disease prevention recording in primary care
result.setting: 14 rural general practices
result.standard: Recording of cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle advice for high-risk patients and those with cardiovascular disease

cycle1.result: High-risk vs diagnosed: blood pressure recorded 94% vs 99% (P = 0.019); physical activity 24% vs 56%; dietary advice 32% vs 51% (P = 0.001); physical activity advice 34% vs 56%.

result.other_findings: Recording of risk factors was positively associated with practice involvement in quality improvement.

result.topic: Laboratory processing of children's urine samples for UTI
result.setting: Microbiology laboratories in England with Clinical Pathology Accreditation; six laboratories in south-west England
result.standard: NICE CG54 (2007) urinary tract infection in children: urgent microscopy and culture, reporting of non-E. coli infections

cycle1.result: 73% of laboratories (110/150) participated; 61% (67/110) reported non-E. coli Enterobacteriaceae only as coliforms; 88% (97/110) provided urgent microscopy for hospital and 54% for GP urines; only 22% (24/110) reported non-E. coli coliforms and provided urgent microscopy for both.

result.other_findings: Less than a quarter of laboratories provided a service allowing full compliance; only one of six laboratories had a significant increase in paediatric urine submissions after the guidance.

result.setting: 96 stores selling tobacco in 4 Scottish communities
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: E-cigarette display units and brands increased between waves; e-cigarettes displayed close to products of interest to children in 36% of stores.

result.other_findings: Observational retail audit and retailer interviews, not a clinical audit against a standard.

result.setting: Bottleneck analysis in 12 countries in Africa and Asia
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Health information systems (11 countries), essential medical products (9 of 11) and service delivery (9 of 11) had significant or very major bottlenecks.

result.other_findings: Health system bottleneck analysis; recommends audit and feedback as part of quality improvement.

result.topic: Metabolic screening for patients on antipsychotics
result.setting: Adult assertive outreach community psychiatric services, POMH-UK programme
result.standard: Evidence-based practice standard for screening all 4 aspects of the metabolic syndrome in the previous year

cycle1.result: Just over 1 in 10 patients had all 4 aspects of the metabolic syndrome documented; almost half had no evidence of any screening.

result.intervention: Customised feedback after each audit with benchmarked performance data and bespoke change interventions.

cycle2.result: Just over 1 in 3 patients had all 4 aspects documented; the proportion with no screening fell to 1 in 7.

result.other_findings: Six audits 2006 to 2012 (21 Trusts at baseline, 32 in 2012); only a minority of patients were screened in line with best practice.

result.setting: Rotunda Hospital, Dublin, specialist maternity hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 2.24 clinically significant positive maternal blood culture episodes per 1000 live births; E. coli 37% (92/252), group B Streptococcus 25% (64/252), Staphylococcus aureus 11%.

result.other_findings: Retrospective surveillance review with no trend over 14 years; listeriosis 4.4 and invasive group A streptococcus 5.3 per 100,000 live births.

result.setting: 10 ICUs in Australia and New Zealand
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 17% (n=29) had VAP characteristics by the checklist and 30 by physician diagnosis; VAP rate 25.9 (checklist) and 26.7 (clinician) per 1000 ventilator days; only 17% of cases identified by both methods.

result.other_findings: Checklist development and incidence audit rather than compliance with a standard; 'inflammatory response' item most associated with physician-diagnosed VAP.

result.topic: NIV in acute hypercapnic COPD exacerbations
result.setting: Odense University Hospital, Medical Emergency Ward and Respiratory Ward
result.standard: National guidelines for NIV in acute COPD exacerbation with hypercapnic respiratory failure

cycle1.result: NIV initiated in 151/804 (18.7%) COPD admissions; in a further 42 (5.2%) NIV criteria were met without initiation; in the respiratory ward cohort (124 admissions) the NIV indication was met in 92.7% of COPD admissions.

result.other_findings: In 82.3% of admissions receiving NIV a COPD diagnosis and correct NIV criteria were met; 14 NIV admissions had no COPD diagnosis.

result.topic: Familial hypercholesterolaemia detection in primary care
result.setting: GP practices in NHS Medway Clinical Commissioning Group
result.standard: NICE CG71: consider familial hypercholesterolaemia in adults with raised cholesterol (total cholesterol >7.5 mmol/L or LDL-C >4.9 mmol/L)

cycle1.result: Baseline recorded prevalence of diagnosed FH 0.13% (1 in 750).

result.intervention: Electronic audit tool (Audit+) flagging patients with raised cholesterol in GP records; after 2 years, a nurse-led clinic to screen for new index cases.

cycle2.result: After 2 years of electronic audit prevalence rose to 0.22% (1 in 450); after the 9-month nurse-led programme it rose to 0.28% (1 in 357), and 'at risk and unscreened' fell from 0.58% to 0.14%.

result.other_findings: Two simple interventions more than doubled the recorded prevalence of detected FH.

result.setting: 178 cardiac rehabilitation centres, National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: No volume-outcome relationship found for BMI, blood pressure, psychosocial well-being, cholesterol, smoking cessation or physical activity.

result.other_findings: Registry analysis of outcomes only; authors find no support for centralisation.

result.setting: Antenatal clinics on the Thai-Myanmar border for migrant and refugee women
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: HIV seroprevalence 0.47% (17/3,599) and syphilis 0.39% (14/3,592); syphilis lower in refugees (0.07%, 1/1,469) than migrants (0.61%, 13/2,123).

result.other_findings: Descriptive audit of the first year of routine syphilis screening; highlights false positive results and counselling difficulties in low-prevalence populations.

result.setting: Five hospitals (Portsmouth, Winchester, Southampton), elective major abdominal, gastrointestinal and orthopaedic surgery
result.standard: Recommended maintenance amounts of sodium, potassium and fluid (guidelines not named)

cycle1.result: 1157 IV fluid days; over half received no IV fluid on postoperative day 1; sodium exceeded recommended maintenance in half of those still on IV fluids; potassium almost universally inadequate.

result.other_findings: Considerable variability in intraoperative fluid volume for three common operations; hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia were common.

result.topic: Red cell transfusion thresholds in critical care
result.setting: Single ICU, North Bristol Trust
result.standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology 2012 guidelines: transfuse at haemoglobin below 70 g/L unless bleeding, sepsis, neurological injury or acute coronary syndrome

cycle1.result: Before intervention, of 10 transfusions 2 appropriate (green), 1 inappropriate (red) and 7 unclear (amber).

result.intervention: Local transfusion guideline with posters in the ICU, then guidance attached to transfusion prescriptions.

cycle2.result: After both interventions 7 green and 3 amber transfusions, none inappropriate; total ICU transfusions fell by about 50% (41 to 18) after the first intervention.

result.other_findings: 30 random transfusions analysed in total; began with an audit of doctors' knowledge of transfusion thresholds.

result.topic: TIA management in the emergency department
result.setting: Croydon University Hospital emergency department
result.standard: Local guideline for management of TIA (including antiplatelet prescription)

cycle1.result: 31% of TIA patients received antiplatelets.

result.intervention: Teaching session for new FY2 doctors on initial TIA management and the local guideline.

cycle2.result: First improvement cycle: 86% received antiplatelets, with significant improvement (P = 0.05) in documentation of symptoms in the prior week; similar results in the second improvement cycle.

result.other_findings: Baseline plus two improvement cycles; all outcomes improved and the effect was sustained.

result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: British Thoracic Society oxygen audit standards (four key standards)

cycle1.result: 55% had a valid oxygen prescription; 50% had a documented target saturation range; 84% had saturations on the MEWS chart; 0% had oxygen signed for at drug rounds.

result.intervention: New oxygen prescription chart, oxygen alert stickers for drug and MEWS charts, point-of-care resources and senior-led education, over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: After PDSA cycle three: valid prescription 94%, target range documented 94%, saturations on MEWS chart 100%, oxygen signed for at drug rounds 18%.

result.other_findings: Signing for oxygen at drug rounds remained poor; Trust-wide rollout projected to save £30,400 a year.

result.topic: Immediate discharge document processing in general practice
result.setting: Single general practice, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: Scottish Patient Safety Programme in Primary Care care bundle for immediate discharge documents (medicines reconciled, follow-up documented, diagnosis coded, all actions completed)

cycle1.result: 20% compliance with the care bundle.

result.intervention: Education at each cycle, all doctors using the Medicines Reconciliation Polypharmacy LES template, and an electronic checklist for the care bundle.

cycle2.result: 100% compliance in PDSA cycles two and three.

result.other_findings: Baseline audit followed by three PDSA cycles; a protocol for processing IDDs was developed.

result.setting: Prospect Park Hospital, Reading, psychiatric inpatient unit
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists: full physical examination on admission or within 24 hours; Trust guidelines

cycle1.result: 78/111 (70.3%) had a physical examination during admission; documentation often poor and incomplete across domains.

result.intervention: Introduction of a psychiatric inpatient physical health assessment sheet (PIPHAS).

cycle2.result: 75/100 (75%) examined on admission, with more thorough documentation of all examination domains when a PIPHAS form was used.

result.other_findings: Snapshot baseline audit followed by retrospective review of the next 100 admissions.

result.setting: Intensive care unit, Great Western Hospital
result.standard: General Medical Council guidance on medical handover

cycle1.result: Handover present only in a minority of patients and documented in none (0%).

result.intervention: Handover prompt and documentation of recipient on discharge paperwork, space in daily review sheets for outstanding handover, and presentation of findings at a local meeting.

cycle2.result: Handover rate 100% (n=12) and documentation of handover 100%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: iMobile critical care outreach team, King's College Hospital
result.standard: Guidelines and evidence identified by scoping review for critical care discharge summaries

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Regular audit and feedback of discharge summary quality, feedback of patient experience, and championing and education by local opinion leaders over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Audit results were mixed across the project, showing difficulty sustaining positive change.

result.other_findings: Fluctuating bed occupancy and staff turnover affected sustainability.

result.setting: Paediatric ward, Altnagelvin Area Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Error-free prescribing on drug charts (predesigned proforma)

cycle1.result: 32 errors across 12 drug charts.

result.intervention: Seven sequential interventions over six months covering education and communication, practical prescribing changes and medicine reconciliation.

cycle2.result: After intervention 7: 10 errors (-63%); lowest after intervention 6: 7 errors (-74%).

result.other_findings: Seven audit cycles of 10 random charts; errors after interventions 1-5 were 32, 31, 17, 12 and 15.

result.topic: Low back pain assessment and management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, inner London teaching hospital
result.standard: Locally developed evidence-based low back pain pathway and medico-legal documentation standards

cycle1.result: Initial review of 75 case notes showed inconsistent assessment, incomplete documentation and a biomedical approach.

result.intervention: Evidence-based low back pain pathway, staff education programme and patient education booklet.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in all areas: red flag screening up 22%, biopsychosocial screening 29%, previous symptoms 44%, observation 57%, classification 59%; analgesic ladder adherence up 45%, reassurance 23%, GP referral 44%.

result.other_findings: Patient experience data were inconclusive due to low response rate.

result.setting: Community paediatric team, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 11 incident reports submitted (1.8 per month).

result.intervention: Agreed definition of a critical incident, presentation of staff questionnaire findings on barriers to senior management, and feedback to staff after critical incident presentations.

cycle2.result: 22 incident reports (3.7 per month), an increase of 100%.

result.other_findings: 12 questionnaires identified 28 barriers in five categories; staff were twice as likely to report negativity after reporting an incident.

result.topic: Alcohol withdrawal screening and detoxification pathway
result.setting: Acute medical unit, Ysbyty Gwynedd
result.standard: Local pathway for recognition and treatment of alcohol dependency

cycle1.result: Over-prescription of chlordiazepoxide with average length of stay 5.5 days (2012/2013); compliance with screening tools in random samples over three months was persistently low (exact figure unclear in abstract).

result.intervention: Redesigned pathway with an abbreviated two-question AUDIT screening tool and threshold, implemented over several PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 86 patients screened with the two-question tool, 18 at possible risk, 16 had full AUDIT and 8 started detoxification; overall pathway compliance 84%.

result.other_findings: Common tools (CIWA, AUDIT) were rejected by junior doctors as too cumbersome; the two-question tool had an AUROC of 1.

result.topic: Induction of labour process and outcomes
result.setting: Inner city district general hospital maternity unit, Barts Health NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Caesarean section rate after induction 29%; time to administer induction medication 6.3 h; outpatient induction 3%.

result.intervention: Dedicated induction of labour suite, promotion of outpatient induction, single-administration prostaglandin, staff engagement and rolling audit.

cycle2.result: Caesarean section rate 22% (p=0.05); time to induction medication 2.7 h (p=0.0001); outpatient induction 33% (p=0.001); reduced inpatient length of stay.

result.other_findings: Positive staff and patient feedback and improved staff morale.

result.setting: One hospital (Royal Free Hospital, London)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Interviews with 34 health professionals identified five themes influencing Sepsis Six implementation, including knowledge, beliefs about consequences, teamwork, empowerment and staffing levels.

result.intervention: Modified intervention with six new behaviour change techniques: Sepsis Six training for the Hospital at Night co-ordinator, a partnership agreement permitting collegial challenge, and revised education and materials.
result.other_findings: Qualitative intervention development study using the Theoretical Domains Framework; no compliance data reported.

result.setting: Respiratory ward, Musgrove Park Hospital, large district general hospital
result.standard: Fluid balance monitoring only when clinically indicated, with complete and accurate charts

cycle1.result: Only 53% of input/output monitoring was clinically indicated; average chart completion 50%.

result.intervention: E-learning and verbal presentations on fluid balance, plus daily medical review of charts to rationalise monitoring.

cycle2.result: 93% reduction in unnecessary monitoring, with increases in completion (40%) and accuracy (48%) of remaining charts.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tuberculosis cohort audit across North West England
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews described a valuable community of practice with shared purpose; TB cohort audit seen as an effective quality improvement tool.

result.other_findings: 1515 cases had been reviewed through cohort audit; continuing success needs consultant and public health engagement and secure funding.

result.topic: Chronic kidney disease blood pressure control in primary care
result.setting: 4 primary care practices in England (QICKD trial)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Focus groups found improved CKD monitoring but scepticism that care improved; pay-for-performance was the main driver of change.

result.other_findings: Process evaluation of a trial comparing audit-based education with guidelines and prompts.

result.topic: Quality assessment of mental health supported accommodation
result.setting: UK mental health supported accommodation services
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: QuIRC-SA of 143 items: 18 items had a narrow response range and 5 poor inter-rater reliability; good discriminant validity.

result.other_findings: Tool development study; potential use in audit and quality improvement.

result.topic: Lung cancer treatment in Aboriginal people
result.setting: Population-based cancer registry, New South Wales
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 30.8% of Aboriginal vs 39.5% of non-Aboriginal people with non-metastatic NSCLC had surgery; 5-year risk of death 83.3% vs 77.6% (adjusted subhazard ratio 1.32).

result.other_findings: Medical record audit of 170 Aboriginal people: 29% had potentially curative treatment, 45% palliative treatment and 26% no active treatment.

result.topic: Stiripentol in adults with Dravet syndrome
result.setting: Epilepsy service, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Responder rate 3/13 (23%) at 36 months; retention 62% at 1 year and 31% at 5 years; adverse effects in 7/13 (54%).

result.other_findings: Observational effectiveness audit without a standard; withdrawal due to adverse effects in 3/13 (23%).

result.setting: All 35 acute public hospitals in the Republic of Ireland
result.standard: National audit standards for acute hospital dementia care (assessment, specialist access, training, discharge planning)

cycle1.result: Mobility assessed in 89%, continence 84%, pressure sore risk 87%, pain 75%, function 36%, cognition 43%, delirium 30%; discharge planning not started within 24 h in 72%.

result.other_findings: 84% of wards had no dementia champion; about half of hospitals gave no dementia training to doctors (45%) or nurses (48%) in 12 months; 33% of carers had no needs assessment before discharge.

result.setting: Acute admissions unit, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, 400-bed teaching hospital, London
result.standard: Reliable documentation of current medication on discharge summaries (complete, verified, intentional changes clarified)

cycle1.result: Reliable documentation of current medication on 49.2% of discharge summaries during the project (10 random patients per week).

result.intervention: Staff education and training, medication documentation templates for electronic prescribing and discharge summaries co-designed with patients, and pharmacist-led team approach.

cycle2.result: Reliable documentation 85.2% in a post-study audit.

result.other_findings: Pharmacist involvement in discharge reconciliation increased; variation seen at doctor changeover and introduction of new systems.

result.topic: Orthotic management of neuropathic scoliosis in children
result.setting: Orthotics service (DM Orthotics), case notes of children with or at risk of scoliosis
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Scoliosis confirmed in 77/180, of whom 39/77 used a DEFO; 22/43 with a developing curve used a DEFO; 60/180 used a DEFO preventatively.

result.other_findings: Descriptive case-note review; 48/60 curves were C-shaped.

result.topic: Employment and mental health after cardiac rehabilitation
result.setting: National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Unemployed patients had a lower proportion in normal mental health categories at baseline and mostly poorer outcomes after weighting.

result.other_findings: Registry analysis of outcomes only.

result.setting: Hospital in a South African sub-district
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Audit data showed 60% of malnourished children admitted were HIV positive; experience-based co-design with 14 staff and 10 mothers/caregivers proposed 38 improvements, 25 implemented or planned.

result.intervention: Experience-based co-design added to an ongoing QI intervention (point-of-care blood machine, play area, standard operating procedures for handover and waiting times, privacy screens).
result.other_findings: Qualitative co-design study; no re-audit reported.

result.topic: Computerised audit and feedback interface design
result.setting: Research-led e-audit and feedback system for primary care (PINGR), University of Manchester
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Usability inspection by 8 evaluators found 47 issues in 8 heuristic themes; the recommended actions component had most issues (n=21, 45%).

result.other_findings: Usability study, not a clinical audit.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice
result.setting: All 795 antibiotic-prescribing NHS general dental practices in Scotland (RAPiD cluster randomised trial)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Baseline antibiotic items per 100 NHS treatment claims: 8.3 control, 8.5 intervention.

result.intervention: Individualised graphical audit and feedback of monthly antibiotic prescribing, with or without a written behaviour change message and health board comparator.

cycle2.result: Prescribing fell by 0.4 items per 100 claims in control and 1.0 in intervention practices (relative reduction -5.7%, p = 0.01); written behaviour change message gave a further 6.1% reduction (p = 0.01).

result.other_findings: Cluster randomised trial; no significant effect of health board comparator (p = 0.06) or of a third feedback round (p = 0.99).

result.setting: UK National Lung Cancer Audit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Pulmonary carcinoid: 77% surgery, 1-year survival 92% and 3-year 84.7%, vs NSCLC 36.2% and 15.6%.

result.other_findings: Registry analysis of outcomes only; 3-year survival fell to 23.8% with ECOG 3-4 and 33.6% for stage IV disease.

result.topic: Type 2 diabetes care processes in primary care
result.setting: 162 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander primary health care centres (CQI programme)
result.standard: 15 service items recommended in clinical guidelines for type 2 diabetes

cycle1.result: Clients received on average 43 to 60% of recommended care.

result.intervention: Wide-scale continuous quality improvement programme with repeated clinical audits.

cycle2.result: Generalist physical checks improved year on year, laboratory tests only in later years, and education/counselling improved early then plateaued; CQI participation increased odds of top-quartile delivery for all modes.

result.other_findings: Health centre factors explained 20-52% of variation; over 15,000 audit records analysed.

result.setting: Obstetric admissions department, Mulago National Referral Hospital, Kampala
result.standard: Traffic Light System for obstetric triage

cycle1.result: Informal triage occurred 46% of the time at the first checkpoint, but the Traffic Light System was not being used and many vital signs were not recorded.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest replacing the system with a simple urgency algorithm.

result.topic: Length of stay in COPD exacerbations
result.setting: European COPD Audit, 13 countries
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 8.7 ± 8.3 days (median 7, IQR 4-11); longer stay associated with GOLD class IV (OR 1.77) and mechanical ventilation (OR 2.15).

result.other_findings: Analysis of audit data for factors associated with length of stay, not compliance.

result.setting: National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation, England
result.standard: English NHS targets for cardiac rehabilitation enrolment (target not stated)

cycle1.result: Of 234,736 (81.5%) referred, 141,648 enrolled and 97,406 initiated CR; 37.2% of initiators completed a programme of 8 weeks or more.

result.other_findings: Enrolment did not meet NHS targets; initiation associated with younger age, having a partner, not being employed, no diabetes and CABG.

result.setting: 40 of 56 UK cancer centres (Royal College of Radiologists national audit)
result.standard: UK guidance for intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) in anal cancer

cycle1.result: 231 (95%) had full dose radiotherapy with prophylactic nodal irradiation; 180 (78%) received IMRT and 52 (22%) two-phase conformal; interruptions 4% with IMRT vs 7% conformal.

result.other_findings: Any acute toxicity 48% with IMRT vs 54% conformal in the audit and 71% in the ACT2 trial.

result.setting: 170 accredited microbiology laboratories in England
result.standard: NICE guidance: test dyspeptic patients for H. pylori by urea breath test, stool antigen or serology

cycle1.result: 121/170 (71%) responded; 96% provided H. pylori testing and 94% used stool antigen; only five laboratories did not comply with NICE guidance.

result.other_findings: Only 22/94 (23%) cultured gastric biopsies on site and 9/22 performed susceptibility testing.

result.setting: Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project registry, England and Wales
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 27.7% of ACS patients were anaemic; anaemia independently associated with 30-day (OR 1.28) and 1-year mortality (OR 1.31).

result.other_findings: Registry outcome study; anaemic patients were less likely to receive evidence-based therapies.

result.topic: Cardiology follow-up after heart failure admission
result.setting: 185 hospitals, National Heart Failure Audit for England and Wales
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Referral to cardiology follow-up varied from 6% to 96% between hospitals and was associated with lower 30-day (OR 0.70) and 1-year mortality (OR 0.81).

result.other_findings: Registry outcome analysis only.

result.setting: Older adult inpatient units, Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National guidelines: duty doctor consultation when a competent patient refuses medication

cycle1.result: Discussion with the duty doctor occurred in 75% of cases (27/36).

result.other_findings: Consultation led to a change in prescription or compliance in 59% (16/27).

result.setting: 54 UK mental health services (Royal College of Psychiatrists quality improvement programme)
result.standard: Practice standards derived from evidence-based guidelines including NICE (indications and annual side-effect screening)

cycle1.result: 64% prescribed antipsychotics; annual screening documented for body weight 41%, blood pressure 32%, and blood glucose and lipids 37%.

result.other_findings: Screening varied widely between services (0-100%); most prescribing was for licensed or evidence-based indications.

result.topic: Audit and feedback in cardiac rehabilitation
result.setting: 18 Dutch cardiac rehabilitation centres (cluster randomised trial)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 233 quality improvement goals identified, 49 (21%) achieved; no effect on primary or secondary outcomes except data completeness (4.5% improvement per year).

result.other_findings: Cluster randomised trial of web-based audit and feedback with outreach visits.

result.setting: Surgical unit, Basildon and Thurrock University Hospital
result.standard: e-CRABEL score (modified CRABEL score for medical note keeping)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Presentation at departmental audit meeting and teaching sessions for junior doctors at two points, using photographic examples and clarification of criteria.

cycle2.result: Preliminary data showed promise in improving record keeping quality (figures not given in the abstract).

result.other_findings: e-CRABEL used as a monthly audit tool, also providing VTE documentation data.

result.setting: UK cardiac rehabilitation programmes in the National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation
result.standard: Six National Certification Programme for Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (NCP_CR) minimum standards

cycle1.result: Of 170 programmes, 30.6% high performance (5-6 standards met), 45.9% mid-level (3-4), 18.2% low (1-2) and 5.3% met none of the minimum criteria.

result.other_findings: Substantial variation below the recommended minimum standards across the UK.

result.setting: 28 long-term care facilities in Queensland
result.standard: Beers criteria for potentially inappropriate medications

cycle1.result: Of 317 residents taking medication, 68% were prescribed at least one potentially inappropriate medication; 200 potential interactions identified in 130 residents, 38% potentially severe and 46% moderate.

result.other_findings: Number of medications prescribed correlated positively with number of potentially inappropriate medications.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Legal criteria of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 (gold-standard documentation)

cycle1.result: 21 capacity assessments (6.9% of referrals); none met the gold standard.

result.intervention: Legally focused educational intervention to staff.

cycle2.result: Month 16 (during intervention): 27 assessments (9.7%), 2 met gold standard; month 21: 24 assessments (6.6%), none met gold standard.

result.other_findings: No effect of the educational intervention was shown; severity of consequences (OR 24.4) and not agreeing to the intervention (OR 21.8) predicted lacking capacity.

result.setting: Welsh Geriatric Registrar-Led Research Network (WeGeN)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: The network has facilitated four national audits (older people in the emergency department, Parkinson's disease, delirium management, surgical disease epidemiology).

result.setting: NHS National PET-CT Clinical Audit Programme
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Survey of 58/59 doctors: audit initially threatening (79%) but reassuring (85%) and validated competence (93%); perceived usefulness drove engagement most.

result.setting: UK HIV services, with data from the National Study of HIV in Pregnancy and Childhood
result.standard: 2012 BHIVA pregnancy guidelines

cycle1.result: 99% of 112 services used dedicated multidisciplinary teams (26% with no specialist midwife or nurse); 17% reported delays >1 week for specialist review; ART started in pregnancy in 37% with >94% of regimens guideline-compliant; 11% of services had local delivery-mode policy contrary to guidelines.

result.other_findings: Late ART initiation was common, especially with low CD4 count or high viral load; delays >2 h for urgent HIV results were common.

result.setting: 211 hospitals in the MINAP registry
result.standard: ESC Acute Cardiovascular Care Association quality indicators for acute myocardial infarction

cycle1.result: 16 of 20 QIs could be calculated; 11 had a significant inverse association with risk-adjusted 30-day mortality.

result.other_findings: A 1% increase in composite quality indicator attainment represented a 3% decrease in 30-day standardised mortality.

result.topic: CA125 follow-up after ovarian cancer treatment
result.setting: Mount Vernon Cancer Centre, Northwood
result.standard: Counselling on follow-up options after the MRC OV05/EORTC 55955 trial

cycle1.result: Agreed CA125 follow-up plan recorded in 69 of 87 (79%) eligible patients; 55 (80%) chose no routine CA125 follow-up and 14 (20%) chose routine follow-up.

result.other_findings: CA125 checked in 28 (51%) of the no-routine group, 26 because of symptoms, with 22 relapses confirmed.

result.setting: Acute inpatient mental health unit, Brisbane
result.standard: Clinical guideline recommendations for antipsychotic monotherapy at minimum effective dose

cycle1.result: Sub-optimal polytherapy and high-dose prescribing identified; overall 62.5% of 400 patients discharged on a single antipsychotic within recommended dose range.

result.intervention: Preliminary findings and education sessions provided to physicians between cohorts.

cycle2.result: Sub-optimal polytherapy and high-dose rates persisted; education programme alone was ineffective.

result.other_findings: Involuntary treatment, frequent hospitalisations and previous clozapine use increased risk of polytherapy and high-dose prescribing.

result.setting: English acute NHS trusts (electronic survey)
result.standard: 2015 ILCOR resuscitation treatment recommendations

cycle1.result: Waveform capnography (45.2%) and ultrasound (39.7%) often only in specialist areas; debriefing after every arrest in 5.5% of trusts.

result.other_findings: Response rate 53.3% (73/137); financial restrictions the main barrier (65.8%).

result.topic: Breast cancer presenting symptoms and diagnostic intervals
result.setting: National audit of cancer diagnosis in primary care
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Breast lump in 83%; women with non-lump symptoms more often waited 90 days or longer before seeking help (15% and 20% vs 7%).

result.topic: Appropriateness of CT coronary angiography referrals
result.setting: Mohammed bin Khalifa Cardiac Centre, tertiary cardiac centre
result.standard: American College of Cardiology Foundation appropriate use criteria for CCTA

cycle1.result: 176 (75.2%) appropriate, 47 (20.1%) uncertain, 11 (4.7%) inappropriate.

result.other_findings: Most inappropriate referrals were for CAD detection in asymptomatic low or intermediate risk patients (63.6%).

result.setting: Royal Surrey County Hospital, Guildford
result.standard: Dementia CQUIN targets for dementia assessment completion

cycle1.result: Completion rate for dementia CQUIN assessments 27%.

result.intervention: Changes to working practices suggested by junior doctors and nurses, informed by interviews; involvement of the multidisciplinary team.
result.other_findings: Involving the multidisciplinary team produced the most significant improvement.

result.setting: Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, Great Ormond Street Hospital
result.standard: Blood tests requested according to previous results and clinical condition

cycle1.result: LFTs requested daily on most patients, even with previous normal results; average blood test spend £23,392 per month.

result.intervention: Blood test request form to document nurse-doctor discussion, with two nurse champions providing bedside support, education and feedback, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Significant sustained reduction in LFT requests, with similar reductions in FBC, coagulation screens and CRP.

result.other_findings: Saving in excess of £36,000.

result.topic: Preventive care in Indigenous primary care
result.setting: 137 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander primary health care centres
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Priority gaps included follow-up of abnormal results, cardiovascular risk assessment and timely recording of results.

result.topic: National lung cancer audit data quality
result.setting: NHS trusts in England submitting National Lung Cancer Audit data
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Sex, age, performance status and stage had over 90% agreement between LUCADA and COSD, but the registry dataset had more missing performance status.

result.setting: High HIV-caseload general practice clinics
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Switch reasons were simplification (73%), toxicity/intolerance (13%) and patient preference (12%); 95.1% remained on therapy at 12 months.

result.topic: Practice walk test in pulmonary rehabilitation
result.setting: UK pulmonary rehabilitation services in the 2015 National COPD Audit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Only 1,666 (22.6%) had a baseline practice walk test.

result.other_findings: Those with a practice test were 2.2 times more likely to enrol and 17% more likely to complete rehabilitation.

result.setting: UK hospitals providing emergency general surgery (study protocol)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Protocol for a prospective national audit over an 8-week period; no results reported.

result.topic: Chronic kidney disease coding and management
result.setting: 1039 general practices in the National Chronic Kidney Disease Audit
result.standard: Recommended CKD interventions: blood pressure targets, proteinuria testing, statin prescription, flu and pneumococcal vaccination

cycle1.result: 30% of patients with biochemical CKD did not have a GP CKD code.

result.other_findings: Uncoded patients were less likely to receive optimal care (e.g. OR for meeting blood pressure target 0.78).

result.setting: UK National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Delays to starting cardiac rehabilitation predicted worse anxiety and depression outcomes.

result.setting: Three Polish hospital pharmacies
result.standard: EU Falsified Medicines Directive

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Only one dispensing location had potential as a primary authentication area; no automated dispensing, unit dose or electronic order system was found.

result.setting: Cambridge University Hospitals
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Technical paper: 797 data sets (25,000 scans) exported in 31.5 h.

result.topic: Electronic audit and feedback system usability
result.setting: Laboratory usability study with primary care physicians
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Seven physicians committed a median of 10 errors and completed a median of five of seven tasks.

result.topic: Community pharmacy management of non-prescription medicine requests
result.setting: 36 community pharmacies in metropolitan Sydney
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 54% of 521 visits resulted in an appropriate outcome.

result.intervention: Repeated mystery shopping visits with immediate feedback and coaching.
result.other_findings: Questioning scores and the proportion of appropriate outcomes improved significantly over time across nine visits.

result.setting: Neonatal admissions to general paediatric wards in 13 hospitals
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Prevalence of dehydration 19.7% (range 9.4% to 27.0%); only 17 of 153 (11.1%) had bolus fluid prescription.

result.other_findings: Documentation of fluids prescribed was poor; no guidelines exist.

result.topic: Abdominal symptoms and time to help-seeking in cancer
result.setting: National audit of cancer diagnosis in England

result.topic: Cataract surgery productivity, cost and carbon footprint

result.topic: Cochlear implant outcomes in children with multiple disabilities

result.other_findings: Secondary cancer risk rose from 0.0004 to 0.0007%, judged not clinically significant; 399 patients audited.

result.topic: Acute medicine services for pregnant women
result.setting: 130 UK hospitals, Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit

cycle1.result: 5.5% had an acute medicine consultant trained in obstetric medicine; 38% had a named maternal medicine lead; 64 units had local guidelines; 43% had a VTE in pregnancy guideline.

result.topic: Type A aortic dissection surgery outcomes
result.setting: UK National Adult Cardiac Surgical Audit dataset, national registry
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Registry outcome analysis of operative mortality; patient characteristics, intraoperative factors, cardiac centre and high-volume surgeons were determinants of outcome.

result.standard: not reported

result.setting: Real-time surveillance systems of suspected suicides covering about 13 million population
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 121.3 suicides per month in April-October 2020 after lockdown versus 125.7 per month in January-March 2020 (-4%; 95% CI -19% to 13%, p = 0.59).

result.setting: All Wales Medical Genomics Service, national genetics service
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Overall germline/somatic pathogenic variant detection rate 11.6%; germline 9.2% (73/791). Parallel testing in 169 patients detected 14.8%, with 6.5% (11/169) somatic variants.

result.other_findings: Two BRCA1 dosage variants (2.0%, 2/98) would have been missed by tumour testing alone.

result.topic: Medical student clinical audit in general practice
result.setting: Graduate entry medical students and 25 GP practices, University College Dublin
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Students reported positive educational impact (55%), better understanding of the audit cycle (72%) and real-world prescribing (77%); significant difference in audit-cycle knowledge versus non-participants (p = 0.001).

result.other_findings: 96% of responding GPs would host future student audits; research skills confidence did not improve.

result.setting: Children's Palliative Care Education and Training Action Group across UK and Ireland
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Framework with four levels (Public Health, Universal, Core, Specialist) and four learning outcomes each; an audit tool template was developed for quality assurance.

result.other_findings: Framework development paper; no audit data reported.

result.setting: BAUS cystectomy registry, 78 UK hospitals
result.standard: High-quality surgery defined by pathological (negative margins, level I node dissection with at least ten nodes), recovery (length of stay 10 days or less) and technical criteria

cycle1.result: 914 patients (19.6%) received high-quality surgery.

result.setting: Flinders Medical Centre, South Australia
result.standard: Surgical safety checklist compliance on direct observation

cycle1.result: Observed compliance 3.5% despite documented compliance of 100%.

result.intervention: Paper checklist replaced with reusable laminated form, multidisciplinary education and marketing campaign, targeted coaching and changes after staff feedback, over four PDSA cycles.
result.other_findings: Five direct observational audits and two staff surveys were done; staff felt the new process improved safety.

result.setting: Emergency department, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: Evidence-based guidelines recommending against routine radiological and laboratory investigations in bronchiolitis

cycle1.result: Infants under 12 months with bronchiolitis were receiving unnecessary investigations; mean average weekly CXR rate 25%.

result.intervention: Locally agreed flowchart with regular performance feedback using run charts and in-person sessions.

cycle2.result: Mean average weekly CXR rate fell to 11% (57% reduction, p = 0.009974).

result.other_findings: Outcome measure was weekly length of stay; balancing measure was representation rate.

result.setting: Emergency department, large teaching hospital, East Lancashire Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: NAP4 recommendation to use a safety checklist for intubation; aim 90% checklist use within 6 months

cycle1.result: Checklist used in 16.7% of applicable cases.

result.intervention: Interventions to raise awareness and expectation of checklist use, build a favourable view of its benefits and prompt its use at the right moment.
result.other_findings: Run chart showed a shift soon after interventions began; some cases likely missed by the capture method.

result.topic: Colonoscopy audit and feedback adverse effects
result.setting: Six English NHS endoscopy centres
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews: unmet targets prompted anxiety and consideration of gaming, including inaccurate documentation of patient comfort and removal of insignificant polyps.

result.other_findings: Negative feedback without an improvement plan risked reducing confidence.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
result.setting: Primary care in 18 European countries
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prescribing varied considerably between countries; point-of-care testing ranged from 0% (Croatia, Moldova, Romania) to over 65% (Denmark, Norway).

result.other_findings: Prescribing related to severity, comorbidity, age, fever and country, not to POC testing; GPs were confident in nearly 90% of decisions.

result.topic: Phenylalanine control and mental health in phenylketonuria

result.standard: ESPKU guidelines: lifelong phenylalanine control of 600 micromol/L or less

result.setting: Acute medicine services at 93 UK hospitals, Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit
result.standard: Survey questions derived from national guidance

cycle1.result: All services had taken measures for increased demand; 81.7% had expanded medical inpatient beds and 80.4% had added extra clinical staff.

result.topic: Linked cancer registration and cardiovascular audit data

result.standard: not reported

result.other_findings: Data resource profile; no abstract supplied.

result.topic: Old age liaison psychiatry service provision

result.topic: Antenatal care for hepatitis B positive women

result.setting: National Oesophago-Gastric Cancer Audit database, England and Wales
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 17 650 had radical surgery; later audit year associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR 0.93) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.94) and shorter stay (IRR 0.98)

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection

result.standard: Indication-specific antibiotic prescribing quality indicators

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection

result.standard: ESAC quality indicators, e.g. bronchitis in adults ≤30% antibiotics; acute upper RTI <20%; tonsillitis and sinusitis 0-20%; pneumonia in adults 90-100%

result.other_findings: Upper RTI target met in most countries except Ireland (both surveys), Croatia (PPAS-1) and Greece (PPAS-4); pneumonia prescribing was below 90-100% in most countries.

result.setting: 45 NHS mental health trusts: acute adult wards/PICU and specialist addictions units (POMH audit)
result.standard: not reported

result.other_findings: Alcohol history, breath alcohol, Wernicke's screening, parenteral thiamine, relapse prevention and onward referral were all documented more often with specialist addictions care.

result.setting: 116 ICUs in a national Brazilian collaborative (Breakthrough Series model)
result.standard: not reported

result.topic: Myocardial infarction management by kidney function
result.setting: 209 English hospitals (MINAP)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Lower adjusted probability of invasive management with worse eGFR, especially NSTEMI (eGFR range 2: 76.6% vs range 5: 44.5%).

result.setting: 128 radiotherapy facilities in Australia and New Zealand (Australian Clinical Dosimetry Service)
result.standard: ACDS audit pass criteria including gamma 5%/2mm

cycle1.result: Pass rates: soft tissue 96% (271/281), spine 90% (215/238), lung 90% (236/263); average gamma pass 98.7%, 96.5% and 96.5%.

result.topic: Inclusion of under-served groups in clinical trials

result.standard: INCLUDE guidance on under-served groups and protected characteristics in the UK Equality Act 2010

result.topic: Intraoperative pain during caesarean birth under neuraxial anaesthesia

cycle1.result: not reported

result.topic: HbA1c assessment and deintensification in diabetes and frailty

result.standard: not reported

cycle2.result: Improvements in HbA1c assessment and deintensification after interventions 1 and 2 (n = 102) persisted after the Diafrailty Champion audit (n = 92); figures not given in abstract.

result.setting: All eight radiotherapy centres in Denmark

cycle1.result: 3163 received retreatment, including 1471 reirradiation courses (1035 palliative; 436 curative/ablative).

result.topic: Laboratory quality management for antimicrobial resistance testing
result.setting: National AMR reference laboratories in South and Southeast Asia (EQASIA programme)
result.standard: External quality assessment and quality management system practices

cycle1.result: 38% lacked a quality management system, 42% did no internal audits, 50% did no competency assessments, 46% did no root cause analysis for EQA deviations and 42% lacked structured quality control.

result.intervention: Online consultations for root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, plus onsite visits and targeted training for persistently underperforming laboratories.

cycle2.result: Improvements observed in quality management system implementation, SOP development, staff training and quality control (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Of four baseline-assessed laboratories, three underperformed twice and one three times across EQA rounds.

result.topic: Low-value diagnostic testing in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency departments across Australia and New Zealand (clinician survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Tests seen as high risk of unwarranted variation or low value: D-dimer (42%), venous blood gas (39%), CRP (35%), abdominal x-ray (35%).
