result.other_findings: Used the Hogard-Barker Communication Audit of Practice survey tool; provides a baseline for future audit.

result.topic: Clinical audit and clinical governance in general dental practice
result.setting: Southend Primary Care Trust general dental services
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Progress report on a method; no results reported. By December 2003, 96% of dentists had undertaken or committed to clinical audit/peer review.

result.topic: Guideline-based cardiac rehabilitation after myocardial infarction
result.setting: Hospital, primary care and community services, Oxford
result.standard: Guideline-based individualised cardiac rehabilitation

cycle1.result: Individualised plans negotiated for all patients; the rehabilitation team achieved high delivery of agreed interventions, better than primary care.

result.other_findings: Problems mostly related to communication failures; patients with major social or psychological difficulties were hardest to treat.

result.setting: One mental health Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: The Trust had no formal mechanisms for reviewing audit projects; informed consent, confidentiality and anonymity were not adequately addressed.

result.other_findings: Qualitative study of clinicians undertaking audits.

result.topic: Variability in LVEF estimation from gated blood pool imaging
result.setting: 63 nuclear medicine centres (national)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: LVEF estimates were highly variable; overall SD 0.076, precision allowing for systematic variation 0.055.

result.other_findings: 16 centres did not quote a minimum normal LVEF; lower variability with higher-count studies.

result.topic: Lung cancer presentation stage and cell type
result.setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin (teaching hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 34 small cell and 150 non-small cell carcinomas; 84% of NSCC were stage 3 or 4 at presentation.

result.other_findings: 14 patients were too ill for tissue confirmation; squamous carcinoma was the commonest cell type.

result.topic: Mandibular repositioning splint use in sleep apnoea
result.setting: Department of Sleep Medicine, University of Edinburgh, with hospital orthodontic department
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 74 of 144 (51%) still used the splint at least occasionally at median 7 months; survival analysis showed 12% still using it at 12 months; Epworth score fell by 2.4 (P=0.005).

result.other_findings: Response rate 81%; problems in 70 non-users included sore mouth, non-retention and sleep difficulties.

result.topic: Acute asthma management in the emergency department
result.setting: Accident and emergency department; authors from Respiratory Education Training Centre, University Hospital Aintree, Liverpool
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Abstract gives only background asthma prevalence figures; no audit results stated.

result.setting: Our Lady of Lourdes International Missionary Training Hospital, County Louth (district general hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: One perioperative death; overall morbidity 25% and procedure-related morbidity 7%; mean stay 12.3 days.

result.other_findings: For simple cholecystectomy (n = 630) there were no deaths, general morbidity 15% and procedure-related morbidity 3%.

result.topic: Consent for national clinical audit database submission
result.setting: Seven paediatric intensive care units (PICANet)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Signed consent obtained for 182 of 422 admissions (43%), range by unit 9% to 84%; one refusal (0.2%).

result.other_findings: Consent rates were better with more severe illness and stays of 6 days or more, and poorer for children aged 10-14.

result.topic: Bloodborne virus prevention in drug users
result.setting: Rural and city general practices, NHS Lothian
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Only 4% (54/1278) completed hepatitis B immunisation; HCV tested 28% (354/1278), HBV 33% (416/1278), HIV 36% (454/1278); BBV discussion recorded in 41% (523/1278).

result.intervention: Audit feedback, training and advice offered to practices (baseline audit only reported).
result.other_findings: 90% had been asked about injecting; only 52% (275/530) of those tested had been tested for all three viruses.

result.topic: Liver monitoring in methotrexate for psoriasis
result.setting: Multicentre (four groups), Dermatology Centre, Hope Hospital, Salford, Manchester
result.standard: Manchester PIIINP monitoring protocol compared with American Academy of Dermatology guidelines (routine liver biopsy)

cycle1.result: Intervention (PIIINP) groups (n = 166) had 0.04 and 0.02 biopsies/patient/year versus 0.26 and 0.30 in control groups (n = 87), a sevenfold reduction.

result.other_findings: Management-changing abnormalities in 1 in 5 biopsied in the main intervention group versus 1 in 16 in controls; significant cost savings expected.

result.topic: Emergency department referral to inpatient specialties
result.setting: Emergency department, The Lister Hospital, Stevenage
result.standard: Locally developed standard for safe referral from emergency medicine to inpatient specialties

cycle1.result: Many problems at referral were identified (no figures reported).

result.intervention: Recommendations implemented at the base hospital (details not reported).
result.other_findings: Authors recommend teaching of referral skills for both referring and receiving doctors.

result.topic: Barium enema sensitivity for colorectal cancer
result.setting: 131 UK radiology departments (Royal College of Radiologists national audit)
result.standard: RCR targets: lesion demonstration >=95%; correct identification as carcinoma >=90%

cycle1.result: Mean demonstration rate 92.9% and diagnosis rate 85.9%, slightly below targets.

result.other_findings: Equivocal rate 6.9%, perception failure 2.8%, technical failure 4.4%; performance similar to the 1995 Wessex audit.

result.setting: Cognitive Function Clinic, Walton Centre for Neurology and Neurosurgery, Liverpool (regional)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Diagnostic accuracy of SPECT ranged from 32 to 58%; sensitivity 77% and 71%, specificity 44% and 38% (blind and informed readings).

result.other_findings: SPECT was of little help in establishing diagnoses in young cognitively impaired patients.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in medical admissions
result.setting: Emergency medical admissions, Kingsmill Hospital, Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: Thromboembolic Risk Factors Consensus Group recommendations

cycle1.result: Initial audit showed poor adherence to recommendations (no figures reported).

result.intervention: Introduction of a VTE risk assessment form.

cycle2.result: Repeated audits assessed form uptake and its effect on thromboprophylaxis; no figures in abstract.

result.other_findings: Doctors' perceptions and reasons for poor form completion were also surveyed.

result.topic: Primary care trust public information guides
result.setting: Primary Care Trusts in England
result.standard: Central guidance on structure and content of Guides to Local Health Services

cycle1.result: Most PCTs complied with central guidance on structure and content, but Guides lost clarity of purpose.

result.other_findings: Content was dominated by financial and strategic accountability information; public consultation was limited.

result.topic: Travel and waiting times for outpatient radiotherapy
result.setting: Outpatient radiotherapy, West of Scotland (Beatson Oncology Centre, Glasgow)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Median travel distance 10 miles, travel time 45 minutes, waiting time in unit 60 minutes, time away from home 2 hours 50 minutes.

result.other_findings: Only 12 of 60 patients away over a meal time were offered a hospital meal; 16% had a relative losing work time.

result.topic: Public education for early melanoma detection
result.setting: West of Scotland (population 2.7 million), Department of Dermatology, University of Glasgow
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Referrals 5 a week; 38% of melanomas under 1.5 mm thick.

result.intervention: Public education campaign (June 1985) with update information sent to GPs.

cycle2.result: Referrals 19 a week (up 278%); 54% of melanomas under 1.5 mm thick (rise of 16%).

result.other_findings: New melanoma diagnoses rose 131%; mortality in women began to fall from 1988.

result.setting: 23 hospitals and 25 primary care trusts, South East England
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Average policy age 12 months, 13 more than 2 years old; 38 (79%) made few or no cautionary points; only 10 used plain English for dosages.

result.other_findings: Primary care policies improved since 2000; little advice on MRSA and less on gastroenteritis and prophylaxis.

result.setting: UK consultant clinical oncologists (national postal survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Response rate 76%; commonest conditions were CLL, myelofibrosis and CML; dose fractionation varied widely.

result.other_findings: Painful splenomegaly and hypersplenism were the commonest indications; re-irradiation was common.

result.setting: Department of Surgery, Maidstone Hospital, Kent
result.standard: Reported 5-year local recurrence rates of 3% to 15% (literature comparison)
result.other_findings: 165 of 423 (39%) had a closest margin under 1 mm; 97.8% had margins under 1 cm.

result.topic: Intravenous drug preparation and administration errors
result.setting: Six hospital departments in the UK, Germany and France
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Product not labelled or incorrectly labelled in 43%, 99% and 20% of doses (UK, Germany, France); wrong administration rate in 49%, 21% and 5%; at least one aseptic technique deviation in 100%, 58% and 19%.

result.other_findings: 824 doses prepared and 798 administered; wrong diluent used in 1%, 49% and 18%.

result.setting: All nine neonatal intensive care units in Northern Ireland (regional network)
result.standard: Agreed regional quality indicators on transfer patterns, thermoregulation, antenatal steroids and surfactant timing

cycle1.result: In utero transfers 26%; antenatal steroids 68%; normothermia on first admission (inborn) 66%; surfactant first dose within 1 hour 13%.

result.intervention: Centralised data collection with annual confidential feedback and anonymised unit comparisons; regional consensus guidelines adopted locally.

cycle2.result: In utero transfers 42%; antenatal steroids 82%; normothermia 71%; surfactant within 1 hour 66%.

result.other_findings: A multi-professional regional network supported agreed standards and regular evaluation.

result.setting: The London Haven Lymphoedema Service, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Abstract describes presenting characteristics and treatment outcomes without figures.

result.topic: Correction of high INR in anticoagulation clinic
result.setting: Anticoagulation clinic, Haematology Department, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: Target: safely correct INR above 4.5 to a maximum of 8.0 within 7 days

cycle1.result: Unacceptable variation in dosage change for high INR results not dosed by the computer programme.

result.intervention: Development of a dosing protocol for INR up to 7.0 (to be tested); patients with higher results to be contacted.
result.other_findings: Putting the protocol on the computer is expected to reduce manual dosing by 15%.

result.setting: Ninewells Hospital, Dundee (teaching hospital)
result.standard: Hospital antibiotic committee indications for linezolid use, including prior infection specialist approval

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with local recommendations very good; only 34 of 77 had documented prior approval by an infection specialist.

result.intervention: Mandatory linezolid order form to be completed by the prescriber (future evaluation planned).
result.other_findings: Main justifications were renal dysfunction or poor venous access (34%) and glycopeptide intolerance or failure (32%); MRSA was the commonest proven pathogen (56%).

result.setting: Endoscopy, Leicester General Hospital (UK general hospital)
result.standard: Hospital informed consent procedure for endoscopy (NHS consent form plus departmental leaflet)

cycle1.result: All 67 records had a signed NHS consent form; departmental leaflet present in only 31, patient-signed in 20; multiple choice test full marks in 17 of 28.

result.other_findings: 11 patients answered questions incorrectly but correct answers were discussed in only 2 records; 33 records unavailable.

result.setting: Department of Urology, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh (teaching hospital)
result.standard: National guidelines for management of epididymo-orchitis (chlamydia testing and appropriate treatment in men under 35)

cycle1.result: Patients were not routinely tested for chlamydia and most men under 35 were treated inappropriately with ciprofloxacin; diagnosis by ultrasound in 94%.

result.intervention: All patients to be tested for chlamydia, men under 35 treated with ofloxacin, and partners treated by genitourinary medicine.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Diabetes management in advanced cancer at end of life
result.setting: Cheltenham General Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Management and monitoring of diabetes was variable; 32 of 42 had blood sugar monitoring up to and including the day of death.

result.intervention: Guidelines for managing diabetes in the palliative setting proposed.
result.other_findings: Little record of discussion about diabetes with patients or families.

result.setting: ENT urgent referral clinic, Northwick Park Hospital, Harrow
result.standard: Trust standard for note keeping

cycle1.result: Notes initially failed to meet the set standard.

result.intervention: Introduction of a computerised template for data entry.

cycle2.result: Notes accurate and contained relevant demographic data in more than 90% of cases.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Appropriateness of GP referrals to acute surgery
result.setting: Acute surgical unit, Leicester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 78 admissions considered inappropriate, 23 needing neither surgical admission nor opinion; estimated cost 25,000 pounds.

result.other_findings: Senior staff were not easily available for GP calls; authors suggest a senior team member screen GP referrals.

result.topic: Transition of adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis to adult care
result.setting: 10 UK paediatric rheumatology centres in a controlled trial of transitional care
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: Before the start of the trial
cycle1.result: Mean age at which independent clinic visit introduced 16.8 years (SD 1.06).

cycle2.dates: 12-24 months after start of the trial
cycle2.result: Improved documentation of transitional issues, educational needs, readiness and parental needs; independent visit introduced at 15.8 years (SD 1.46), p = 0.01; more preparatory adult clinic visits and transition plans.

result.other_findings: No improvement in documentation of dental care, dietary calcium and home exercise programmes.

result.setting: Maternity unit, George Eliot Hospital, Nuneaton
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Service reported effective in normalising childbirth and increasing maternal satisfaction (no figures reported).

result.other_findings: Concurrent staff audit showed enthusiasm and identified areas for development.

result.topic: PUVA and narrowband UVB phototherapy guideline compliance
result.setting: Photobiology Department, St John's Institute of Dermatology, St Thomas' Hospital, London
result.standard: British Photodermatology Group PUVA guidelines and unit narrowband UVB guidelines

cycle1.result: Guidelines followed relatively closely; exceptions were one high cumulative PUVA exposure, failure to measure minimal phototoxic doses in some PUVA patients, and slightly prolonged referral delays.

result.other_findings: 31 patients received PUVA and 20 narrowband UVB.

result.topic: Quality tool for mental health education and training
result.setting: Department of Health-funded project, piloted in a region of England
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes development and piloting of a continuous quality improvement tool; results reported separately.

result.topic: Knowledge needs of primary care managers
result.setting: Primary Care Trusts (interview study of senior managers)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Knowledge requirements were broad; biggest gap was how to perform needs assessment and quality improvement using aggregated routinely collected general practice computer data.

result.other_findings: A 'knowledge audit' based on recorded interviews; not a clinical audit against a standard.

result.setting: Five trusts on 6 hospital sites across the North Central London Critical Care Network
result.standard: British Thoracic Society guideline on NIV in acute respiratory failure (2002) and NHS Modernisation Agency weaning and long term ventilation document (2002)

cycle1.result: Results discussed against BTS guidelines; figures not given in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Allowed comparisons between hospitals; key areas for future service improvement were identified.

result.setting: UK dental hospital, hospital departments
result.standard: Dentists' requirements for response letter content as determined in a previous questionnaire study

cycle1.result: Almost all departments achieved a minimum total score of 80%; over 90% across departments for all items except those relating to time. Most letters written within 18 days of the appointment.

result.other_findings: Fifteen letters sampled per department; the three departments scoring over 90% were the only ones to include SHO letters.

result.setting: Department of Plastic Surgery, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne; multidisciplinary audit clinics
result.standard: Comparison with Clinical Standards Advisory Group (CSAG) report and other recent studies

cycle1.dates: Audit clinics March 1998 to April 2002 (children born 1985 to 1997)
cycle1.result: Oro-nasal fistula requiring closure 4.7%; velopharyngeal insufficiency requiring pharyngoplasty 26.4%; hypernasality in 14.9% on CAPS assessment.

result.other_findings: VPI requiring secondary surgery in 16% with unilateral cleft lip and palate versus 29.2% with isolated cleft palate; 128 Wardill-Kilner and 20 Von Langenbeck repairs.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer service resources
result.setting: Cancer networks and cancer units in England (postal survey)
result.standard: National targets for time to diagnosis and treatment

cycle1.result: MDT working evident in all centres but not always fully staffed (pathology, radiology, dietetics, speech therapy); clinically significant delays in complex investigations, ICU beds and oncology, especially radiotherapy.

result.other_findings: Rapid referral pathways existed for initial assessment; major service reconfiguration likely needed to meet national targets.

result.setting: Four specialist palliative day care centres
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 145 (91%) prescribed at least one drug that was a CYP substrate, inhibitor or inducer; 24 drug combinations involving 34 patients could have caused a clinically important interaction.

result.other_findings: About one in five patients were at risk of a clinically important CYP-mediated interaction.

result.setting: Cheltenham General Hospital, district general hospital labour ward
result.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists recommended general anaesthesia rate for caesarean section

cycle1.result: Potential serious shortfalls in communication and teamworking; insufficient information to assess appropriateness of indication for general anaesthesia.

result.intervention: Recommendations to improve communication channels between labour ward personnel.
result.other_findings: A reduction in use of general anaesthesia coincided with the recommendations, but no figures are given.

result.topic: Nutritional management in head and neck radiotherapy
result.setting: Nutrition and Dietetic Department, Royal Free Hospital, London
result.standard: Locally produced nutritional guidelines for head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy

cycle1.result: Previous audits used as comparison; figures not given in the abstract.

result.intervention: Implementation of local nutritional guidelines, including prophylactic gastrostomy, and a dietitian present at the multidisciplinary head and neck clinic.

cycle2.result: Fewer patients lost weight over radiotherapy and there were no admissions for feeding.

result.other_findings: More patients had combined treatment than in previous audits.

result.topic: Rapid trisomy testing versus full karyotype
result.setting: Four London Regional Genetics Centres
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 118/24,891 (0.47%) abnormal sex chromosome karyotypes; 153/24,891 (0.61%) autosomal abnormalities that rapid trisomy testing would miss.

result.other_findings: Switching to rapid trisomy testing would miss clinically serious abnormalities in about 0.06% (1 in 1659), possibly up to 0.12%.

result.topic: Tooth wear monitoring with study casts
result.setting: General dental practice, following advice letters from GKT Dental Institute
result.standard: Consultant advice to monitor tooth wear with study casts

cycle1.result: Replies from 60 dentists (87%) and 53 patients (75%); study casts taken reported by 23 dentists (38%) and 18 patients (34%).

result.other_findings: Compliance with monitoring advice was poor, raising questions about the value of consultant advice letters.

result.setting: Community/general practice drugs project, Muirhouse Surgery, Edinburgh
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 85% receiving a prescription for an opiate and/or benzodiazepine; retention, death rate and behaviour change similar with methadone and dihydrocodeine.

result.other_findings: Trends towards more methadone prescribing and longer-acting benzodiazepines.

result.topic: HIV in pregnancy and prevention of mother-to-child transmission
result.setting: Eight clinics across Yorkshire (regional audit)
result.standard: British HIV Association guidelines for management of HIV infection in pregnancy

cycle1.result: 20/22 mothers received therapy as recommended; 16/22 (73%) elective caesarean; 12/22 (55%) definitely received intravenous zidovudine in delivery; 19/22 infants received appropriate antiretrovirals for four to six weeks.

result.other_findings: No mother-to-child transmission; two mothers initially received inappropriate dual therapy; no mothers known to have breast-fed.

result.setting: Mount Vernon Centre for Cancer Treatment, Northwood
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 44% of patients attending routine radiotherapy had abnormally high anxiety and might benefit from counselling.

result.other_findings: HADS proposed as an objective measure of benefit; costing discussed.

result.setting: UK consultant adult cardiac surgeons (postal questionnaire via SCTS)
result.standard: ACC/AHA 1998 and American College of Chest Physicians 2001 anticoagulation guidelines after valve replacement

cycle1.result: All use lifelong warfarin after mechanical valves; only 16% (16/97) follow guidelines for bioprosthetic AVR and 28% (24/86) for bioprosthetic MVR.

result.other_findings: 53% (51/97) never use warfarin after bioprosthetic AVR versus 33% (28/86) after bioprosthetic MVR; no guidelines exist for mitral repair.

result.setting: Basingstoke and Alton Cardiac Rehabilitation Centre, Hampshire
result.standard: CHD National Service Framework Standard 12 Milestone 3: at one year, regular physical activity (30 minutes five times a week), not smoking and target BMI

cycle1.dates: Patients starting rehabilitation 1 April 2001 to 31 March 2004
cycle1.result: Questionnaires returned by 903 (80%); of responders 74% exercising regularly, 95% not smoking and 79% met the BMI target.

result.other_findings: Post-AMI and high-risk patients were least likely to respond; smoking and BMI targets were judged too low as most met them before rehabilitation.

result.topic: Health equity audit uptake in primary care trusts
result.setting: Primary care trusts in England (national electronic survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Replies from 132 PCTs (44%); most had completed only a few steps of the health equity audit cycle.

result.other_findings: Limited engagement with local strategic partnerships; PCTs wanted comparator data, good practice examples and methodological expertise.

result.topic: Alveolar bone grafting in cleft care
result.setting: Regional cleft service, Birmingham Children's Hospital
result.standard: CSAG organisational standards for cleft care (national CSAG success rate 58%; published series about 95%)

cycle1.result: 81% alveolar bone graft success (68 of 82 with sufficient data); grafting after age 11 in 28% (6/21) BCH patients and 46% (22/47) referred patients.

result.other_findings: Problems included poorly standardised occlusal radiography, inconsistent orthodontic management and lack of prospective data collection.

result.setting: Outpatient department, Bournemouth and Christchurch Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: PALS national standards and National Service Framework for Children (DH 2003)

cycle1.result: Parents reported good information before and during consultation but wanted more written information; very few had heard of PALS and around half did not know whom to approach with concerns.

result.other_findings: Older children felt the waiting area lacked suitable activities.

result.topic: First clinic assessment of suspected epilepsy
result.setting: Hospital and community consultant paediatricians, Nottingham City region
result.standard: British Paediatric Neurology Association (BPNA) audit tool for children with suspected epilepsy

cycle1.result: Seizure sequence recorded in 91%; early development and school performance documented in 41%; 24% had no documented physical and neurological examination; referral to epilepsy nurse or support group in 11%.

result.other_findings: Drug treatment and follow-up plans recorded in nearly all applicable cases; 12% diagnosed epilepsy, 26% non-epileptic, 62% uncertain.

result.setting: Seven breast screening centres in the East Anglian region
result.standard: Current breast screening assessment guidelines

cycle1.result: Of 21,657 negative assessments, 193 women later had cancer at the assessed site; 17 deaths, 15 in women with unsatisfactory assessments; five-year breast cancer survival 93%.

result.other_findings: Estimated 7-9 lives (14-18%) could have been saved had assessments met current guidelines.

result.topic: Fertility preservation in women with cancer
result.setting: Human Assisted Reproduction Ireland, Rotunda Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Five (26%) women had oocytes cryopreserved; mean 8 oocytes (range 3-16).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: University College London Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Advanced age still rated important by 61% in 2003; 18% considered intravenous fluids and 26% antibiotics inappropriate for patients not for resuscitation.

result.other_findings: In 2003 nurses were more likely to consider active treatment appropriate for patients with DNR orders.

result.setting: Tayside Forensic Psychiatric Service; referrals from Procurators Fiscal at three courts in Tayside
result.standard: Home Office guidelines (1990) on diversion of mentally disordered offenders

cycle1.result: Urgent referral rate increased over time, mainly patients already known to psychiatric services, 37% of whom were detained and admitted.

result.other_findings: Urgent assessment avoided remand in custody purely for report preparation and allowed early decisions about diversion from prosecution.

result.topic: Urinary catheter care in care homes
result.setting: 37 randomly selected care homes for older people in three health districts, Gloucestershire
result.standard: NICE and Association of Continence Care urinary catheter care standards

cycle1.result: 750/1438 (52%) staff responded; 83% of nursing and 40% of other care staff had formal catheter training; at least 10% did not wash hands before handling a catheter; bladder washouts used routinely by 50%; urine specimens taken from bag tap by 29% of nursing and 54% of other staff.

result.other_findings: Compliance had improved greatly since a 1998 audit; only 45% of nursing and 40% of other staff encouraged residents to empty their own bags.

result.topic: Inpatient quality after mental health service redesign
result.setting: Acute mental health admission wards, Royal Cornhill Hospital, Aberdeen (Grampian)
result.standard: Scottish Framework for Mental Health (1997); local quality indicators (admissions, bed occupancy, incidents, locked-door days, observation levels, sickness, bank hours)

cycle1.result: Baseline indicator rates; figures not given in the abstract.

result.intervention: Closure of one of five acute admission wards, remaining four wards increased from 25 to 28 beds, and increased community mental health team staffing.

cycle2.result: Rates of the indicators had not increased, so quality of inpatient care was judged at least as good as before.

result.other_findings: Differences in numbers of observations and in times ward doors were locked merited further discussion.

result.topic: Use of routine primary care data for research
result.setting: Primary care informatics review
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Review of opportunities and challenges of routinely collected primary care computer data; not an audit.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer service resources
result.setting: 34 cancer networks and 52 cancer units in England (questionnaire survey)
result.standard: National targets for time to diagnosis and treatment

cycle1.result: MDT working in all centres but often not fully staffed (pathology, radiology, dietetics, speech therapy); clinically significant delays in complex investigations, ICU beds and oncology, especially radiotherapy.

result.other_findings: Rapid referral pathways existed for initial assessment; major service reconfiguration likely needed to meet national targets.

result.setting: Multicentre UK cancer study of MDT communication
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 87% (342/394) wanted all possible information; recalled discussion of clinical trials 43% (119/280), family history 28% (90/320) and sexual well-being 37% (116/314).

result.other_findings: 39% wanted shared decision making; older patients more likely to prefer the doctor to decide.

result.setting: University Department of Dermatology outpatient clinic, Western Infirmary, Glasgow
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 67% (30/45) said their lifestyle was affected by psoriasis.

cycle2.result: 40% (18/45) said lifestyle affected; 76% (34/45) felt psoriasis improved and 11% (5/45) deteriorated.

result.other_findings: Patient and dermatologist severity scores correlated significantly (P less than 0.001).

result.topic: Age threshold for urgent endoscopy in dyspepsia
result.setting: Scottish Audit of Gastric and Oesophageal Cancer (national prospective database)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 290 (8.8%) of 3293 patients with upper GI malignancy were in the younger age group (figure truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Raising the endoscopy age threshold from 45 to 55 years would not adversely affect diagnosis of upper GI malignancy.

result.setting: West Midlands Cancer Intelligence Unit and breast screening units
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Screening status assigned to 14,680 women (96% of the cohort); 110 cancers not registered.

result.other_findings: Methodology paper describing an algorithm usable as a quality assurance tool.

result.setting: Vascular Studies Units in the UK (questionnaire to Society of Vascular Technology members)
result.standard: ECST or NASCET measurement methods for diagnosing carotid stenosis over 70%

cycle1.result: 26% of units used NASCET, 31% ECST and 43% did not know; similar proportions of each group used a peak systolic velocity threshold over 230 cm/s.

result.other_findings: Considerable confusion about what constitutes an ultrasound diagnosis of stenosis over 70%.

result.setting: Royal Marsden Hospital, London and Surrey
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 114 (79%) had a 50% or greater reduction in hot flushes and 30 (21%) less than 50%; 17 (9%) had minor side effects.

result.other_findings: Treatment algorithm presented; mean treatment duration nine months.

result.setting: BAUS Section of Endourology national laparoscopic nephrectomy audit (UK centres)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean operative time 173 min; mortality 0.7%; major complications 10%; transfusion 10%.

cycle2.result: Mean operative time 166 min; mortality 0.2%; major complications 4%; transfusion 7%.

result.other_findings: 1294 nephrectomies reported since 2001; centres doing fewer than 12 cases a year had longer operations and higher transfusion and conversion rates.

result.setting: Accident and emergency department, University Hospital of Hartlepool
result.standard: DVLA 'At a glance guide to the current medical standards of fitness to drive'

cycle1.result: Of 22 patients needing driving restrictions, only one had documented advice about driving.

result.other_findings: Recommended further education for A&E doctors and patient information leaflets.

result.topic: COPD exacerbation outcomes and hospital resources
result.setting: 234 UK acute hospitals (UK National COPD Audit 2003)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Inpatient mortality 7.4%, 90-day mortality 15.3%, readmission 31.4%, mean length of stay 8.7 days (median 6).

result.other_findings: Four or more respiratory consultants per 1000 beds associated with lower inpatient (OR 0.67) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.75).

result.topic: Informal carer documentation in palliative care notes
result.setting: Palliative care service patient files (King's College London department)
result.standard: Completeness of assessment data recording for informal carers (no external standard stated)

cycle1.result: 100 files (69.9%) had identifiable informal carers; patient data complete but carer data severely lacking; primary carer need was finance and welfare advice (n=64).

result.other_findings: Recommended files identify informal carers separately from family and record carer assessments on a par with patients.

result.setting: UK radiotherapy centres (questionnaire to service managers)
result.standard: Current practice in treatment verification (no external standard stated)

cycle1.result: Response 48% (30/62); 97% (29/30) had site-specific written verification protocols; 67% (20/30) audited set-up errors; 83% (24/29) with portal imaging used image analysis software; 53% used off-line correction strategies.

result.other_findings: Verification strategies varied widely within and between departments.

result.topic: Blood product use in cardiac surgery
result.setting: Cardiac intensive care unit, Western Infirmary, Glasgow
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Red cells used in 60%, FFP in 17% and platelets in 16% of patients.

result.intervention: Introduction of near-patient thromboelastometry (ROTEM) in January 2002.

cycle2.result: Red cells used in 53%, FFP in 12% and platelets in 11% (P < 0.05).

result.other_findings: 990 sequential patients covered both periods combined.

result.topic: Ambulance triage identification of acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: Hampshire Ambulance Service NHS Trust, Southampton area
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 263 patients had ACS; AMPDS sensitivity 71.1%, specificity 92.5%, PPV 5.6%; 12.5% (33/263) classed as non-life threatening.

result.other_findings: 76 of 263 ACS patients presented without chest pain.

result.setting: Moorfields Eye Hospital linked with centres in Malaysia, Ghana, Tanzania, South Africa and Gambia
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 132 cases posted; 24% without images; response time fell from 13 days in the first four months to three days in the last four.

result.other_findings: Main problem was internet down-time.

result.topic: Antiplatelet therapy and bleeding after CABG
result.setting: London Chest Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean 24-hour chest drain output 694.4 mL (clopidogrel and aspirin) vs 831.9 mL (aspirin) vs 726 mL (neither); differences not significant.

result.other_findings: Mean units transfused 1.67 (aspirin) vs 1.0 (both) vs 0.6 (neither), not significant.

result.setting: Department of Dermatology, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
result.standard: SIGN guidelines for melanoma management

cycle1.result: Re-excision and sentinel node biopsy guidance closely followed; only 30% of referrals marked urgent; median time to first appointment 20 days (1998) to 52 days (2001); surgical margins recorded in 13%.

result.other_findings: Median time to biopsy 6 days; time to first appointment exceeded national recommendations.

result.setting: Liver Unit, University Hospital Birmingham
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Major impact on management in 7 patients; unexpected extrahepatic disease in 7/23 (30%); decision possible from CT-PET report in 21/23.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis for external ventricular drains
result.setting: Intensive Care Unit, St George Hospital, Sydney
result.standard: Restrictive EVD antibiotic protocol (e.g. intravenous cephalothin 1 g 6-hourly for 24 hours)

cycle1.result: Prophylactic antibiotics in 5/12 (42%); positive CSF Gram stain 3/12 (25%); CSF not analysed in 35/72 samples (49%).

result.intervention: Introduction of an EVD management protocol with restrictive antibiotic prophylaxis, daily sterile CSF sampling and drain removal after five days.

cycle2.result: Prophylactic antibiotics in 12/15 (80%); positive Gram stain 0/15 (0%); positive CSF cultures fell (17 vs 5, p = 0.0009).

result.other_findings: CSF not analysed in 45/88 samples (51%) after the protocol; drain times similar.

result.setting: Intensive Care Service, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, Sydney
result.standard: Predicted daily energy requirement for patients staying over 3 days

cycle1.result: Nutrition started 2.2 +/- 1.3 days after admission; 100% of requirement reached by 4.8 +/- 3.3 days; nutrition on 82.3% of patient-days; daily average 71.7% of energy requirement; interrupted on 30% of patient-days.

result.intervention: Clinical Practice Improvement model used to analyse reasons for inadequate feeding and change practice, targeting interruptions for extubation and upper GI intolerance.

cycle2.result: Interruptions for these reasons significantly reduced but no significant overall improvement in time to nutritional goals or energy received.

result.other_findings: 379 consecutive patients over 12 months in total.

result.setting: Department of Otolaryngology, Northampton General Hospital
result.standard: National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit rates

cycle1.result: Haemorrhage and return to theatre rates for coblation tonsillectomy similar to national rates for cold steel and ties.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 17 acute hospitals in Wales (regional audit)
result.standard: NICE recommendation that all patients are referred to a multidisciplinary anal cancer team

cycle1.result: About 26 cases a year; 80% referred for oncology opinion; 50% had curative chemoradiotherapy; stoma rate 35%; five-year survival 45%.

result.other_findings: Wide variation in data quality; radiological staging used inconsistently; documentation of staging, treatment and pathology needed improvement.

result.topic: Organ donation potential in intensive care
result.setting: 341 intensive care units in 284 UK hospitals (national audit of ICU deaths)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 2740 potential heartbeating donors and 1244 actual donors; 41% of families of potential donors denied consent; no record of next of kin being approached in 15%.

result.other_findings: Refusal rate among families of ethnic minority potential donors was twice that of white potential donors.

result.setting: Department of Otolaryngology, University Hospital Lewisham, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 30% of theatre sessions attended; case participation 27%.

result.intervention: Simple timetable (rota) changes to maximise SHO theatre attendance.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Old age psychiatry liaison to forensic units
result.setting: Specialist old age psychiatry liaison service to a medium and a high secure forensic unit, West London Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: All referrals judged appropriate and new management advice given in all cases; main reasons were diagnostic, placement and treatment advice.

result.other_findings: Placement advice was hardest because few care homes accept patients with a forensic history.

result.topic: Interhospital transfer of critically ill patients
result.setting: Mobile Intensive Care Ambulance Service (MICAS), Ireland
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: No deaths during transfer; 93% needed airway intervention before transfer and 32% inotropic support during transfer.

result.other_findings: 47% of transfers were within greater Dublin and 45% from regional centres to Dublin.

result.setting: Gastrointestinal and Liver Service, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Bowel preparation good in 263 (42.5%), satisfactory in 242 (39.1%) and poor in 114 (18.4%); poor preparation caused incomplete colonoscopy in 28 (4.5%).

result.other_findings: No difference between inpatients and outpatients.

result.topic: Effect of audit participation on asthma care
result.setting: 77 self-selected Scottish general practices compared with 319 practices from a national sample
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Audit practices had more structured nurse reviews (61% v 45%), fewer acute GP contacts (33% v 43%), more symptom-free days (42% v 23%) and fewer attacks (16% v 20%).

result.other_findings: Less use of A&E (2% v 3%) and outpatients (3% v 5%) in audit practices; comparison group 9617 patients.

result.topic: Allergic rhinitis management in primary care
result.setting: 70 UK general practices; GPs with a self-declared interest in allergic and respiratory disorders
result.standard: Consensus statement on the treatment of allergic rhinitis (four standards: symptom identification, diagnostic information, examination and investigations, treatment)

cycle1.result: All criteria met: Standard 1 14% (n=26), Standard 2 23% (n=43), Standard 3 0% (n=0), Standard 4 0.6% (n=1).

result.other_findings: Baseline audit by semi-structured interview; 90% of 210 GPs interviewed.

result.topic: Audit and feedback for urinary incontinence care
result.setting: Community nurses in 157 family practices
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Audit and feedback and educational outreach did not improve care compared with educational materials alone; improvements of 10-17% for assessment and 20-30% for management were similar across arms.

result.other_findings: Cluster randomised trial of 194 nurses; not itself an audit.

result.setting: Department of Gynaecological Oncology, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (Grampian)
result.standard: Completeness of staging information compared with previously published Scottish audit results

cycle1.result: FIGO stage available in 100%; chest X-ray 85%; peritoneal cytology 93%; pelvic lymphadenectomy 28%; all significantly better than the Scottish audit.

result.other_findings: All cases managed by specialist gynaecological oncologists; effect on outcome unknown.

result.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, King's College Hospital, London
result.standard: Local corneal abrasion guidelines developed by A&E and ophthalmology staff

cycle1.result: Contact lens enquiry 35.3%; local anaesthetic drops given out; visual acuity documentation lower (figure not given).

result.intervention: Introduction of local guidelines on corneal abrasion management with some training.

cycle2.result: Visual acuity documented in 93%; contact lens enquiry 71.9%; no local anaesthetic drops given; appropriate discharges up 40%, inappropriate eye clinic referrals down 75%, abrasion advice up 101%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Medical Microbiology, King's College School of Medicine and Dentistry, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Of 203 diagnoses needing surveillance, 30% viral; of 142 bacterial isolates, 27% multiply resistant Enterobacteriaceae and 9% MRSA; four outbreaks involving nine people.

result.other_findings: Describes a computer system replacing a manual T-card surveillance system.

result.setting: 49 general practices in Brighton and Hove
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Standardised diabetes prevalence 26% higher (remainder truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: High exception reporting in deprived practices may disguise unmet need.

result.topic: Early warning score and observation documentation
result.setting: Combined medical and surgical assessment unit, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Baseline documentation of physiological parameters recorded (848 patients across both periods); figures not given in abstract.

result.intervention: Introduction of a standardised early warning scoring system (SEWS).

cycle2.result: Documentation of physiological parameters improved (P<0.001-0.005) except oxygen saturation (P=0.069); inpatient mortality decreased (P=0.046).

result.other_findings: Admission early warning score correlated with in-hospital mortality (P<0.001) and length of stay (P=0.001). Staff reported increased awareness of illness severity (80%) and earlier interventions (60%). Total sample 848 patients over two periods.

result.topic: Nurse-led carpal tunnel service and waiting times
result.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Leicester General Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Unacceptable waiting times for carpal tunnel syndrome before the service (figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Rapid-access nurse practitioner-led single practitioner pathway from first clinic through surgery to discharge.

cycle2.result: Waiting times improved considerably while standard and quality of care were maintained (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Acute general hospital, Royal Gwent Hospital, Newport (Gwent Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: Aim to reduce CAUTI rate by 20%

cycle1.result: CAUTI rates captured with Trust standard catheters (figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Introduction of silver alloy-coated Foley catheters.

cycle2.result: Aim of reducing CAUTI rate by 20% met and exceeded; CAUTI risk rate and device rate fell.

result.other_findings: 117 newly catheterised patients monitored in total. Silver alloy catheters judged cost-effective and recommended for short-term catheterisation in acute admissions.

result.setting: Periodontal department of a teaching hospital, Eastman Dental Hospital, London
result.standard: Periodontal referral guidelines/criteria

cycle1.result: Use of Basic Periodontal Examination (BPE) score in referrals 17%; medical history mentioned in 31-34% of letters.

result.intervention: Referral guidelines implemented (2000/2001), then referral criteria redefined and circulated via Primary Care Trusts (2004/2005).

cycle2.result: BPE score use 57%; medical history still mentioned in only 31-34% of letters; clinical details had increased in 2000/2001 with a tendency to decrease in 2004/2005.

result.other_findings: 450 referrals across three periods (1997, 2000/2001, 2004/2005). Little agreement between referral clinical details and consultation findings; a pro forma was not associated with better referral quality.

result.setting: Two general practices, one in southwest London and one in Surrey
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians stroke guidelines for primary care; QOF stroke quality points

cycle1.result: Practice A scored 93.5% (29/31) of QOF stroke points; practice B 73.4% (22.75/31) but better RCP adherence: assessed in secondary care 96% vs 79% (P=0.001); seen same day 64% vs 44%; rehabilitation 56% vs 37%.

result.other_findings: Higher QOF quality points did not reflect better adherence to RCP guidance.

result.setting: Paediatric department nurse-led allergy clinic, West Middlesex University Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Previous community study found most families prescribed adrenaline auto-injectors could not use them properly.

result.intervention: New prescribing protocol for doctors and a nurse-led allergy clinic with one nurse training all patients.

cycle2.result: Most patients reported training, had written instructions, demonstrated competence on a dummy and would appropriately call an ambulance; significantly better than before.

result.other_findings: 68 of 81 (83%) clinic patients took part.

result.setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: British Thoracic Society CAP guidelines

cycle1.result: Severity assessment at presentation per guidelines in 56 (34.1%); appropriate antibiotics within 8 hours in 123 (75.0%).

result.other_findings: Overall mortality 8.5%, comparable with previous results.

result.setting: Otolaryngology departments in England (internet-based national audit)
result.standard: Action on ENT baseline clinical and administrative standards (23 standards)

cycle1.result: Only 8% of 97 departments met all 23 standards; microsuction 99%, outpatient endoscopy 97%, activity monitoring 98%; poor compliance for common waiting lists (51%), patient feedback facilities (56%) and treatment plan in notes (46%).

result.other_findings: Response 91% (97/107). More than one in four departments lacked dedicated children's facilities or a lead clinician for paediatric audiology.

result.topic: P-POSSUM risk prediction in gynaecological oncology surgery
result.setting: Northern Gynaecological Oncology Centre, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Gateshead
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: P-POSSUM predicted 7% mortality (35 deaths) vs observed 2% (10 deaths); H&L chi2=542.9, d.f. 8.

result.other_findings: P-POSSUM overestimates mortality risk for gynaecological oncology surgery and needs adjustment.

result.setting: Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Kumasi
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Perforation 39% (249/638); negative appendicectomy 25.9% (56/216); complications 43.1% (wound infection 41.5%); mean stay 7 days; mortality 1.9% (12 deaths).

result.other_findings: Morbidity and mortality attributed mainly to late presentation; mean duration of illness 74 hours.

result.setting: Genitourinary medicine department, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Screen performed in 433; chlamydia-positive 41 (9.5%) vs background 8.5%; HIV test uptake 71.2% (311/433); average wait to appointment 3 days vs background 2-3 weeks.

result.other_findings: 46 (10.6%) treated epidemiologically as contacts and 18 (4.1%) as chlamydia-negative urethritis/cervicitis; patient satisfaction judged good.

result.setting: Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge (large teaching hospital)
result.standard: British Society of Medical Mycology and IDSA candidaemia audit standards (e.g. central venous catheter removal within 48 h)

cycle1.result: CVC removed within 48 h in 79% (37/47); identification and susceptibility tests 94.7%; antifungal started within 24 h in 84%; appropriate initial therapy 95% (61/64); at least 2 weeks' treatment 81%; transfer guidance on duration only 45%.

result.other_findings: 92 episodes in 90 patients; 30-day mortality 41%; Candida-related complications associated with mortality (OR 6.5, 95% CI 1.2-36.5, p=0.03).

result.setting: Care homes in Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: National standards for diabetes care; Department of Health health-equity audit guidance

cycle1.result: Diabetes register under-represented known diabetes (3.5% vs 11.5%); inappropriately high glucose monitoring and secondary care involvement; little co-ordinated eye screening; staff needed diabetes training.

result.other_findings: Rapid-evaluation methods were feasible for health-equity audit; a local action plan was agreed.

result.setting: General surgical wards, Kent and Canterbury Hospital
result.standard: All regular cardiac medication should be given preoperatively even when nil by mouth

cycle1.result: 42% of patients had one or more cardiac drugs omitted.

result.intervention: Information sheet and brief verbal reinforcement to nursing staff and junior doctors.

cycle2.result: Omissions reduced to 20% (p=0.023); p=0.0029 when omissions on medical instruction excluded.

result.other_findings: Significant fall in 'nil by mouth' given as reason for omission.

result.setting: Delivery suite, Leeds General Infirmary (4500-delivery teaching hospital unit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 22.8% normal BMI, 41.9% overweight, 31.9% obese, 3.4% morbidly obese; epidural failure more likely as BMI increased.

result.other_findings: Obesity increased epidural resite rates, and caesarean section rate rose sharply with BMI.

result.setting: Acute Trusts across the UK (2003 National COPD Audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 103 of 233 units (44%) had early discharge schemes; admission prevention in the emergency department 5%; 30% of patients could be put into early discharge schemes.

result.other_findings: Mortality and readmission rates were the same as in units without early discharge schemes; each unit audited 40 clinical cases.

result.setting: Cardiac intensive care unit, tertiary paediatric ECMO centre, Great Ormond Street Hospital, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Sepsis rate 29.3 episodes per 1000 ECMO days before policy changes.

result.intervention: Monthly multidisciplinary surveillance meetings; re-education, electively preprimed ECMO circuits, and preference for neck rather than chest cannulation in cardiac patients.

cycle2.result: Sepsis fell to 20.1 per 1000 ECMO days; neonatal respiratory 28.0 to 6.6 and paediatric respiratory 42.4 to 16.9 per 1000 ECMO days.

result.other_findings: 215 children overall with 47 septic episodes in 39 (24.9 per 1000 ECMO days). Sepsis stayed high in cardiac patients with open sternum (65.1 per 1000 ECMO days).

result.topic: Head and neck cancer radiotherapy outcomes
result.setting: Regional Centre for Radiotherapy and Oncology, Mount Vernon Hospital, Northwood
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Complete response 94% in node-negative T1/T2 and 59% node-positive; 5-year local control 77% vs 20%; T3/T4 complete response 72% node-negative and 32% node-positive, 5-year local control 37% and 0.

result.other_findings: Complete response, freedom from recurrence and survival related to T stage, N stage and primary site.

result.setting: Division of Oncology, Guy's Hospital, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes an approach to auditing the cost-effectiveness of palliative cancer chemotherapy; no results reported.

result.setting: 12 nongovernmental outpatient dermatology clinics in north Palestine
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 616 of 2458 medications were topical corticosteroids; information on strength, duration and quantity was inadequate in most prescriptions, while frequency, route and area of application were adequate.

result.other_findings: High and highest efficacy steroids prescribed for about 18% of patients and intermediate efficacy for about 50%.

result.setting: 99 general practices (Primary Care Data Quality programme)
result.standard: Cholesterol target in secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease

cycle1.result: Mean cholesterol 4.75 mmol/l before the programme.

result.intervention: Primary Care Data Quality programme: audit-based educational intervention.

cycle2.result: Mean cholesterol fell to 4.64 mmol/l; diagnostic coding and numbers with cholesterol measured and treated increased.

result.other_findings: No significant change in statin dosage or in inequity between groups prescribed statins.

result.setting: Obstetrics and gynaecology department, Daisy Hill Hospital, Newry
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Audit of delivery statistics successfully performed using the new database.

result.other_findings: Describes design of an obstetrics and gynaecology electronic record database; further audits of mode of delivery and Robson groups under way.

result.setting: Three district dental facilities of a UK NHS Trust (two community clinics and one hospital orthodontic department)
result.standard: American Dental Association guideline on DUWL water quality and EU potable water standard

cycle1.result: The two units using disinfection regimes met the ADA guideline and EU potable water standard; the unit that only flushed failed both.

result.intervention: All three facilities standardised DUWL disinfection using Bio 2000; one unit then moved to continuous super-oxidised water (Sterilox).

cycle2.result: Colony counts from all samples stayed well below the EU recommended level; the Sterilox unit achieved and maintained zero readings.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Peer review of GP audit quality
result.setting: Voluntary peer review model for general practitioners, west of Scotland
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 552 of 1002 (55%) criterion audit submissions judged satisfactory; GP registrars more likely than GP trainers to be satisfactory.

result.other_findings: A significant proportion of GPs may be unable to apply audit methods adequately.

result.topic: Nutritional screening in upper GI cancer
result.setting: Upper gastrointestinal oncology outpatient clinic, Kingston Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Only 40% weighed at clinic visit; 65% self-reported weight loss; only 35% had received dietary advice and 68% of the rest would have liked some.

result.other_findings: Nutritional screening was not routine; nausea and dysphagia significantly more frequent in those with weight loss.

result.topic: Quality of life in infant atopic eczema
result.setting: Paediatric dermatology clinics, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean IDQOL and DFI scores both 8.47 (medians 8 and 7); the two measures correlated well (rs=0.776).

result.intervention: Initial consultation with a paediatric dermatology team.

cycle2.result: Parents of 50 infants completed both questionnaires before first and second consultations; beneficial effect of the initial consultation on quality of life reported.

result.other_findings: Validates the IDQOL and DFI measures for routine clinical use.

result.setting: Mater Misericordiae Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Five-year survival 61% (17/28); disease-free survival 76% (13/17); survival 79% (11/14) if nodes negative vs 17% (1/6) if positive.

result.other_findings: Age, stage and lymph-node status were prognostic; 12 local/regional recurrences.

result.setting: Jessop Wing, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield
result.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists postoperative pain audit target: 90% of patients with pain score no more than 3/10

cycle1.result: Only 37.9% of patients given 300 microg intrathecal diamorphine had pain score of 3/10 or less throughout; target not achieved at any dose.

result.other_findings: Randomised controlled trial; dose-dependent improvement in analgesia and itching. Authors consider the target too arduous.

result.setting: Oral medicine unit, Eastman Dental Hospital, London (university teaching hospital)
result.standard: UK National Cancer Referral Guidelines for suspected oral mucosal malignancy (2000)

cycle1.result: 487 of 901 referrals classed as potentially malignant; in a subgroup of 241, 18 had malignant (8) or dysplastic (10) lesions; guidelines missed 15% of malignant or dysplastic lesions.

result.other_findings: Only 9 of 75 persistent ulcer referrals and 8 of 116 white patch referrals were malignant or dysplastic; missed lesions presented with orofacial pain of unknown cause.

result.topic: Nurse and pharmacy-led oral chemotherapy clinic
result.setting: Nurse-/pharmacy-led capecitabine clinic, Beatson Oncology Centre, Glasgow
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 79% completed at least 3 cycles (mean 3.5); dose reduced in 15 (29%); at least one delay in 17 (30%).

result.other_findings: Patient satisfaction high (n=27 questionnaires); at least 85% found the service useful and well organised.

result.setting: The Liver Unit, Birmingham Children's Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Cronbach's alpha 0.72; score >15 had odds ratio 7 (P=0.0125) for death or transplant at 6 months.

result.other_findings: Development and validation of a dependency score; agreed with PELD score in 12 transplant-listed patients (r=0.660).

result.setting: HSE (SWA) Regional Orthodontic Unit, St James's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Gold standards based on authors' ideal requirements and published guidelines

cycle1.result: 20% of laboratory work arrived late; 65% met all gold standards; 10% of appliances unsatisfactory; 20% needed adjustment for more than 30 seconds before fit.

result.other_findings: 46% of appliances needed adjustments; functional appliances accounted for almost half of unsatisfactory work, one in five being unsatisfactory.

result.topic: Cardiovascular disease management in primary care
result.setting: UK general practices in a cardiovascular data feedback programme (St George's, University of London)
result.standard: Evidence-based audit criteria for cardiovascular disease, e.g. cholesterol management in ischaemic heart disease

cycle1.result: Cholesterol recording 47.6%; mean cholesterol 5.18 mmol/L; statin prescribing 46%; recorded IHD prevalence 3.8%.

result.intervention: Educational feedback of routinely collected computer data with peer-led learning, inter-practice comparisons and lists of patients needing intervention.

cycle2.result: After three iterations: cholesterol recording 89.0%; mean cholesterol 4.67 mmol/L; statin prescribing 68% (via 57%); recorded IHD prevalence 4.0%.

result.other_findings: Eight years of the programme; the approach was also applied to atrial fibrillation, heart failure and renal disease.

result.topic: Organisational capacity for chronic disease care
result.setting: General practices in Australia (University of New South Wales programme)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 82 of 247 GPs (33%) from 57 of 97 practices (59%) took part; 37 (65%) recognised the area most needing improvement; 25 (46%) developed an action plan; 22 (39%) implemented their chosen activity.

result.intervention: Feedback report on capacity for chronic disease care followed by practice-chosen clinical audit activity.
result.other_findings: Change activity focused on teamwork was judged most successful; the link between need and action was weak.

result.topic: Prenatal ultrasound detection of congenital anomalies
result.setting: Birmingham Maternity Hospital, Queen Elizabeth Medical Centre
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Anomaly incidence 12.9/1000 (booking scan, n=3565) vs 9.83/1000 (mid-trimester scan, n=4984); sensitivity before 20 weeks 30% vs 45%; overall prenatal sensitivity 65% vs 63%.

result.other_findings: Mid-trimester scanning detected anomalies earlier; cardiac anomalies were the largest group not detected equally; three lethal anomalies were missed in the booking group.

result.setting: 15 Scottish maternity services
result.standard: Miscarriage audit criteria (e.g. providing a 7-day miscarriage service)

cycle1.result: Before feedback clinicians had positive attitudes, strong subjective norms and intentions to comply, with lower perceived behavioural control.

result.intervention: Three feedback approaches compared: printed report alone; report plus action planning letter; report plus face-to-face facilitated action planning.

cycle2.result: Attitudes, norms and intentions generally increased but no change reached statistical significance; no consistent relationship between feedback method and scores.

result.other_findings: Interviews (n=17) showed positive views of audit but frustration at lack of capacity to implement change.

result.setting: ENT departments in England and Wales (national postal survey)
result.standard: Department of Health and Royal Colleges of Surgeons and Anaesthetists standards for paediatric surgical services

cycle1.result: Named paediatric ENT consultant 54.7%; designated clinical lead for children's surgery 56.6%; only 30% met theatre facility requirements; acute pain service in only 26%; 50% of small DGHs had appropriate anaesthetic supervision.

result.other_findings: Response rate 56%; guidelines not met in nearly 50% of targeted areas, with specialist stand-alone units scoring highest and small DGHs lowest.

result.setting: 163 adult general critical care units in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (ICNARC)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: New ICNARC model: mean c index 0.870, mean Shapiro's R 0.665, mean Brier's score 0.132.

result.other_findings: ICNARC model outperformed recalibrated existing models and was recommended for UK risk adjustment.

result.topic: Cardiac risk factor management in intermittent claudication
result.setting: Claudication clinic, Department of Vascular Surgery, NHS Grampian
result.standard: Secondary prevention standards for cardiac risk factors

cycle1.result: 104 patients assessed in the previously published audit (results not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: 30% (n=91) did not have a diagnosis of intermittent claudication confirmed; cardiac risk factor management remained sub-optimal.

result.other_findings: Difficulties exist in diagnosing intermittent claudication in primary care. Abstract results truncated.

result.topic: Nasal fracture management in the emergency department
result.setting: Accident and emergency department of a busy district general hospital
result.standard: Best practice for nasal fracture management

cycle1.result: 10 had nasal X-ray; 9 had no documentation of septal haematoma; 7 had no follow-up arranged.

result.intervention: Education and a departmental protocol based on best practice.

cycle2.result: Two nasal X-rays (looking for foreign bodies); all patients had septal haematoma documentation and appropriate follow-up.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Merton, Sutton and Wandsworth Health Authority area (endoscopy referrals)
result.standard: National referral guidelines for suspected colorectal cancer; seen within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: 67% (119/177) seen within 2 weeks; only 47% (71/151) of referral letters mentioned rectal examination.

result.intervention: Local acceptance of national referral guidelines, faxable urgent referral pro forma developed with GPs, educational meetings and a waiting-time monitoring database.

cycle2.result: Average waiting times dropped quickly and remained low (figures not given).

result.other_findings: Qualitative interviews with 19 patients and review of 33 case records; patients perceived most delay in secondary care after non-urgent referral.

result.topic: Epidural analgesia in paediatric empyema thoracotomy
result.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, Leeds General Infirmary (single centre)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: No infective complications of epidural space or insertion sites; moderate-severe pain 18% and severe pain 2% in first 24 h.

result.other_findings: Two of three children given systemic opioids had respiratory complications.

result.setting: 10 Scottish hospitals
result.standard: Appropriateness of intravenous route and agent (Glasgow Antimicrobial Audit Tool)

cycle1.result: 1079 (28.3%) on antibiotics, 381 (35.3%) IV; IV route appropriate in 84% (IDP) and 84.8% (algorithm); agent appropriate in 80%; median IV duration 4 days.

result.other_findings: Third-generation cephalosporins most frequent (28.3%), then co-amoxiclav (20.2%); regional differences seen.

result.setting: Accident and emergency department, University College Hospital, Ibadan (tertiary hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 81.25% male; armed robbery the cause in 71.3%; extremities injured in 61.3%.

result.other_findings: Low-velocity missiles predominated and most patients were physiologically stable.

result.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
result.standard: RCOG guidelines on Chlamydia trachomatis screening and treatment before VTOP and ERPC

cycle1.result: VTOP group (n=30) screening and treatment satisfactory, aided by a proforma; ERPC group (n=30) had weaknesses in identifying and treating at-risk patients.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest universal prophylactic antibiotics for ERPC until a national screening programme is established.

result.topic: Postcoital and intermenstrual bleeding clinic pathway
result.setting: General gynaecology and colposcopy clinics, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 33 (55%) seen at general gynaecology clinic and 27 (45%) at colposcopy; Chlamydia testing deficient in both; no malignancy; CIN in 3 (11%) at colposcopy.

result.other_findings: Proposes a new PCB/IMB outpatient service with guidelines to standardise care.

result.setting: 277 NHS and independent hospitals in England and Northern Ireland (National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 1,197 (3.5%) postoperative haemorrhages: primary 188 (0.6%), secondary 1,033 (3%); bipolar diathermy OR 2.47 (1.81-3.36) vs cold steel.

result.other_findings: 40,514 patients submitted, 84% consented. National guidance issued midway through the audit influenced practice and reduced haemorrhage rates.

result.setting: Regional colorectal cancer database, Digestive Diseases Centre, Brighton
result.standard: ACPGBI colorectal cancer minimum dataset (18 key data points)

cycle1.result: 83% of data elements present in records; agreement between records and database 61% overall (70% preoperative, 47% operative).

result.other_findings: Suggests weekly review of entries and/or clinician data entry to improve accuracy.

result.setting: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital (single institution)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 1611 transfusions in 881 patients; transfusions rose 25% in 3 years; mean haemoglobin trigger rose from 8.53 to 8.86 g/dl.

result.other_findings: Identifies high-risk areas where alternatives such as erythropoietin could be considered.

result.setting: Emergency Department, Royal Bolton Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes a follow-up meeting for relatives 4-6 weeks after bereavement; audit results not given in abstract.

result.setting: Clinical biochemistry laboratory, Royal Liverpool & Broadgreen University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: January to June 2005 (retrospective) and July to December 2005 (prospective)
cycle1.result: 45 of 46 results negative at the 99th percentile cut-off.

result.other_findings: Authors conclude cTnT testing is not useful in general practice and advise referral if acute coronary syndrome is suspected.

result.setting: General dental practitioners in Merseyside (University Dental Hospital of Manchester)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 251 of 330 (76%) returned; 82% preferred diagnosis and treatment plan in list format; only 71% aware of what was happening to patients and 75% knew required actions.

result.other_findings: GDPs felt much of the information in reply letters was not needed.

result.setting: Alder Hey Children's Hospital, Liverpool
result.standard: Locally developed standards for urethral catheter care

cycle1.result: Catheter duration 1 to 38 days; in 13% duration could not be identified because of poor documentation.

result.other_findings: Staff questionnaire (384 nurses, 174 doctors) showed low training levels and limited understanding; most nurses had never or rarely catheterised a child.

result.topic: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy outcomes by surgeon specialty
result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Upper GI vs other firms: laparoscopic completion 96.2% vs 80.1%; cholangiogram 83.4% vs 16.9%; operating time 69 vs 84 min; stay 2 vs 3.6 days; bile duct injury 0.1% vs 0.9%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Paediatric pain services in Great Britain and Ireland (national audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 96 incidents; 56 related to insertion or maintenance (1:189); 5 grade 1 serious (about 1:2000); 9 grade 2 (about 1:1100); one child with residual effects at 12 months (about 1:10 000).

result.other_findings: 33 pressure sores; four compartment syndromes, none masked by the epidural.

result.setting: Accident and emergency departments across England (67 hospitals)
result.standard: Department of Health national tetanus guidance (2002)

cycle1.result: 75% had a local tetanus guideline but only 29% said it was always followed; 46.2% would give a booster if fifth dose >10 years ago, contrary to guidance; 22.1% would consider any wound tetanus prone.

result.other_findings: Only 31.4% managed injecting drug users as high risk; 2002 changes not widely implemented.

result.topic: Peer review of GP audit quality
result.setting: West of Scotland general practice peer review
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 132 (39%) audits unsatisfactory; 118 (89%) of these had a design flaw such as criteria definition; 119 (90%) had deficiencies in analysis or change management.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Sixteen primary care health centres
result.standard: WHO recommendation that all TB suspects undergo sputum microscopy before treatment

cycle1.result: Peru: 31% (95% CI 27-35) of TB suspects assessed with sputum microscopy; Bolivia: 30% (95% CI 25-35) had at least two examinations.

result.intervention: Clinical audit intervention with standard setting, performance measurement and feedback.

cycle2.result: Availability of sputum microscopy results improved by 7% (95% CI 1-12) (further figures truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Results available for only about one third of suspects.

result.setting: 75 general practices in Warwickshire
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Practice manager audit of risk management activities used to derive a competence score (figures not given).

result.intervention: Practice initiatives, significant event audit and Medical Defence Union workshops.

cycle2.result: Improved risk management competence, especially in breadth of staff involved and formal recording systems.

result.other_findings: Little evidence that improvements were mediated by organisational culture.

result.setting: Day Surgery Unit, Gartnavel General Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: ECG criteria for day-case surgery patients

cycle1.result: Only 24 of 60 patients meeting ECG criteria were referred; significant abnormality in 12.5%; none had surgery postponed or management changed.

result.other_findings: No adverse events or perioperative cardiovascular complications.

result.setting: Intensive care unit, John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle, NSW
result.standard: No explicit standard; ICU quality improvement review listing end-of-life management as a possible audit item (Curtis et al. 2006)

cycle1.result: 55% of ICU deaths were the result of treatment withdrawal; treatment failure or futility was overwhelmingly the reason cited; no cases of conflict between medical team and family.

result.other_findings: Pilot of an audit tool with structured intensivist interviews; intensivists reported high confidence and wanted earlier support from admitting medical officers.

result.setting: Community cardiology specialist nursing team, Sunderland Teaching PCT
result.standard: National service framework for coronary heart disease (no target stated)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Audit of home visiting after discharge for acute myocardial infarction, to consider whether other nursing teams could deliver the service; no results given in the abstract.

result.setting: Royal Marsden Hospital (Chelsea and Sutton), Velindre Hospital Cardiff and Royal Surrey County Hospital Guildford
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Time on unit 2 h 36 min for pamidronate vs 1 h 38 min for zoledronic acid; 94% needed cannulation and almost one-third needed two or more attempts; over 77% attended solely for the infusion.

result.other_findings: Infusion times: RMH pamidronate 1 h 29 min, zoledronic acid 18 min; Royal Surrey zoledronic acid 21 min; Velindre pamidronate 1 h 42 min, zoledronic acid 17 min. About 71% had breast cancer.

result.setting: Royal North Shore Hospital, Sydney (requests mainly from accident and emergency centre)
result.standard: International guidelines on urine drug screening in overdose (no target stated)

cycle1.result: Clinical utility identified in only 85 of 171 UDS; 61% of AEC requests had no clinical utility vs 24% from other specialties.

result.other_findings: 70.8% of requests came from the accident and emergency centre; the authors conclude excessive requesting in routine overdose.

result.topic: Primary care oral surgery referral service outcomes
result.setting: Practice-based oral surgical referral service (primary care), Cumbria
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 79% treated within four weeks of referral; 53 not treated; complications dry socket 31/703, suture pain and inflammation 11/453, post-operative infection 9/547.

result.other_findings: One patient with post-operative infection needed acute hospital care; most common procedure was surgical removal of impacted third molars.

result.setting: Plastic surgery unit, St James's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 92 patients with 96 bite wounds; infection documented in 18 cases (20%), higher with upper limb bites and late presentation (>12 h).

result.other_findings: Alcohol documented in 86%; 70% facial, with the ear the commonest facial target (65%).

result.topic: Postoperative care without ICU after head and neck cancer surgery
result.setting: Specialist head and neck ward, Worcester Royal Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: More than 98% of flaps survived; over half had no complications; median length of stay 12 days (range 2-63); no cancellations.
