result.setting: Emergency department, Tembisa Provincial Academic Hospital (tertiary)
result.standard: Antibiotic protocols and rabies and tetanus post-exposure prophylaxis guidelines

cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed to 120 (45.1%); tetanus toxoid given to 152 (57.4%); first rabies vaccine dose to 240 (89.1%); 15 (5.6%) wounds sutured.

result.other_findings: Children had more head/face/neck and buttock/perineum wounds; adults more lower limb wounds.

result.topic: Warfarin time in therapeutic range in haemodialysis
result.setting: In-centre haemodialysis unit, Jewish General Hospital, Montreal
result.standard: Warfarin time in therapeutic range >60%

cycle1.result: Patients achieving TTR >60% varied between 33% and 45% (mean ± SD, 40% ± 5%).

result.intervention: Quarterly individualised TTR audit-feedback report to each patient's warfarin prescriber, refined through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Patients achieving TTR >60% varied between 52% and 71% (mean ± SD, 61% ± 8%), with sustained improvement on statistical process control.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Children Eye Care Center, Sadguru Netra Chikitsalaya, Chitrakoot
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 943 of 1000 eyes needed no sutures; sutures applied for wound leak in 57 eyes on the table and 5 eyes on postoperative day 1.

result.other_findings: Wound leak risk was greater in children under 5 years. Retrospective case series.

result.setting: 19 government health centres, Burera District (rural primary care)
result.standard: Target goals for supervisory visits and clinical checklist use

cycle1.result: 70% of supervisory visit and 76% of clinical checklist target goals met; checklist item completion improved significantly.

result.other_findings: 2239 service users completed 15,744 visits; GHQ-12 median improved from 26 to 10 over six months in 121 of 146 users. Quasi-experimental implementation-effectiveness study.

result.setting: European radiology departments (ESR EuroSafe Imaging Star network and national societies)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 47/116 (41%) EuroSafe Imaging Star departments and 43 departments from 16/48 national societies responded; low awareness of ESR audit publications and lack of audit infrastructure for BSSD compliance.

result.other_findings: Survey of departments, not a clinical audit.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer tumour board database
result.setting: SingHealth Duke-NUS Head and Neck Centre, Singapore General Hospital and National Cancer Centre Singapore
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Over 2000 presentations recorded for 1279 patients; commonest cancers squamous cell (41%), thyroid (16%) and nasopharyngeal (11%).

result.other_findings: Description of an electronic synoptic tumour board data system to support audit and research.

result.topic: Strong opioid initiation in cancer palliative care
result.setting: Department of Radiotherapy and Oncology, PGIMER Chandigarh (tertiary cancer centre)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Strong opioids initiated in 16% of patients after registration.

result.other_findings: Younger age, visceral metastases and prior weak opioid use predicted strong opioid initiation. Association study rather than audit against a standard.

result.setting: Internal medicine ward, Imam Hossein teaching hospital, Tehran (tertiary)
result.standard: International and local antibiotic prescribing guidelines

cycle1.result: Baseline rate of discrepancies from guidelines (figures truncated in abstract); length of stay 16.1 days.

result.intervention: Prospective post-prescription review of IV antibiotics by a clinical pharmacy specialist with feedback to physicians over nine months.

cycle2.dates: Nine-month intervention phase (last two months compared)
cycle2.result: Significant reduction in discrepancies in antibiotic choice (47%, p values truncated); length of stay fell to 11.6 days.

result.other_findings: 167 recommendations made for 75.3% of patients, mainly stopping antibiotics (35%) and IV-to-oral switch (22%); acceptance 80.2%; no effect on mortality.

result.setting: Brazilian public hospitals (planned at least 10)
result.standard: Guideline-recommended care measures for acute coronary syndrome, atrial fibrillation and heart failure (Get With The Guidelines adapted)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Study design and rationale paper; no results reported yet.

result.setting: Paediatric emergency department and inpatient unit, Hassenfeld Children's Hospital at NYU Langone
result.standard: Evidence-based clinical practice guideline for well-appearing febrile infants 7-60 days (appropriate risk stratification)

cycle1.result: Low-risk infants admitted inappropriately 14.8%; mean length of stay for admitted high-risk infants 49.4 hours.

result.intervention: Physician education, process audit and feedback, and an electronic order set.

cycle2.result: Inappropriate low-risk admissions 10.8%; mean length of stay for high-risk infants 38.2 hours, sustained for 18 months.

result.other_findings: Adherence to appropriate risk stratification was strong in both periods.

result.setting: General intensive care unit, Riyadh Armed Forces Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean APACHE II score 13 (SD 7) in survivors and 24 (SD 9) in non-survivors; mortality ratio 1.2.

result.other_findings: 75% of deaths were in patients with chronic ill health or late-transferred 'old' trauma; authors suggest changing admission policy.

result.setting: Two tertiary care teaching hospitals (one government, one private), Islamabad
result.standard: Standard guidelines for pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis (choice, timing, route, dose)

cycle1.result: Prophylaxis given in 596/660 (90.3%); correct antibiotic choice 25/596 (4.2%); correct timing 304/596 (51%); route and dose appropriate in 100%.

result.other_findings: Timing compliance was 32.3% in the government hospital vs 69.9% in the private hospital (P = 0.001); ceftriaxone was most used despite no longer being recommended.

result.topic: Childcare physical activity environment audit reliability
result.setting: 20 early childhood education and care centres, Perth
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Intra- and inter-rater ICCs good to excellent for outdoor items (0.70-0.94) and fair to excellent for indoor items (0.46-0.78).

result.other_findings: Environmental audit tool reliability study, not a clinical audit.

result.setting: Intensive care units, National Taiwan University Hospital (university medical centre)
result.standard: Completeness and correctness of essential intrahospital transport tasks

cycle1.result: Adverse event incidence 1.08%; essential transport task completeness and correctness 80.8%.

result.intervention: Standardised transport process, better equipment maintenance, teamwork training, then reminder-assisted briefing with mnemonic cards (VITAL, STOP).

cycle2.result: Adverse event incidence 0.23% (p=0.01); essential task completeness and correctness 96.5%.

result.other_findings: Interventions were based on healthcare failure mode and effects analysis.

result.setting: Department of Anaesthesiology, Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital (tertiary referral centre)
result.standard: Practice guidelines and policy on fibreoptic bronchoscope use

cycle1.result: Annual repair rate 1%, repair cost 18,757 USD, FOB unavailability at induction 1.4%.

result.intervention: Quality improvement campaign based on the baseline audit, then regular internal audits of compliance with FOB policy.

cycle2.result: Repair rate fell by 81% to 0.19% in 2013 (p value truncated).

result.other_findings: Repair cost and unavailability also fell.

result.topic: Giant cell myocarditis versus cardiac sarcoidosis diagnosis
result.setting: Nationwide case series, Helsinki University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 45 of 73 GCM cases (62%) reclassified as cardiac sarcoidosis, mostly from granulomas originally missed (29) or misinterpreted (11).

result.other_findings: Reclassified patients had less heart failure at presentation (20% vs 46%) and better 1-year transplant-free survival (82% vs 45%).

result.setting: Regional Cancer Centre, PGIMER Chandigarh (tertiary)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 16/35 (45.71%) had HDR-ICBT under general anaesthesia and 19/35 (54.28%) under procedural sedation; rectal doses differed significantly between groups.

result.other_findings: Better rectal sparing under general anaesthesia. Comparative dosimetric study rather than audit against a standard.

result.setting: Community hospitals and nonhospital facilities (referrals to six tertiary centres)
result.standard: Colonoscopy quality indicators: caecal intubation rate, withdrawal time (6 minutes), bowel preparation adequacy, polyp number

cycle1.result: Caecal intubation 93.1%; median withdrawal time 8.3 minutes, with 31.3% withdrawn within 6 minutes.

result.other_findings: Community hospitals had longer withdrawal times than nonhospital facilities (median 9.9 vs 7.5 minutes).

result.setting: ICU clinicians across India (electronic questionnaire)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 33% of respondents unaware of SUP guidelines; about 32% had no SUP protocol; 69% felt all ICU patients must receive SUP.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire survey (197 of 550 responded), not an audit of practice against records.

result.setting: Nursing homes of the Canton of Geneva
result.standard: Pressure ulcer preventive practices (repositioning, anti-decubitus mattress) and prevalence

cycle1.result: Acquired pressure ulcer prevalence 4.5% in homes participating all 3 years.

result.intervention: Oral and written feedback to nursing home reference nurses 2 months after each survey.

cycle2.result: Acquired pressure ulcer prevalence 2.9% (p 0.035); repositioning and anti-decubitus bed or mattress use improved significantly.

result.other_findings: 27 homes took part in 2015 and 2016 (4607 patients across both years) and 15 in 2017; a 2016 survey was also done.

result.setting: 87 public and private hospitals (district, provincial, regional, specialty)
result.standard: Quality of care standards for PPH prevention, detection and management

cycle1.result: Uterotonics for PPH prevention in 73.3% (district), 71.2% (provincial/regional/specialty) and 72.7% (private); blood loss monitoring 48.4%, 36.9% and 43.3%; manual removal for retained placenta 97.8%.

result.other_findings: Placenta completeness checked in about half of women; oxytocin available in about 90% of public hospitals but misoprostol in only 52.5-56.8%.

result.topic: Asthma discharge management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Singapore General Hospital
result.standard: GINA guideline recommendations for ED discharge (oral and inhaled corticosteroid prescription and outpatient follow-up); target adherence 80%

cycle1.result: Baseline median adherence: OCS prescription 58%, ICS initiation 27%, follow-up issued 69%.

result.intervention: After-hours asthma nurse counselling and clinical decision support service (A-CARE) in the ED three nights a week, run through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: In patients reviewed by A-CARE, median adherence: OCS prescription 86%, ICS initiation 67%, follow-up issued 92%.

result.other_findings: Referral rate to A-CARE was only 16% in an audit of all ED asthma patients; follow-up attendance was higher with counselling (41.7% vs 15.9%, p=0.0388).

result.setting: Cardiac rehabilitation programmes in India (ICCPR global audit survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 18 of 23 programmes (78.3%) responded; one CR spot for every 360 IHD patients per year, with 3,304,474 more spaces needed each year.

result.other_findings: Most programmes accepted guideline-indicated patients and delivered care broadly in line with guidelines; top barriers were lack of referral and finance.

result.topic: Knowledge translation implementation in rectal cancer surgery
result.setting: 14 health regions of Ontario (provincial cancer system)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Thirty interviews; KT Signature scores averaged 78 (range 73-83) in 2 regions and 30.5 (range 22-38) in 12 regions.

result.other_findings: Pilot of a method to score implementation of knowledge translation interventions across regions.

result.topic: Profile of elderly patients with cervical cancer
result.setting: Tertiary cancer centre, Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 78 (88.63%) presented at advanced stage (II-IV) and 10 (11.36%) at early stage; median age 74 years.

result.other_findings: Discharge (51.13%), vaginal bleeding (28.40%) and abdominal pain (20.45%) were the commonest symptoms; 69% had comorbidities.

result.topic: Massage therapy for childhood functional gastrointestinal disorders
result.setting: Paediatric surgeon's rooms and remedial massage therapist rooms, Albury
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Complete resolution of symptoms in 88/96 (92%) children completing psoas massage therapy.

result.other_findings: Of 72 children followed up, 75% remained symptom free, 18% had marked and 7% mild improvement.

result.topic: Haemostasis sample non-conformity and phlebotomy practice
result.setting: Hospital wards, General Hospital Pula (secondary healthcare centre)
result.standard: Current phlebotomy guidelines; education deemed effective if more than half of wards significantly reduced sample non-conformity rate

cycle1.result: Clotted samples made up 84% of non-conformities; questionnaire showed poor nurse knowledge of phlebotomy.

result.intervention: One-hour lectures on blood sampling to nurses in small groups each working day over one month.

cycle2.result: Non-conformities fell in 7 of 9 wards, significantly in 5 wards.

result.other_findings: Nurse knowledge did not differ by education level or work experience.

result.setting: Tertiary care academic cancer centre, Moffitt Cancer Center, Tampa
result.standard: VTE prophylaxis guidelines and protocols for multiple myeloma

cycle1.result: Baseline VTE event rate 10%.

result.intervention: Education programme: 2 grand rounds, 3 web-based case discussions and a patient education module, with continuous QI involving 20 providers.

cycle2.result: VTE events fell to 4% (not statistically significant).

result.other_findings: Higher rates of guideline-based prophylaxis were seen in low-risk patients, and lower VTE incidence in patients with a prior VTE.

result.setting: Multisite oncology practices in Ontario and Quebec
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Over 6000 patients completed e-PROs; site completion rates 51%-95%.

result.intervention: Multi-faceted implementation (audit and feedback, champions, coaching, clinician training, educational outreach).

cycle2.result: Compared with the pre-population: reduced anxiety (p = 0.008), higher activation (p = 0.045), hospitalisation 12.3% vs 10.1% (p = 0.034).

result.other_findings: e-PROs were acceptable to 76% of patients and 80% of clinicians; ED visits 14.8% vs 12.8% (p = 0.081).

result.topic: Head and neck free-flap care pathway
result.setting: Foothills Medical Centre, Alberta Health Services, Calgary
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Quality management programme with care pathway and measurement, audit and feedback system sustained over 9 years.
result.other_findings: Methods paper describing design, costs and resources of a sustained quality management programme.

result.setting: Major medical centre (Alfred Health), Melbourne
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews with 35 clinicians; access to fungal diagnostics including bronchoscopy was the key barrier.

result.other_findings: Ad hoc surveillance, audit and feedback frustrated quality improvement; outpatients were a neglected area.

result.setting: The Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi (university hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 75 of 1718 children managed for trauma had peripheral arterial injury; 68 (90.66%) had vascular procedures and limb salvage was 92.65%.

result.other_findings: Late presentation (>6 h) was a risk factor for limb loss (p=0.014).

result.setting: Women operated for breast cancer in Lombardy, Emilia-Romagna and Lazio regions (administrative health data)
result.standard: Italian Health Ministry quality indicators for breast cancer care (surgery timeliness, medical therapy timeliness, complementary radiotherapy, mammographic follow-up)

cycle1.result: Adherence: medical therapy timeliness 53%, mammographic follow-up 73%, surgery timeliness 74%, complementary radiotherapy 82%.

result.other_findings: Adherence was associated with mortality risk reductions of 26% (medical therapy timeliness), 62% (radiotherapy) and 56% (mammographic follow-up); surgery timeliness showed no effect.

result.setting: 131 UK hospitals (National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 415 of 2341 (17.7 per cent) had SBO due to hernia; 312 (75.2 per cent) had surgery; in-hospital mortality 9.4 per cent (39 of 415).

result.other_findings: Mortality was highest with groin hernia (11.1 per cent); increasing age was associated with death (HR 1.05) and complications (OR 1.05).

result.setting: Endoscopy service, MercyAscot, Auckland
result.standard: Colonoscopy quality performance indicators (polyp and adenoma detection rate, withdrawal time)

cycle1.result: Polyp detection 40.7% in 2004; adenoma detection 25.8% and SSP detection 4.5% in 2012.

result.intervention: Continuous audit of colonoscopy performance with histology data added from 2012.

cycle2.result: Polyp detection 62.2%, adenoma detection 28.3% and SSP detection 14.7% in 2019.

result.other_findings: Removal of polyps >1 cm stayed constant (11%); most SSP improvement occurred in the first 2 years of the histology audit.

result.topic: Child and adolescent health policy evaluation
result.setting: National child and adolescent health policy, Slovenia
result.standard: Standards of public health policy (health, safety and environmental approaches)

cycle1.result: No clear evidence that the policy contributed to positive changes in child and adolescent health, owing to poor intersectoral coordination.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend auditing as an essential component of measuring public health policy success.

result.setting: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario A. Gemelli IRCCS, Rome (single centre)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean duration of antibiotic therapy 18.1 days (SD 11.4) with day 3 review only.

result.intervention: Added active re-evaluation of clinical status and antibiotic regimen at day 10 as well as day 3.
result.other_findings: Length of stay was also reduced; no difference in 30-day mortality.

result.topic: Audit and feedback on antimicrobial resistance prevention
result.setting: High-risk AMR departments at a regional hospital (Hospital Group Twente)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews with 16 healthcare workers on needs for audit and feedback.

result.other_findings: Staff wanted simple, actionable, recurrent feedback covering diagnostics, treatment and infection control.

result.setting: Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai (tertiary cancer centre)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Opioids were the mainstay; epidural inserted in only 9%; pain on movement moderate-severe in more than 50% within the first 24 h.

result.other_findings: Regional techniques gave better satisfaction; choice was not related to time of surgery, ASA grade or p-POSSUM.

result.setting: Outpatient IBD services, multicentre national survey
result.standard: International standards of IBD care (including MDT staffing and minimum IBD nurse FTE per 250 000 population)

cycle1.result: No service met international MDT FTE standards; 62.5% held regular MDT meetings; nurses were more likely than doctors to document weight, smoking status and arrange colonoscopic surveillance (492 doctor-led and 196 nurse-led visits).

result.other_findings: IBD nurses had a 6.8-hour shortfall between task hours and rostered hours; all services responded to patients within 48 hours.

result.setting: Nursing home physicians receiving an audit and feedback report, Ontario
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 33 of 89 (37%) physicians completed the questionnaire; goal priority was the only significant predictor of intention to adjust prescribing.

result.other_findings: Physicians prioritised antipsychotic prescribing, influenced by media and government mandate.

result.topic: Cervical screening in women living with HIV
result.setting: Antiretroviral clinics of district and regional hospitals, Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal
result.standard: South African cervical cancer screening guidelines for women living with HIV

cycle1.result: Questionnaire of 85 healthcare workers showed suboptimal knowledge; most did not know screening intervals for WLWH.

result.other_findings: Responses were significantly associated with healthcare worker occupation.

result.setting: 17 high case-load departments across Austria (Austrian Lung Cancer Audit)
result.standard: International lung cancer guidelines

cycle1.result: Median time presentation to diagnosis 8 days; diagnosis to treatment 15 days (chemotherapy), 21 days (radiotherapy), 24 days (surgery); unjustified surgery in 3 of 147 (2.0%).

result.other_findings: One-year survival 49.8%, ranging 37.8-66.7 between departments; 75.8% diagnosed on histology.

result.setting: Urban private hospital, Sitaram Bhartia Institute of Science and Research, Delhi
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: CS rate 79% in 2001.

result.intervention: Full-time salaried consultants, regular CS audit, joining an improvement collaborative in 2011, practice guidelines, monitoring by consultant, labour ward support, antenatal preparation and group practice.

cycle2.result: CS for foetal heart rate abnormalities fell from 23 to 5%.

result.other_findings: Guidelines ensured admission in active labour; overall final CS rate not given in the abstract text supplied.

result.topic: Perinatal death audit including bereaved women
result.setting: 11 maternity hospitals in Seine-Saint-Denis
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 75 women (one-third) agreed to interview; 41% of interviews gave new information for the expert panel.

result.other_findings: 35% of interviewed women were referred to a professional; acceptance ranged from 6% to 60% by maternity unit.

result.topic: Heart failure case finding and care in general practice
result.setting: Eight general practices (51 GPs) in Flanders (OSCAR-HF pilot)
result.standard: Heart failure quality indicators (echocardiography, natriuretic peptides, RAAS blockers and beta-blockers at target dose)

cycle1.result: Extended EHR audit increased identified HF patients by 74% (310 to 538); echocardiography in 86%, natriuretic peptides in 19%; in HFrEF RAAS blockers 84% and beta-blockers 86%, but target doses reached in 34% and 14%.

result.other_findings: A specialist diagnosis was recorded in only 42%, and diagnosing HFpEF was particularly difficult.

result.setting: Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto
result.standard: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) guidelines (17 major recommendations)

cycle1.result: Of 17 GINA recommendations, adherence was good for 5 (29.4%), moderate for 7 (41.2%) and poor for 5 (29.4%); moderate adherence in 61 (96.8%) and poor in 2 (3.2%) patients.

result.other_findings: Most were discharged on a short course of oral corticosteroid only (58.8%).

result.setting: NICU and neonatal intermediate care unit, Pramukhswami Medical College, Karamsad (tertiary care)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: FFP 37.82%, red cell concentrate 31.34%, platelets 28.14% and whole blood 2.70% of transfusions; 277 (81.5%) transfused in the first week.

result.other_findings: Neonatal sepsis was the commonest indication; authors state whole blood use should stop.

result.setting: Al-Manhal Family Practice Center (PHCC), Abha, Aseer region
result.standard: CBAHI standards for diabetes care (structure, process and outcome)

cycle1.result: Processes satisfactory except laboratory investigations and eye examination (partially met); good glycaemic control 28%, BP control 71%, lipid control 54%, appointment compliance 85%.

result.other_findings: Health education programme and laboratory facilities only partially met standards; retinopathy documented in 14%.

result.setting: Community, hospital and aged care settings across Australia (quality improvement collaborative)
result.standard: Dementia guideline recommendations on non-pharmacological care (self-reported adherence by checklist)

cycle1.result: Baseline audit of current practice with feedback (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Quality improvement collaborative: start-up meeting, online learning course, expert-reviewed QI plans, audit feedback and peer sharing.

cycle2.result: 42.1% immediate increase in self-reported adherence (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.08-1.87; p = 0.012).

result.other_findings: 45 health professionals joined and 28 completed all requirements.

result.setting: Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh (tertiary care)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Sedation effective in 95.8% without repeat scan; adverse events in 12 (5%).

result.other_findings: Propofol, ketamine and midazolam were used; 60% received two drugs.

result.setting: Tertiary care hospital (RG Kar Medical College and Hospital), Kolkata
result.standard: Ideal surgical hand washing technique; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: Baseline compliance 33.59%.

result.intervention: Video demonstration, personal demonstration by a consultant and individual instruction over repeated attempts.
result.other_findings: Personal instruction was the most effective intervention; hand washing technique needed the most attempts (6) to correct.

result.setting: All 90 full-time primary oral health care facilities in Gauteng Province
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean patients per month rose from 587 (2017) to 654 (2019); patient-to-clinician ratio 376 to 428; 15 extractions for every restoration.

result.other_findings: Mean operator-to-dental assistant ratio 1.3:1; clinicians saw on average 19 patients per day.

result.setting: NICU, Leiden University Medical Center
result.standard: Local neonatal stabilisation guideline

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Weekly plenary audits reviewing video and physiological recordings of neonatal stabilisation from 2014.
result.other_findings: Perspective article; areas for improvement were guideline compliance, documentation, device use, delivery room studies and clinical decision making.

result.setting: NICU, NYU Winthrop Hospital, Mineola
result.standard: Target incidence of perioperative hypothermia less than 25%

cycle1.result: Incidence of perioperative hypothermia 44.4%.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary team, staff education and a 9-task checklist, with quarterly PDSA cycles and monthly audit of checklist compliance.
result.other_findings: Hypothermia occurred mostly in the operating room and was associated with emergency procedures; higher checklist compliance correlated with less hypothermia.

result.topic: Nursing and midwifery care quality standards
result.setting: Eight wards of Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa (training hospital)
result.standard: Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health nursing and midwifery quality standards (Quality Audit tool)

cycle1.result: 83% of nursing assessments not completed within eight hours of arrival; 58% of charts lacked data compilation based on Gordon's functional model; only two wards met Standard 1.

result.other_findings: 75% of wards lacked materials and supplies; half of nursing stations had adequate patient visibility.

result.setting: Emergency departments and inpatient units of 2 community hospitals
result.standard: Evidence-based asthma pathway measures (e.g. systemic corticosteroids within 60 mins, tobacco smoke screening)

cycle1.result: Pre-pathway: timely steroids 32% (Site 1) and 62% (Site 2); tobacco screening 82% and 54%; CXR use 44% (Site 1); antibiotics 23% (Site 2); ED LOS 230 mins (Site 1).

result.intervention: Asthma pathway implementation with local champions, educational meetings, audit and feedback and EHR integration.

cycle2.result: Post-pathway: timely steroids 57% and 75%; tobacco screening 100% and 89%; CXR 29%; antibiotics 3%; ED LOS 197 mins.

result.other_findings: 881 ED visits and 138 hospitalisations analysed; no significant change in other outcomes.

result.setting: 4 private hospitals in eThekwini district
result.standard: National Core Standards and Batho Pele principles

cycle1.result: NCS and Batho Pele principles were not fully implemented or evaluated in the selected hospitals.

result.other_findings: Mixed-methods study to develop an audit tool, involving 24 nurse managers and 270 nurses.

result.setting: Feeder primary care clinics of Madwaleni Hospital, rural Eastern Cape
result.standard: UNAIDS target of 90% viral suppression

cycle1.result: Viral suppression 55.3%; prescription accuracy, scheduled viral loads and response to high viral loads were also poor.

result.intervention: Clinical mentorship through dedicated doctor outreach to clinics.

cycle2.result: Viral suppression 67.4%; most other process measures also improved.

result.other_findings: Still below the 90% UNAIDS target.

result.topic: Gastrectomy versus oesophagectomy for junctional tumours
result.setting: Dutch Upper GI Cancer Audit (national)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 3-year overall survival 35.8% after oesophagectomy (790) and 28.4% after gastrectomy (81) (HR 1.2, P = 0.557).

result.other_findings: Morbidity, mortality, radicality and lymph node yield did not differ.

result.topic: Anatomical side marker use on radiographs
result.setting: Paediatric medical imaging department, Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide
result.standard: Anatomical side marker on every radiographic image (best practice)

cycle1.result: ASMs present on 99 per cent of radiographs; digital 78.8 per cent, radiopaque 20.2 per cent; 4 images had no marker.

result.other_findings: Interviews with 11 radiographers identified time, infection precautions and patient factors as barriers.

result.topic: Breast screening programme planning and audit system
result.setting: 15 breast cancer screening programmes in Lombardy region
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Planning software application and audit cycle based on the PRECEDE-PROCEED model, tested in a 3-day workshop with programme coordinators.

cycle2.result: Plans produced with the application were more standardised and had clearer monitoring indicators than the previous year's.

result.other_findings: Development paper; the regional authority negotiated targets with local programmes during the audit cycle.

result.setting: Two academic (university) hospitals, Johannesburg
result.standard: International paediatric CT diagnostic reference levels (CTDIvol and DLP)

cycle1.result: Most local DRLs compared favourably with international standards, except CT chest and CT abdomen in the 0-1 year age group.

result.other_findings: DLP was higher after hours at both hospitals, most in the 0-1 year group (150.56% increase); CT brain made up 72.23% of examinations.

result.setting: Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital, Johannesburg
result.standard: ACR BI-RADS audit definitions compared with RSNA benchmark values

cycle1.result: Screening (n = 808): cancer detection rate 13.6 per 1000, recall rate 5.94; diagnostic (n = 741): CDR 175.4 and abnormal interpretation rate 39 per 100, significantly above RSNA benchmarks.

result.other_findings: Fewer minimal and node-negative cancers were found, reflecting advanced disease at presentation.

result.setting: Hepatobiliary surgeons' databases across the Anglophone Caribbean (AHPBA Caribbean Chapter)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: All 12 completed laparoscopically with no conversions or mortality; mean operating time 130.5 minutes.

result.other_findings: Two minor bile leaks resolved without intervention.

result.setting: Cancer research centre (ICMR-NICPR, Noida) and paediatric tertiary care hospital (Chacha Nehru Bal Chikitsalaya, Delhi)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Sensitivity 100%, specificity 92.6% and accuracy 97.7% for malignant paediatric tumours (histology available in 112).

result.other_findings: 100% concordance in liver and kidney tumours.

result.setting: Hiwot Fana Specialized University Hospital, Harar
result.standard: Eight standard criteria for PPH management adapted to the local setting

cycle1.result: All eight criteria met in 3 of 45 women (6.7%); low criteria: IV line set-up 71.1%, vital sign monitoring 51.1%, typing and cross-matching 48.9%, fluid chart 13.3%.

result.other_findings: Deficiencies in documentation, monitoring, blood availability and delays were found; local recommendations and an intervention plan were drawn up.

result.setting: All hospital deliveries in Suriname (national study)
result.standard: National PPH guideline (criteria-based audit)

cycle1.result: In severe PPH: prophylactic oxytocin 61.3% (95/155), oxytocin treatment 68.8% (106/154), tranexamic acid 4.9% (5/103).

result.topic: CT KUB scan extent protocol compliance

cycle1.result: Overall compliance in 8 cases (5.3%); 142 (94.7%) non-compliant, commonly over-scanning at the kidneys by 4-5 cm and at the pubic symphysis by 1-2 cm.

result.other_findings: Phantom simulation estimated dose increases of up to 35% to 45%; a follow-up audit is suggested.

result.setting: Patan Hospital, Lalitpur
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Notified/suspected cases highest in those over 60 years (32.54%); males had 1.67 times more smear-positive TB.

result.other_findings: Among AFB-positive cases, smear 3+ was commonest (38.54%).

result.topic: Chronic disease audit and feedback tool design
result.setting: General practices in metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Codesign with 17 practice staff and 5 patients produced the Future Health Today prototype.

result.other_findings: Staff wanted a simple tool within existing workflow, supporting recall and linked to guidelines.

result.setting: Three emergency departments in Ontario (Hamilton)
result.standard: Evidence-based PE diagnosis protocol; feasibility criteria including data capture on at least 80% of CTPAs

cycle1.result: 5094 patients tested for PE before the intervention (adherence figures not reported).

result.intervention: Clinical leadership endorsement, new PE testing pathway, physician education, personalised confidential audit and feedback, and patient outcome collection (November 2019).

cycle2.result: Implemented in 2 of 3 sites; data captured on 90% of CTPAs; feedback finalised before month end; extraction time 14 h per week or less.

result.other_findings: Feasibility study; protocol implementation failed in the third ED.

result.setting: Statewide hospital administrative data, Nevada
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: NAS incidence fell from 8.6 to 7.7 per 1000 hospital births; overall incidence 8 per 1000.

result.other_findings: Incidence was higher in white newborns (12) and Medicaid enrollees (13.2); nearly 75% of cases were in Clark County.

result.topic: Enhanced recovery care pathway adherence in colorectal surgery
result.setting: 10 hospitals in 4 European countries (5 analysed as cases)
result.standard: Colorectal cancer surgery care pathway protocol adherence

cycle1.result: Mean protocol adherence 56% before implementation.

result.intervention: Implementation of a care pathway for colorectal cancer surgery.

cycle2.result: Mean protocol adherence 62%; mean LOS fell by 2.1 days.

result.other_findings: Improvement varied widely; integration into daily practice, team motivation, management support and physician involvement explained differences.

result.topic: Developmentally supportive positioning of preterm infants
result.setting: Tertiary care neonatal unit, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Rishikesh
result.standard: Optimum positioning defined as Infant Position Assessment Tool (IPAT) score of 8 or more; aim to improve positioning by 50%

cycle1.result: 16.6% of infants had optimum position at baseline; mean IPAT 3.4 (1.4).

result.intervention: PDSA cycles of educational sessions, positioning audits, low-cost nesting aids and training of mothers.

cycle2.result: Mean IPAT score improved to 9.2 (2.8); optimum positioning maintained in 83.3% during sustenance phase.

result.other_findings: 74 neonates observed at 714 opportunities.

result.setting: Veterinary clinics in Spain and Portugal
result.standard: Modified human anaesthetic machine check system; vaporiser error 20% or less

cycle1.result: 42.7% of machines non-conforming, 26.4% conforming and 30.9% repaired in situ; 27.1% of isoflurane and 35.9% of sevoflurane vaporisers incorrect.

result.other_findings: Veterinary audit; scavenger system and canister were the most important items for non-conformity. Also covered Portugal.

result.setting: Trauma floors, Kings County Hospital Center, Brooklyn
result.standard: Mechanical VTE prophylaxis (SCD) as standard of care; aim to increase SCD compliance by 30% in 4 weeks

cycle1.result: Baseline SCD compliance 45% (morning 45%, afternoon 48.5%).

result.intervention: Patient education flyer and short educational sessions on VTE risk and SCD use over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 60% (morning 45%, afternoon 53%); aim not achieved.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest patient education should be combined with measures addressing other barriers.

result.setting: Obstetric department (Institute of Child Health and Hospital for Children / hospital), Chennai
result.standard: RCOG blood transfusion in obstetrics guidance (Green-top Guideline no. 47)

cycle1.result: 214 transfusion episodes in 51 patients; FFP was the most misused component, then whole blood; whole blood 34.5%, single unit transfusion 23.3%.

result.intervention: Targeted education on blood transfusion practice.

cycle2.result: 181 episodes in 43 patients; whole blood fell to 14.4%, single unit transfusion 18.2%, cryoprecipitate use 6.6%; inappropriate PRBC and FFP use fell significantly.

result.other_findings: Sample size given as patients; episodes were 214 and 181.

result.setting: South East Coast Ambulance Service
result.standard: Evidence-based prehospital thermal burn management (cooling, pain assessment, analgesia, reassessment, dressings)

cycle1.result: Adequate cooling 35%; pain assessed 87%; analgesia given 75%; pain reassessed after analgesia 54%; near 100% avoided hydrogel dressings and topical medicines.

result.other_findings: Most patients were children aged 0-10 injured at home; only nine were major burns.

result.setting: IAEA dosimetry audit networks database (worldwide)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 79 organisations in 58 countries offer radiotherapy dosimetry audit services.

result.other_findings: Access of radiotherapy centres to audit remains insufficient.

result.standard: Independent audit measurements of predefined IMRT and VMAT plans

cycle1.result: Audit agreed with local QA in 92% (ionisation chamber), 88% (array) and 76% (film) of measurements.

result.other_findings: Both failed in 2% (chamber), 4% (array) and 0% (film); agreement depended on equipment and analysis metric.

result.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, University Children's Hospital Zurich; retrospective single-institution cohort
result.standard: Manufacturer's size recommendation chart for second-generation Microcuff paediatric endotracheal tubes

cycle1.result: Of 13,219 oral intubations, 12,049 (84.9%) followed the manufacturer's size recommendation and 1170 used divergent tubes. Oral reintubation rate 0.13% (95% CI 0.08-0.22%) with recommended size vs 22.74% (95% CI 20.42-25.23%) with non-recommended tube.

result.other_findings: Authors urge adherence to the manufacturer's tube size chart given the low exchange rates when it is followed.

result.setting: Department of Radiation Oncology, Sir H.N. Reliance Foundation Hospital, Mumbai; tertiary care hospital
result.standard: Peer Review Audit Tool (PRAT), Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Radiologists

cycle1.result: Clinical note check 99% adherence to standards; minor changes in contour delineation 2.7% and treatment planning 1.7%; treatment set-up minor variations 0.3% and major changes 0.2%.

result.other_findings: Weekly multidisciplinary audit of all patients starting radiotherapy; prescription accuracy and patient-specific QA showed high compliance.

result.setting: Assiut University Children Hospital; residents
result.standard: WHO criteria for reporting causes of death

cycle1.result: Reporting the mechanism of death as cause (error) in 90% of death notification forms.

result.intervention: One-day training workshops for 100 residents using WHO criteria and local case scenarios, plus weekly audit of 10-15 forms for six months with reporting to the quality assurance director.

cycle2.result: Reporting of mechanism of death fell to 18%; significant decline in writing cause of death in Arabic only.

result.other_findings: Knowledge score rose from 11.9 ± 2.8 to 15.7 ± 3.2 among 89 physicians completing pre-post assessment.

result.setting: General Surgery Department, Ribat University Hospital, Khartoum; inpatient records
result.standard: 26-point structured documentation checklist

cycle1.result: Poor documentation of patient full name (17.6%), admission policy (21%), admission time (2%), treatment plan approval (2%) and discharge summary (4.4%); better for admission date (86.3%), medical history (81.5%) and diagnosis (87%).

result.other_findings: Single-cycle audit of long-stay records; authors recommend initiatives to improve documentation.

result.topic: Long-term stroke care in primary care
result.setting: Long-Term Stroke Clinic, HCTM UKM Primary Care Clinic, Kuala Lumpur
result.standard: 11 service criteria adapted from the Canadian Post-Stroke Checklist; clinical targets from Malaysian CPG on Cardiovascular Disease 2017 and CPG on Ischaemic Stroke 2020

cycle1.result: 9 of 11 service criteria met the standard; not met were asking about fatigue (43.4%) and access to community resources (26.5%). BP and HbA1c target attainment met the standards.

result.other_findings: Significant reductions in DBP (4.15 mmHg) and LDL-C (0.30 mmol/L) and in the proportion of smokers (p<0.05).

result.topic: Digital primary care psychiatry training courses

result.standard: not reported
